section: CORE-018 - Basic Subscription [A, S] (pp. 56-57)
title: Basic Subscription
purpose: Verify provisioning, acquisition, and execution of subscription resources. The basic subscription test verifies: the IEEE 2030.5 server supports a set of resources which can be subscribed to; the client devices can receive and act on notifications from those resources. This test shall include basic test scenarios where a set of resources are made available for subscribing by an IEEE 2030.5 server, and periodic notifications are made on a subset of those resources to a client device.
applicability_reason: PROFILE SCOPE 2026-07-28 (owner decision, SUPERSEDING the DER Aggregator Client scoping taken earlier the same day; docs/PROFILE_SCOPE_2026-07-28_der-client-gfems.md, and lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1-§1.2 rev. b): the DUT is certified against the CTP §4 DER CLIENT column in the Generating Facility EMS (GFEMS) posture — the DERs behind ONE point of interconnection, presented to the utility as a single 2030.5 client with one EndDevice and one LFDI and each admitted DER a DER instance beneath it (lexa-gw product decision D3.1), which is the shape docs/UTILITY_DECISION_PACK.md §1 already commits to as Scenario 1 / Direct. CSIP Conformance Test Procedures V1.3 §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves this row BLANK in the DER Client column and marks it X only in the DER Aggregator Client column (profile_conformance: der_client_required=false, der_aggregator_client_required=true). The two client columns nest strictly — no row is required of a DER Client that is not also required of a DER Aggregator Client — so this is one of exactly twenty-two rows the narrower claim drops: it is NOT REQUIRED of this DUT and is no part of the certification claim. INFORMATIVE, NOT UNIMPLEMENTED: the check stays registered in suitecsip and keeps running, which is this tool's standing treatment of an implemented-but-inapplicable row. Its criteria are real evaluators rather than the not-applicable stub, so its verdicts — including negative ones — are evidence about a capability this product does not claim, and no verdict of this row gates conformance. dut_role stays csip-client because the row still exercises the 2030.5 CLIENT surface; `certify -applicable` is the flag that drops it from a run. BENCH: this row turns on the 2030.5 Subscription/Notification function set — the DUT must accept a server-originated Notification POST at its notificationURI. `sim/server -subscription` serves that function set, also off by default. One bench limit is disclosed rather than papered over: gridsim is pure Go and Go's crypto/tls has no ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-CCM-8, so its built-in notifier REFUSES an https:// notificationURI rather than dialling a non-conformant one (sim/gridsim/subscribe.go), and conformant delivery needs an externally installed Notifier. The three outcomes stay apart: the DUT answered wrongly is a FAIL; nobody was subscribed, or the server could not DELIVER, is a SKIP naming which. OWNER INTENT, recorded as context and not as a claim: Subscription/Notification — the CORE-018/CORE-019 function set — is the capability the owner intends to implement first, as an OPTIONAL capability UNDER the DER Client profile, not as a move toward the aggregator column (lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1, §3.2; product decision D4 selects polling and defers subscription delivery until a target utility programme requires it). As of lexa-gw build d73d036 the surface does not exist — repository-wide searches for Subscription, Notification, SubscriptionList and NotificationList return no type, no handler and no route — so this row is expected to read NEGATIVE today. When the capability ships it becomes an informative row that can pass rather than one that must fail, and the profile claim is unaffected either way. ERRATA seq 44 applies and TIGHTENS this row: 'The 204 response is not included in the WADL — Remove the acceptance of 204 response in Procedure and Pass/Fail Criteria'. A DUT answering a Notification 204 is NOT conformant here. Note the narrow scope: erratum seq 23 ADDS a 204 expectation to CORE-014's PUTs, which critDERPut asserts.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: n/a — no lexa-gw surface implements this test; each DERControlResponse POST body with its status code (1 received / 2 started / 3 completed / 7 superseded) and the 201 Created reply; source observables to assert verbatim: HTTP GET EndDeviceList -> 200 OK; DUT's EndDevice contains a SubscriptionListLink with all=0 / HTTP GET SubscriptionListLink -> 200 OK SubscriptionList payload
preconditions: [S] The EndDevice resource with the SFDI/LFDI value of the Client device shall have a SubscriptionListLink element included with the appropriate attributes so the Server and Client can use the SubscriptionListLink to support subscription and notification requests. This link shall be empty at this stage of this test. For example, all=0.
[S] The FSAList belonging to the EndDevice instance with the Client SFDI/LFDI shall be able to be subscribed to with a value of one, unconditional, subscription.
[S] The server shall be able to update an attribute included in the Client FSAList to trigger a notification message to the Client.
Test header applicability marker is [A, S] (Aggregator, Server) - not marked [C].
steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.

2. [C] Search the retrieved list of EndDevice instances from the Server for the Client SFDI/LFDI value. Next, find the SubscriptionListLink elements and its attribute to confirm the Server supports subscription.
3. [C] Search the FSAList assigned to the Client EndDevice and verify it can be subscribed to.
4. [C] Prepare a subscription request (with all required elements/attributes) that includes the FSAList and send an HTTP POST request.

5. [S] For the received subscription request from the Client, process and send an HTTP 201 Created response (after validating such request can be made by the Client) with the correct HTTP Location header which indicates the URI of the created resource for the subscription request stored on the Server.

6. [S] Cause a change for one the elements of the FSA resource for the Client, which shall cause a notification message. At such resource change, send a notification message using the URI information sent by the Client from the previous test step and include the updated FSA resource payload.
7. [C] When the Notification message is received from the Server, process the incoming Notification message and payload, including validation.

8. [C] Perform an HTTP GET request on the href of the resource included in the Server Notification message. Process the payload returned from the Server from the HTTP GET request and compare to the Notification body payload, where they shall be identical.
expected: [C, S] The Client successfully searched the retrieved list of EndDevice instances from the Server and found the correct instance, which includes the Client SFDI/LFDI value. Successfully requested the SubscriptionListLink included in the EndDevice instance payload and received a conformant response for the SubscriptionList payload from the Server. Successfully processed the SubscriptionList payload to confirm the Server supported the Subscription mechanism for its EndDevice instance. The Server successfully responded to the Client request with the correct payload that belongs to the incoming href.
[C, S] The Client successfully found the FSAList assigned to the Client EndDevice and verified the FSAList could be subscribed to.
[C, S] The Client successfully prepared and requested a subscription request to the Server using the correct href for the NotificationURI for each.
[S] Successfully received and processed the subscription request and responded with a new Location header and HTTP 201 Created.
[S] Caused a change for one (or more) of the FSA included resource and sent a notification message with the updated resource payload as the Notification body.

[C, S] The Client successfully received (respond with HTTP 201 Created) the Notification message from the Server and processed the change in its internal state reflecting the updated resource information. Client may need to take further action based on the updated resource information sent. For example, a new DERProgram and/or DERControl was included.

[C, S] The Client successfully sent the HTTP GET request on the resource included in the step 7 notification body from the Server. Successfully received the response from the Server and compared the response payload resource to the resource included in the previous step notification body and concluded they were identical.
observables: HTTP GET EndDeviceList -> 200 OK; DUT's EndDevice contains a SubscriptionListLink with all=0
HTTP GET SubscriptionListLink -> 200 OK SubscriptionList payload
HTTP GET on the FunctionSetAssignmentsList (FSAList) -> 200 OK with subscribable=1 (unconditional subscription)
HTTP POST of a Subscription XML (containing subscribedResource = FSAList href and notificationURI) to the SubscriptionList href
HTTP 201 Created response carrying a Location header with the new subscription resource URI
Server -> Client HTTP POST of a Notification to the Client's notificationURI, body = updated FunctionSetAssignments/FSAList payload
Client responds to the Notification POST with HTTP 201 Created
Client HTTP GET on the notified resource href -> 200 OK; payload byte-for-byte equivalent to the Notification body payload
notes: Applicability header is [A, S] - i.e. subscription/notification is required of Aggregators and Servers, NOT of a plain Client DUT; a client-only DUT such as lexa-gw may legitimately be out of scope for this test, but the procedure body still uses [C] steps for the subscribing side, so it defines what our harness's simulated server must do if we choose to exercise subscriptions. Note the odd requirement that the CLIENT answer an inbound Notification with HTTP 201 Created (2030.5 notification handling); this means the DUT must run an HTTP listener at its notificationURI. 'subscribed to with a value of one' refers to the subscribable attribute value 1 = unconditional subscription. Step 6 wording 'Cause a change for one the elements' is verbatim (missing 'of').

[S] For the received subscription request from the Client, process and send an HTTP 201 Created response, after validating such a request can be made by the Client, with the correct HTTP location header, which indicates the URI of the created resource for the subscription request stored on the Server.

8. [S] Cause a change for one the elements of the FSA resource for the Client, which shall cause a notification message. At such resource change, send a notification message using the URI information sent by the Client from the previous test step and include the updated FSA resource payload.

9. [C] When the Notification message is received from the Server, process the incoming Notification message and payload, including validation and respond back to the Notification message with HTTP 201 Created message.

10. [C] Perform an HTTP GET request on the href of the resource included in the Server notification message. Process the payload returned from the Server in response to the HTTP GET request and verify that it is identical to the notification body payload. Repeat the HTTP GET and validation steps for each notification received.

11. [S] Cancel the outstanding FSA subscription by sending a notification message to Client indicating notification status = 1 (Subscription canceled, no additional information) and required elements/attributes for the Notification payload.

12. [C] Receive the Notification message that indicates cancellation sent by the Server, process the message, and update the internal subscription state so future subscription requests are not done, or the Client continues to expect future Notifications on the canceled resource.
expected: [C, S] The Client successfully searched the retrieved list of EndDevice instances from the Server and found the correct instance, which includes the Client SFDI/LFDI value. Successfully requested the SubscriptionListLink included in the EndDevice instance payload and received a conformant response for the SubscriptionList payload from the Server. Successfully processed the SubscriptionList payload to confirm the Server supported the Subscription mechanism for its EndDevice instance. The Server successfully responded to the Client request with the correct payload that belongs to the incoming href.
[C, S] The Client successfully found the FSAList assigned to the Client EndDevice and verified the FSAList could be subscribed to.
[C] The Client successfully prepared and requested a subscription request to the Server using the correct href for the NotificationURI for each.
[S] Server successfully received and processed the subscription request and responded with a new Location header and HTTP 201 Created.
[S] Server caused a change for one (or more) of the FSA included resource and sent a notification message with the updated resource payload as the Notification body.

[C] The Client successfully received (respond with HTTP 201 Created) the Notification message from the Server and processed the change in its internal state reflecting the updated resource information.
[C] The Client successfully received the Notification cancellation message from the Server and provided an HTTP response.

HTTP GET SubscriptionListLink -> 200 OK SubscriptionList
HTTP POST #1: Subscription XML for the EndDevice instance -> 201 Created + Location header
HTTP GET FSAList/FunctionSetAssignments -> 200 OK with subscribable=1
HTTP POST #2: Subscription XML for the FSA resource -> 201 Created + Location header
Server -> Client HTTP POST Notification carrying the updated FSA payload to the Client's notificationURI
Client responds to each Notification POST with HTTP 201 Created
Client HTTP GET on the notified resource href -> 200 OK, payload identical to the Notification body (repeated per notification)
Server -> Client Notification with status = 1 (Subscription canceled, no additional information) to cancel the FSA subscription
Client HTTP response to the cancellation Notification
Absence of further subscription requests on the canceled resource after step 12 (or continued expectation of notifications - the doc allows either)
notes: Applicability header is [A, S] like CORE-018; a plain Client DUT may be out of scope, but the procedure defines the simulated-server behavior a harness needs. Two subscriptions are created here (EndDevice-level and FSA-level) vs one in CORE-018. Notification status = 1 means 'Subscription canceled, no additional information'. Step 12's outcome is ambiguous/permissive: it accepts either 'future subscription requests are not done' OR 'the Client continues to expect future Notifications on the canceled resource' - the pass criterion only requires that the Client provided an HTTP response, so cancellation-state handling is effectively unasserted. The purpose text promises 'multiple conflicting resources' notification scenarios but the numbered procedure never actually issues conflicting notifications. Step 8 wording 'Cause a change for one the elements' is verbatim.

errata.description: The test states that if a subordinate resource has a change, there should be a notification for that resource but also for the 'parent' resource (if that resource is subscribed to). However, based on the information in the 2030.5 spec, a second notification (for edev) is not required. Moreover, the pass/fail criteria for the test in CSIP doesn't look for the second notification.
corrective_action: Remove steps 10 and 11

section: 6 Core Function Tests (implied) - CORE-021 - Randomized Events [C, A, S]
title: Randomized Events [C, A, S]
purpose: Verify provisioning, acquisition, and execution of randomized events. The randomized events test verifies the Client ability to handle DER events randomized to minimize the impact on overall grid stability. This test shall include DER events with plus/minus randomization in the event start and duration times.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §3.1-§3.5: cmd/northbound is a full CSIP DER client — mTLS with the CSIP §5.2.1.1 suite 0xC0AE, a /dcap-rooted discovery walk (EndDevice, Registration PIN, Time, DER*, FSA, DERProgram, DefaultDERControl, DERControl, ActiveDERControl, DERCurve), DER PUT reporting, Response/LogEvent/FlowReservation POSTs and MirrorUsagePoint telemetry — and the §4 profile matrix marks this test der_client=required.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 11113` (gridsim leg): TLS1.2 ClientHello offering exactly TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8 (0xC0AE) -> server Certificate -> client Certificate -> Finished; plus gridsim's plaintext HTTP transcript (RPT-051/052 Test Log JSON: method, uri, vers, headers, sep+xml body) correlated by timestamp; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; source observables to assert verbatim: HTTP GET of the FSA-assigned DERProgramList href -> 200 with XML DERProgramList containing 3 DERProgram instances with distinct primacy values / HTTP GET on DERCurveListLink href -> 200 XML DERCurveList
preconditions: [S] Construct 1 DERProgramList, which includes three DERPrograms and three DERControl, and required subordinate resources.

[S] DERProgram1/DERControl1 has at minimum of one immediate control mode. It shall start three minutes from now with duration of two minutes and have highest Primacy value (lowest priority). This DERControl1 shall have 0 values for randomizeStart and randomizeDuration values.

[S] DERProgram#2/DERControl#2 includes one curve-based control relevant for the target Client. It shall start six minutes from now with duration of one minute and have next highest Primacy value (second highest priority). This DERControl#2 shall have plus 30 seconds for randomizeStart and randomizeDuration values.

[S] DERProgram#3/DERControl#3 includes curve-based controls, which are relevant. It shall start nine minutes from now with duration of three minutes and have lowest Primacy value (highest priority). This DERControl#3 shall have minus 30 seconds for randomizeStart and randomizeDuration values.
[S] At least one DERProgram shall have DefaultDERControl attribute and other requirements listed above.
[S] Immediate- and curve-based controls shall conform to the above requirements.
[S] All three DERControl instances shall be used across DERProgram and/or DefaultDERControl instances.
steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.

2. [C] Process the received DERProgramList assigned to the Client through the FSA instance and find the highest priority DERProgram/DERControl to process by following the list ordering rules. The DER-Client shall schedule the selected DERProgram/DERControl with the correct randomizeStart and randomizeDuration values applied (should be DERProgram 3, above).

3. [C] Client shall issue subsequent HTTP GET requests to retrieve the subordinate resources associated with all of the DERProgram and DERControl instances, such as DERCurveListLink with one or more DERCurveList instances.

4. [C] For the DERCurve resources in the DERCurveList, the Client shall do HTTP GET requests to retrieve the 3 or 4 curve points (depending on the curve type) and their values. The Client shall use these curve point and related values to construct the DER curve-based control, which shall be communicated to the internal inverter system and the schedule information. For example, start time + duration + randomizationStart + randomizeDuration.
5. [C] Until the selected DERProgram/DERControl becomes active, the Client shall use the DefaultDERControl value by setting the DER control mode using the DefaultDERControl attribute.

6. [C] Periodically poll the associated DERControl resource to check the Status of the DER event. Client completes the DER event based on either the DERControl Status value and/or start time + duration + randomizationStart + randomizeDuration period.
7. [C] Repeat steps #4 and 5 for rest of the DERProgram/DERControl instances that have are scheduled.
expected: [C, S] The Client successfully received a conformant, or any, DERProgramList payload from the Server. Client was able to find which multiple DERPrograms take priority by using the list ordering rules. Client was able to schedule a DER event based on the DERProgram/DERControl information, including randomization values applied, which was received.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved the subordinate resources for the DERProgram/DERControl payload. For example, DERCurveList information. The Server sent all requested resource information as a response to the Client HTTP GET requests.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved all curve points and their values from the Server. The Server sent all curve points and their values as requested by the Client. The Client successfully constructed the curve points and their values to send the information to the DER inverter system.
[C] The Client successfully found and scheduled the DefaultDERControl while no DER event was active.
[C] The Client successfully retrieved the DERControl status to find the completion of the DER event and successfully completed the DER Event, including the application of the randomization values.
observables: HTTP GET of the FSA-assigned DERProgramList href -> 200 with XML DERProgramList containing 3 DERProgram instances with distinct primacy values
HTTP GET on DERCurveListLink href -> 200 XML DERCurveList
HTTP GET on each DERCurve href -> 200 XML with 3 or 4 DERCurve points (curve-type dependent)
Repeated HTTP GET (polling) of each DERControl href to observe currentStatus transitions
XML elements randomizeStart and randomizeDuration present in DERControl with values 0, +30 (seconds), -30 (seconds) respectively for DERControl1/#2/#3
Timing of DER control activation on the wire offset from interval/start by the randomization value
HTTP GET on DefaultDERControl href while no scheduled event is active
notes: Test is labelled [C, A, S] (Client, Aggregator, Server). The doc uses both 'randomizeStart'/'randomizeDuration' and 'randomizationStart' inconsistently (steps 4 and 6 say 'randomizationStart'); treat them as the same 2030.5 DERControl elements randomizeStart/randomizeDuration. Step 7 says 'repeat steps #4 and 5' but the intent appears to cover steps 4-6 for the remaining DERPrograms. Setup says DERControl1 has 'highest Primacy value (lowest priority)' and DERControl#3 'lowest Primacy value (highest priority)' — the numerically lowest primacy wins. Section heading for this test is not printed on the page (test starts mid-section).

errata.description: No way to determine what a “not applicable” default control is.
corrective_action: Change Setup 3rd bulleted, first sentence as follows, “DERProgram#3/DERControl#3 includes curve-based controls.”
errata.observable_impact: Server setup only.

errata.description: Incorrect number of points for test case. Procedure, Step 4 "retrieve the 10 curve points and their values." We are not using 10 points.
corrective_action: Change procedure step 4, first sentence as follows, “[C] For the DERCurve resources in the DERCurveList, the Client shall do HTTP GET requests to retrieve the 3 or 4 curve points (depending on curve type) and their values.”
errata.observable_impact: HTTP GET on each DERCurve href in the DERCurveList; the returned DERCurve carries 3 or 4 CurveData points depending on curveType (not 10).

requirement_trace.description: When a client receives an Event and calculates an Effective Start Time (Start Time + Start Randomization) in the past and a Specified End Time in the future ((Effective Start Time < Current Time) AND (Specified End Time > Current Time)), the client SHALL begin the Event using the current time and the absolute value of Start Randomization.
For response reporting purposes, the start time shall be reported as the Current Time plus applied Start Randomization applied.
For Event duration purposes, the Specified End Time SHALL be preserved, and any duration randomization attributes SHALL be applied to the abbreviated duration.
Randomization SHALL NOT artificially create a gap between Successive Events.
randomizeDuration: Number of seconds boundary inside which a random value must be selected to be applied to the associated interval duration, to avoid sudden synchronized demand changes.
randomizeStart: Number of seconds boundary inside which a random value must be selected to be applied to the associated interval start time, to avoid sudden synchronized demand changes.
Any device handling these Events and not operating on them SHALL NOT modify or apply them.
The device SHALL randomly select a number in seconds from zero to the randomizeStart specified for this event.
Depending on the sign of the value (positive or negative), randomization SHALL be applied before or after the scheduled Start Time of the Event.
If the value is negative, randomization SHALL be applied before the specified Start Time of the Event.
If the value is positive, randomization SHALL be applied after the specified Start Time of the event, causing the device to delay commencement of the Event.
Devices SHALL randomly select a number in seconds from zero to the randomizeDuration value specified for the Event.
Depending on the sign of the value (positive or negative), randomization SHALL be applied to increase or decrease the duration of the event.
If the value is negative, randomization SHALL decrease the EffectiveDuration of the Event.
If the value is positive, randomization SHALL be added to the duration of the event, causing the device to delay termination of the Event.
Clients that use fixed pseudo random values SHALL scale the applied randomization based on the range indicated by the given randomizeStart or randomizeDuration.
Stated differently, fixed pseudo random values SHALL indicate a percentage of the randomizeStart or randomizeDuration to be applied.
Manufacturers SHALL assure that fixed pseudo randomization values are random over a population of like devices.
Manufacturers SHALL assure that random number generators maintain a distribution of values over a population of like devices (e.g., by using differing seeds).[SR{EC65].
Clients that act upon Events SHALL support randomization.
Clients SHALL apply randomization attributes when present in an Event's attributes.
Cancellation of an active Event SHALL cause clients to apply the greater of (absolute value of randomizeStart attribute) and (absolute value of randomizeDuration) to the abbreviated Event.
If an Event is in progress and user override occurs, the client SHALL respond to the user override without randomization.

section: 6 Core Function Tests (implied) - CORE-022 - Responses [C, A, S]
title: Responses [C, A, S]
purpose: Verify generation and handling of event responses. The responses test verifies the Client ability to handle responses to programs scheduled by the Server. This test shall include DERPrograms that specify responses by the Client for various DER event states.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §3.1-§3.5: cmd/northbound is a full CSIP DER client — mTLS with the CSIP §5.2.1.1 suite 0xC0AE, a /dcap-rooted discovery walk (EndDevice, Registration PIN, Time, DER*, FSA, DERProgram, DefaultDERControl, DERControl, ActiveDERControl, DERCurve), DER PUT reporting, Response/LogEvent/FlowReservation POSTs and MirrorUsagePoint telemetry — and the §4 profile matrix marks this test der_client=required.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 11113` (gridsim leg): TLS1.2 ClientHello offering exactly TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8 (0xC0AE) -> server Certificate -> client Certificate -> Finished; plus gridsim's plaintext HTTP transcript (RPT-051/052 Test Log JSON: method, uri, vers, headers, sep+xml body) correlated by timestamp; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; each DERControlResponse POST body with its status code (1 received / 2 started / 3 completed / 7 superseded) and the 201 Created reply; source observables to assert verbatim: DERControl XML containing replyTo href and responseRequired=7 / HTTP POST of DERControlResponse to the replyTo URI with status=1 (Received)
preconditions: [S] Construct 1 DERProgramList, which includes 3 DERPrograms and 3 DERControl (and required subordinate resources).

[S] DERProgram1/DERControl1 has at minimum of one immediate control mode relevant for the target Client. It shall start three minutes from now with duration of two minutes and have highest Primacy value (lowest priority).

[S] DERProgram#2/DERControl#2 includes one curve-based control relevant for the target Client. It shall start six minutes from now with duration of one minute and have next highest Primacy value (second highest priority).
[S] DERProgram#3/DERControl#3 curve-based controls. It shall start nine minutes from now with duration of three minutes and have lowest Primacy value (highest priority).
[S] At least one DERProgram shall have DefaultDERControl attribute and other requirements listed above.
[S] Immediate- and curve-based controls shall conform to the above requirements.

[S] Each DERControl shall include a replyTo and responseRequired elements as follows: the replyTo element of the DERControl resource shall map to the available URI location where the Server accepts POST of responses from the Client devices; the responseRequired element of the DERControl resource shall be specified with the value of 7. See the IEEE 2030.5 standard response status code table, which requires Client devices to send responses at each state of the DERControl event.
steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.

2. [C] Process the received DERProgramList assigned to the Client through the FSA instance and find the highest priority DERProgram/DERControl to process by following the list ordering rules. The DER-Client shall schedule the selected DERProgram/DERControl (should be DERProgram 3, above).

3. [C] After the correct DERProgram/DERControl is selected, Client shall issue subsequent HTTP GET requests to retrieve the subordinate resources associated with the DERProgram and DERControl, such as DERCurveListLink with one or more DERCurveList instances.

4. [C] For the DERCurve resources in the DERCurveListLink, the Client shall do HTTP GET requests to retrieve the 10 curve points and their values. The Client shall use these curve point and related values to construct the DER curve-based control, which shall be communicated to the internal inverter system and the schedule information. For example, start time and duration.
5. [C] Until the selected DERProgram#1/DERControl#1 becomes active, the Client shall use the DefaultDERControl value by setting the DER control mode using the DefaultDERControl attribute.

6. [S] Update the DERControl#1 currentStatus/dateTime values at each state of the DER event by following its event schedule. Before the event completes its schedule, cancel the event by updating its currentStatus value to 2 (canceled).

7. [C] Periodically poll the associated DERControl#1 resource to check the Status of the DER event and send the requested response at the responseRequired attribute, such as a Response message with status=1 (Received) and status=2 (Started). Client completes the DER event either based on the DERControl#1 Status value and/or start time plus duration interval. Because this event was canceled in step 5, the Client shall notice such cancellation and send a response with status=6 (cancellation).
8. [S] Update the DERControl#2 currentStatus/dateTime values at each state of the DER event by following its event schedule.

9. [C] Periodically poll the associated DERControl#2 resource to check the Status of the DER event and send the requested response at the responseRequired attribute. Client completes the DER event either based on the DERControl#2 Status value and/or start time plus duration interval.
10. [S] Update the DERControl#3 currentStatus/dateTime values at each state of the DER event by following its event schedule.

11. [C] Periodically poll the associated DERControl#3 resource to check the Status of the DER event and send the requested response at the responseRequired attribute. Client completes the DER event either based on the DERControl#3 Status value and/or start time plus duration interval.
expected: [C, S] The Client successfully received a conformant, or any, DERProgramList payload from the Server. Client was able to find which multiple DERPrograms take priority by using the list ordering rules. Client was able to schedule a DER event based on the DERProgram/DERControl information, including randomization values applied, which was received.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved the subordinate resources for the DERProgram/DERControl payload. For example, DERCurveList information. The Server sent all requested resource information as a response to the Client HTTP GET requests.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved all curve points and their values from the Server. The Server sent all curve points and their values as requested by the Client. The Client successfully constructed the curve points and their values to send the information to the DER inverter system.
[S] Server successfully updated the currentStatus/dateTime attributes at the event states, including when the event was canceled.
[C] The Client successfully found and scheduled the DefaultDERControl while no DER event was active.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved the DERControl#1 status to detect the event status from its creation to cancellation including sending the Response messages that correspond to: Status=1 (received), Status=2 (started), Status = 6 (cancellation) at the correct times.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved the DERControl#2 and DERControl#3 status to detect the event status from its creation to completion including sending the Response messages that correspond to: Status=1 (received), Status=2 (started), Status = 3 (completed) at the correct times.
observables: DERControl XML containing replyTo href and responseRequired=7
HTTP POST of DERControlResponse to the replyTo URI with status=1 (Received)
HTTP POST of DERControlResponse with status=2 (Started)
HTTP POST of DERControlResponse with status=6 (Event cancelled) for DERControl#1
HTTP POST of DERControlResponse with status=3 (Completed) for DERControl#2 and DERControl#3
Repeated HTTP GET (polling) of each DERControl href showing currentStatus/dateTime transitions, including currentStatus=2 (canceled) written by the Server
HTTP GET on DERCurveListLink and each of 10 DERCurve points -> 200 XML
notes: Step 7 refers to the cancellation being performed 'in step 5' but the Server cancellation is actually step 6 — off-by-one in the doc. Step 5 mentions DERProgram#1/DERControl#1 becoming active while step 2 says the highest-priority selection 'should be DERProgram 3'; the doc is internally inconsistent here (CORE-021 has the same 'should be DERProgram 3' text). Step 4 says 10 curve points here whereas CORE-021 step 4 says 3 or 4 curve points. Test labelled [C, A, S].

corrective_action: Change Setup 3rd bulleted item as follows, “DERProgram#3/DERControl#3 includes curve-based controls. It shall start nine minutes from now with duration of three minutes and have lowest Primacy value (highest priority).”

section: 6 Core Function Tests (implied) - CORE-023 - Superseding Events [C, A, S]
title: Superseding Events [C, A, S]
purpose: Verify creation of overlapping superseding events and client's ability to properly select the correct event to process using the 2030.5 event rules.
applicability_reason: CORE-023 does not appear in the §4 Profile Test Conformance table at all: Annex A Errata I seq 33 adds it, and the entry reads in full 'Adding a new test (Optional)'. It is therefore OPTIONAL for every profile, including the DER Aggregator Client profile the 2026-07-28 re-scope adopts, and conformance is not gated on it — profile_conformance is null for this row rather than all-false, because the printed matrix has no row for it to record. It stays applicable and implemented because cmd/northbound implements the superseding-event behaviour the row drives and coreSuperseding produces a real verdict against gridsim's two-primacy programs.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 11113` (gridsim leg): TLS1.2 ClientHello offering exactly TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8 (0xC0AE) -> server Certificate -> client Certificate -> Finished; plus gridsim's plaintext HTTP transcript (RPT-051/052 Test Log JSON: method, uri, vers, headers, sep+xml body) correlated by timestamp; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; each DERControlResponse POST body with its status code (1 received / 2 started / 3 completed / 7 superseded) and the 201 Created reply; source observables to assert verbatim: HTTP GET of FSAList showing two FSA instances (topology and non-topology) / HTTP GET of DERProgramList with 7 DERPrograms and 3 DERControl
preconditions: [S] Construct 1 FSAList that has two FSA instances (Topology group FSA and non-Topology group FSA). The Topology group FSA includes 1 DERProgramList, that has 7 DERPrograms and 3 DERControl (and required subordinate resources).

[S] DERProgram#1/DERControl#1 has opmodMaxLimW and opModVoltvar for the target Client. It shall start two minutes from now with duration of one minute and have highest Primacy value (lowest priority).

[S] DERProgram#2/DERControl#2 includes opmodMaxLimW for the target Client. It shall start identical time as DERcontrol#1 duration of one minute and have next highest Primacy value (second highest priority).

[S] DERProgram#3/DERControl#3 has opmodMaxLimW and opModVoltvar for the target Client. It shall start identical time as DERcontrol#1 duration of one minute and have next highest Primacy value (third highest priority).
[S] At least one DERProgram shall have DefaultDERControl attribute and other requirements listed above.
[S] Immediate- and curve-based controls shall conform to the above requirements.

[S] Each DERControl shall include a replyTo and responseRequired elements as follows: the replyTo element of the DERControl resource shall map to the available URI location where the Server accepts POST of responses from the Client devices; the responseRequired element of the DERControl resource shall be specified with the value of 7. See the IEEE 2030.5 standard response status code table, which requires Client devices to send responses at each state of the DERControl event.
steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.

2. [C] Process the received DERProgramList assigned to the Client through the FSA instance and find the highest priority DERProgram/DERControl to process by following the list ordering rules. The DER-Client shall schedule the selected DERProgram/DERControl (should be DERProgram#1/DERControl#1 above).

3. [C] After the correct DERProgram/DERControl is selected, Client shall issue subsequent HTTP GET requests to retrieve the subordinate resources associated with the DERProgram and DERControl, such as DERCurveListLink with one or more DERCurveList instances.

4. [C] For each of the DERControl instances retrieved by the Client, the client shall send DERcontrolResponse messages with Status=1 (Received) followed by another set of DERControlResponse messages with Status=7 (superseded) or Status=14 (aborted due to alternate program event) for the two DERControl instances that are not started.

5. [C] For the DERCurve resources in the DERCurveListLink, the Client shall do HTTP GET requests to retrieve the 10 curve points and their values. The Client shall use these curve point and related values to construct the DER curve-based control, which shall be communicated to the internal inverter system and the schedule information. For example, start time and duration.
6. [C] Until the selected DERProgram#1/DERControl#1 becomes active, the Client shall use the DefaultDERControl value by setting the DER control mode using the DefaultDERControl attribute.
7. [S] Update the DERControl#1, #2, and #3 currentStatus/dateTime values at each state of the DER event by following its event schedule.

8. [C] Check the DERControl#1 EventStatus before acting upon it. Upon Start time of the event, the Client shall send DERControlRespone message with Status=2 (Started) followed by Status=3 (Completed) upon effective end time of the event.
expected: [C, S] The Client successfully received a conformant, or any, DERProgramList payload from the Server. Client was able to find which multiple DERPrograms take priority by using the list ordering rules. Client was able to schedule a DER event based on the DERProgram/DERControl event rules.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved the subordinate resources for the DERProgram/DERControl payload. For example, DERCurveList information. The Server sent all requested resource information as a response to the Client HTTP GET requests.

[C, S] The Client successfully retrieved all curve points and their values from the Server. The Server sent all curve points and their values as requested by the Client. The Client successfully constructed the curve points and their values to send the information to the DER inverter system.
[S] Server successfully updated the currentStatus/dateTime attributes at the event states, including when the event was canceled.
[C] The Client successfully found and scheduled the DefaultDERControl while no DER event was active.

[C, S] The Client successfully detected the correct DERProgram#1/DERControl#1 to start including sending the Response messages that correspond to: Status=1 (received), Status=2 (started), Status = 3 (completed) at the correct times.

[C, S] The Client successfully detected the correct DERProgram#2/DERControl#2 and DERProgram#3/DERControl#3 to supersede/abort including sending the Response messages that correspond to: Status=1 (received), Status = 7 (superseded) or 14 (aborted due to alternate program event) at the correct times.
observables: HTTP GET of FSAList showing two FSA instances (topology and non-topology)
HTTP GET of DERProgramList with 7 DERPrograms and 3 DERControl
DERControl XML with identical interval start times across DERControl#1/#2/#3 and distinct primacy
HTTP POST DERControlResponse status=1 (Received) for all three DERControls
HTTP POST DERControlResponse status=7 (Superseded) or status=14 (Aborted due to alternate program event) for DERControl#2 and DERControl#3
HTTP POST DERControlResponse status=2 (Started) then status=3 (Completed) for DERControl#1
HTTP GET on DERCurveListLink and 10 DERCurve points
DERControl contains opModMaxLimW and opModVoltVar control modes
requirement_refs: IEEE 2030.5 standard response status code table
notes: Doc typos preserved in spirit: 'opmodMaxLimW' (2030.5 element is opModMaxLimW), 'opModVoltvar' (opModVoltVar), 'DERcontrol#1', 'the Clint', 'DERControlRespone'. Setup declares 7 DERPrograms but only defines 3; the remaining 4 are the other topology nodes. Pass/fail bullet about 'when the event was canceled' appears copy-pasted from CORE-022 — no cancellation is defined in CORE-023. Status 7 vs 14 is an either/or (implementation choice), not both. Test labelled [C, A, S].

section: 10 Error Handling Tests - ERR-001 - Error Scenario 1 [C, A]
title: Error Scenario 1 [C, A]
purpose: The error scenario 1 test verifies error handling for various IEEE 2030.5 server and client scenarios. This test shall include scenarios where certain HTTP response codes are used by a server. Specifically it verifies that the Client correctly follows an HTTP 301 Moved Permanently / 302 Redirect Location header to the new URI over the TLS port and then retrieves the DeviceCapability and a resource contained in it.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §3.1-§3.5: cmd/northbound is a full CSIP DER client — mTLS with the CSIP §5.2.1.1 suite 0xC0AE, a /dcap-rooted discovery walk (EndDevice, Registration PIN, Time, DER*, FSA, DERProgram, DefaultDERControl, DERControl, ActiveDERControl, DERCurve), DER PUT reporting, Response/LogEvent/FlowReservation POSTs and MirrorUsagePoint telemetry — and the §4 profile matrix marks this test der_client=required.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 11113` (gridsim leg): TLS1.2 ClientHello offering exactly TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8 (0xC0AE) -> server Certificate -> client Certificate -> Finished; plus gridsim's plaintext HTTP transcript (RPT-051/052 Test Log JSON: method, uri, vers, headers, sep+xml body) correlated by timestamp; source observables to assert verbatim: HTTP GET /dcap (DeviceCapability) from the client -> HTTP 301 Moved Permanently or HTTP 302 Redirect with a Location: header containing the new URI / Client re-issues HTTP GET to the Location URI over the TLS port (all traffic in this test is inside TLS, including the redirect exchange)
preconditions: 1. [TS] Verify a DeviceCapability resource exists on the Server and include at least one resource in the DeviceCapability resource. The DeviceCapability is available only through TLS port and if an unencrypted HTTP GET is received, the Server shall respond with an HTTP 301, Moved Permanently, or HTTP 302, Redirect, which include a location header to the new URI of the requested resource.
2. [TS] All testing is done over a TLS link for this test, including the request triggering the 301 or 302 response.
DER client shall have previously completed Communication Fundamentals Tests, Core Function Set Tests, and Basic Functions Tests (section 10 preamble).
steps: 1. [TS] Record the Client/Server communications.
2. [C] Do an HTTP GET on DeviceCapability resource from the Server using the supported HTTP and IP address.
3. [TS] Respond to the HTTP GET request by responding with either HTTP 301 Moved Permanently or HTTP 302 Redirect and Location header specifying the new URI of the resource being requested.
4. [C] Process the HTTP 301 or 302 messages, including the location header and prepare a new HTTP request and perform an HTTP GET request using the TLS port using the URI included in the response.
5. [TS] Respond to the HTTP GET request by responding with the resource body of the DeviceCapability resource and HTTP 200 OK response.
6. [C] Process the retrieved DeviceCapability resource and verify there is at least one resource in the DeviceCapability.
7. [C] Perform an HTTP GET operation on the found resource in step 2 and process the response payload from the Server.
expected: [C] The Client successfully requested the DeviceCapability resource from the Server using the HTTP configuration information provided.
[TS] Server responded with HTTP 301 or 302 and Location header for the new URI.
[C] Client received the HTTP 301 or 302 responses, processed the Location header which was provided in the HTTP response and successfully did an HTTP GET using the TLS port and URI.
[TS, C] Server successfully received the HTTP GET request on the TLS port and URI and responded with HTTP 200 OK with DeviceCapability payload.
[TS, C] Client found at least one resource included in the DeviceCapability. Server included at least one resource link in the returned DeviceCapability to the Client.
[TS, C] The Client successfully received the payload of the found resource from the DeviceCapability resource. The Server responded with 200 OK and returned a conformant payload for its resource.
observables: HTTP GET /dcap (DeviceCapability) from the client -> HTTP 301 Moved Permanently or HTTP 302 Redirect with a Location: header containing the new URI
Client re-issues HTTP GET to the Location URI over the TLS port (all traffic in this test is inside TLS, including the redirect exchange)
HTTP GET <new URI> -> 200 OK with a DeviceCapability XML payload containing at least one resource link (e.g. EndDeviceListLink, TimeLink, ...)
Follow-on HTTP GET on the linked resource -> 200 OK with a conformant payload for that resource
TLS session establishment on the 2030.5 TLS port before the redirected request
requirement_refs: CSIP guide section 5.8 Error Handling (section 10 preamble)
notes: Applicability marker [C, A] = Client and Aggregator - directly in scope for lexa-gw as a 2030.5 client. Role tags: [TS] = Test Server, [C] = Client. Ambiguity: the Setup describes the 301/302 as the response to an UNENCRYPTED HTTP GET, but Setup item 2 and the Pass/Fail criteria say all testing including the redirect-triggering request is done over TLS - the harness should drive the redirect over TLS and treat the plaintext wording as descriptive of the server's general policy. Step 7 says 'the found resource in step 2' but the resource is actually found in step 6 (DeviceCapability retrieved in step 5) - off-by-one in the step cross-reference. The doc does not name a concrete DeviceCapability path here; /dcap is the conventional 2030.5 path, not text quoted from this page. PDF pages: 178-179.

errata.description: Clarify all testing is done over TLS for this test. The test is expecting the client to make a TLS and non-TLS GET request on /dcap.
corrective_action: Add item 2 to Setup stating, “All testing is done over a TLS link for this test, including the request triggering the 301 or 302 response.”
errata.observable_impact: HTTP GET /dcap over TLS; server answers 301 or 302 redirect; client follows it over TLS.

section: 10 Error Handling Tests - ERR-002 - Error Scenario 2 [A, S]
title: Error Scenario 2 [A, S]
purpose: The error scenario 2 test verifies the error handling of various IEEE 2030.5 server and client scenarios. This test shall include client subscription to a resource and, subsequently, the subscription is canceled by a server, which should trigger the client to post another subscription request. This test shall also include the server sending an undesired subscription to a client, which shall return an HTTP 400 error and the server shall delete the subscription without notification.
applicability_reason: PROFILE SCOPE 2026-07-28 (owner decision, SUPERSEDING the DER Aggregator Client scoping taken earlier the same day; docs/PROFILE_SCOPE_2026-07-28_der-client-gfems.md, and lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1-§1.2 rev. b): the DUT is certified against the CTP §4 DER CLIENT column in the Generating Facility EMS (GFEMS) posture — the DERs behind ONE point of interconnection, presented to the utility as a single 2030.5 client with one EndDevice and one LFDI and each admitted DER a DER instance beneath it (lexa-gw product decision D3.1), which is the shape docs/UTILITY_DECISION_PACK.md §1 already commits to as Scenario 1 / Direct. CSIP Conformance Test Procedures V1.3 §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves this row BLANK in the DER Client column and marks it X only in the DER Aggregator Client column (profile_conformance: der_client_required=false, der_aggregator_client_required=true). The two client columns nest strictly — no row is required of a DER Client that is not also required of a DER Aggregator Client — so this is one of exactly twenty-two rows the narrower claim drops: it is NOT REQUIRED of this DUT and is no part of the certification claim. INFORMATIVE, NOT UNIMPLEMENTED: the check stays registered in suitecsip and keeps running, which is this tool's standing treatment of an implemented-but-inapplicable row. Its criteria are real evaluators rather than the not-applicable stub, so its verdicts — including negative ones — are evidence about a capability this product does not claim, and no verdict of this row gates conformance. dut_role stays csip-client because the row still exercises the 2030.5 CLIENT surface; `certify -applicable` is the flag that drops it from a run. BENCH: this row turns on the 2030.5 Subscription/Notification function set — the DUT must accept a server-originated Notification POST at its notificationURI. `sim/server -subscription` serves that function set, also off by default. One bench limit is disclosed rather than papered over: gridsim is pure Go and Go's crypto/tls has no ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-CCM-8, so its built-in notifier REFUSES an https:// notificationURI rather than dialling a non-conformant one (sim/gridsim/subscribe.go), and conformant delivery needs an externally installed Notifier. The three outcomes stay apart: the DUT answered wrongly is a FAIL; nobody was subscribed, or the server could not DELIVER, is a SKIP naming which. OWNER INTENT, recorded as context and not as a claim: Subscription/Notification — the CORE-018/CORE-019 function set — is the capability the owner intends to implement first, as an OPTIONAL capability UNDER the DER Client profile, not as a move toward the aggregator column (lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1, §3.2; product decision D4 selects polling and defers subscription delivery until a target utility programme requires it). As of lexa-gw build d73d036 the surface does not exist — repository-wide searches for Subscription, Notification, SubscriptionList and NotificationList return no type, no handler and no route — so this row is expected to read NEGATIVE today. When the capability ships it becomes an informative row that can pass rather than one that must fail, and the profile claim is unaffected either way. ERRATA seq 38 applies: 'Remove Step 6' — the client is NOT required to re-POST a Subscription after the server cancels it with status 1. A check that waited for that re-POST would hang and then fail a conformant client, so the check does not look for it. The client's INTERNAL state is not assertable either way: absence of traffic does not distinguish a client that dropped a subscription from one with nothing to say, and that criterion SKIPs saying so.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: n/a — no lexa-gw surface implements this test; the HTTP PUT request lines (DERCapability/DERSettings/DERStatus/DERAvailability hrefs) with 204/200 responses in the gridsim transcript; each DERControlResponse POST body with its status code (1 received / 2 started / 3 completed / 7 superseded) and the 201 Created reply; source observables to assert verbatim: Server power cycle followed by re-established TLS session; subscription state survives (no re-POST of /sub required by the client) / HTTP POST from Server to the client's notificationURI carrying a Notification whose body is the changed FunctionSetAssignmentsList, truncated per the 'limit' parameter of the original subscription; verdict row citing BASE.063, BASE.064, BASE.065, BASE.066, BASE.067, BASE.068
preconditions: Setup 1. Server shall be able to power reset itself and preserve the subscription requests
Setup 2. Server shall be able to cancel an outstanding subscription and send cancellation Notification to clients.
Setup 3. Server shall be able to send invalid Notification to clients.

Chapter 10 preamble: Before running these tests, the DER client shall have previously completed the tests described in Communication Fundamentals Tests, Core Function Set Tests, and Basic Functions Tests of this document.
The Client must already hold an outstanding subscription to a FunctionSetAssignmentsList (established in earlier tests) with a 'limit' parameter in the original subscription request.

steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.

2. [S] Power reset the system, so it restarts. All outstanding subscriptions shall be persistent across a power reset. After a successful power reset, cause a change on one of the resources in the subscribed FunctionSetAssignmentsList which shall trigger a notification message to be sent to the Client.

3. [C] When the Notification message is received from the Server, process the incoming Notification message and payload, including validation and respond to the Notification message with HTTP 201 Created or 204 No Content message.

4. [C] Perform an HTTP GET request on the href of the resource included in the Server Notification message. Process the payload returned from the Server from the HTTP GET request and compare to the Notification body payload. They shall be identical.

5. [TS] Cancel the Client subscription request by sending a notification to the URI provided in the original subscription with the following values: Notification/status = 1 (Subscription canceled, no additional information); Notification/subscriptionURI = URI of the subscription instance created by the server for the original request.
6. [C] Process the incoming Notification cancellation message from the Server by removing it from own list of outstanding Subscriptions.

7. [TS] Prepare and send an invalid Notification message to the outstanding Client FunctionSetAssignmentsList subscription by using the following values: Instead of the FunctionSetAssignmentsList items to be included in the body of the notification message, insert EndDevice instance information.
8. [C] Receiving an invalid Notification sent by the Server shall cause the client to respond with an HTTP 400 error.
9. [S] On receipt of the HTTP 400 error, the subscription for which the notification was sent in step 8 shall be deleted without notification.

For example, limit.

section: 11 Maintenance of the Model Tests
title: Inverter Maintenance (Out-Of-Band) [A, S]
purpose: The out-of-band (OOB) inverter maintenance test verifies inverter population change handling. The inverter population is managed by an aggregator using an OOB method. This test shall test scenarios that include inverter addition and deletion using EndDevice/EndDeviceList for a client device/aggregator.
applicability_reason: PROFILE SCOPE 2026-07-28 (owner decision, SUPERSEDING the DER Aggregator Client scoping taken earlier the same day; docs/PROFILE_SCOPE_2026-07-28_der-client-gfems.md, and lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1-§1.2 rev. b): the DUT is certified against the CTP §4 DER CLIENT column in the Generating Facility EMS (GFEMS) posture — the DERs behind ONE point of interconnection, presented to the utility as a single 2030.5 client with one EndDevice and one LFDI and each admitted DER a DER instance beneath it (lexa-gw product decision D3.1), which is the shape docs/UTILITY_DECISION_PACK.md §1 already commits to as Scenario 1 / Direct. CSIP Conformance Test Procedures V1.3 §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves this row BLANK in the DER Client column and marks it X only in the DER Aggregator Client column (profile_conformance: der_client_required=false, der_aggregator_client_required=true). The two client columns nest strictly — no row is required of a DER Client that is not also required of a DER Aggregator Client — so this is one of exactly twenty-two rows the narrower claim drops: it is NOT REQUIRED of this DUT and is no part of the certification claim. INFORMATIVE, NOT UNIMPLEMENTED: the check stays registered in suitecsip and keeps running, which is this tool's standing treatment of an implemented-but-inapplicable row. Its criteria are real evaluators rather than the not-applicable stub, so its verdicts — including negative ones — are evidence about a capability this product does not claim, and no verdict of this row gates conformance. dut_role stays csip-client because the row still exercises the 2030.5 CLIENT surface; `certify -applicable` is the flag that drops it from a run. BENCH: the fixture this row was written against is built and is OFF BY DEFAULT, so an informative lever cannot re-measure certified evidence — `sim/server -fleet` serves the CTP Figure-15 topology (an aggregator EndDevice plus EDA1/EDA2 under SPA1/SPA2 and EDB1/EDB2 under SPB1/SPB2) and the default tree is pinned byte-identical by sim/gridsim/golden_default_test.go. With -fleet on, the per-EndDevice criteria grade for real against the LFDIs gridsim derived for EDA1/EDA2/EDB1/EDB2, read from GET /admin/fleet rather than inferred from /edev ordering; with it off they SKIP naming the fixture, and a SKIP is a runtime fact about this bench, never a pass. BENCH: this row turns on the 2030.5 Subscription/Notification function set — the DUT must accept a server-originated Notification POST at its notificationURI. `sim/server -subscription` serves that function set, also off by default. One bench limit is disclosed rather than papered over: gridsim is pure Go and Go's crypto/tls has no ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-CCM-8, so its built-in notifier REFUSES an https:// notificationURI rather than dialling a non-conformant one (sim/gridsim/subscribe.go), and conformant delivery needs an externally installed Notifier. The three outcomes stay apart: the DUT answered wrongly is a FAIL; nobody was subscribed, or the server could not DELIVER, is a SKIP naming which. The notification halves of this row rest on that same function set, which lexa-gw does not implement and which the owner intends to add as an optional capability under this profile (see CORE-018). gridsim now has the lever this procedure describes: step 3's out-of-band agreement that a device is no longer managed is POST /admin/fleet with managed_by '-', step 4 is the server acting on it, and cleanup rebinds unconditionally so a detached device is not missing from every later case's EndDeviceList and reported there as a DUT finding. What is NOT assertable is the client's internal state, which SKIPs saying so; the EndDeviceList walk is asserted for real.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: n/a — no lexa-gw surface implements this test; source observables to assert verbatim: Client subscription POSTs for the EndDeviceList and for each EndDevice instance -> HTTP 201 Created with a Location header naming the created subscription instance / Server Notification POST to the client's notificationURI whose body is the EndDeviceList, list length honoring the 'limit' parameter from the original subscription
preconditions: Chapter 11 preamble: Before running these tests, the DER client and server EUTs shall have previously completed the tests described in the Communication Fundamentals Tests, Core Function Set Tests, and Basic Functions Tests sections of this document.

Chapter 11 preamble: the aggregator is assumed to be managing four EndDevices (EDA1, EDA2, EDB1, and EDB2) per the topology of Figure 16 (System SY:10 > Subtransmission ST:9 > Substation SS:8 > Feeders FDA:7 and FDB:7 > Segments SGA:6 and SGB:6 > Transformers TFA:5 and TFB:5 > Service Points SPA1:4, SPA2:4, SPB1:4, SPB2:4 > End Devices EDA1, EDA2, EDB1, EDB2; legend = [Name]:[Primacy]).

Chapter 11 preamble: IEEE 2030.5 permits many ways to create this topology using FunctionSetAssignments and associated DERProgram, but there must be a DERProgram associated with each group node used to send DER controls to all devices connected to that node.

Setup 1. Follow test setup section in the AGG-001 - Aggregator Operation Subscription test with additional setup as described in this section. Client in this test represents an aggregator, which manages number of individual DERs in its EndDeviceList. At the completion of the AGG-001 - Aggregator Operation Subscription test, the set of EndDevice instances included for the aggregator client are: SPA1: EDA1 and EDA1X; SPA2: EDA2; SPB1: EDB1; SPB2: EDB2.
Setup 2. Server shall configure the EndDeviceList and each of its EndDevice instances for the Client with an attribute that can be subscribed to.
Setup 3. Client shall be able to subscribe to its EndDeviceList and receive notifications for changes when they occur.
Setup 4. Server shall be able to send notifications to subscribed clients when the subscribed resource changes.
steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.
2. [C] Subscribe to the EndDeviceList so notifications can be received when there are changes to each instance and to the list.
3. The aggregator and Utility agreed out-of-band that EDA1X is no longer being managed by the aggregator and needs to be deleted from its list.
4. [S] Delete the EDA1X EndDevice instance from the aggregator EndDeviceList and send a notification to the EndDeviceList subscriptions.

5. [C] Receive the notification for the EndDeviceList and do additional HTTP GETs to receive the rest of the EndDeviceList contents not sent as part of the Notification message payload. Client shall also receive a notification on the deleted EndDevice instance. Based on the received EndDeviceList, it shall notice the EDA1X EndDevice instance is deleted and its internal state should also reflect the change so it no longer manages that device.
6. [TC] Do a GET on the EDA1X EndDevice href and it shall result in an HTTP 404 Not Found error.
expected: [C, S] The Client successfully subscribed to the EndDevice instances and EndDeviceList and received an HTTP 201 Created response.
The aggregator and Utility successfully agreed that EDA1X is no longer managed by the aggregator and its EndDevice instance will be deleted by the Server.

[C, S] Server successfully deleted the EDA1X EndDevice instance from the aggregator EndDeviceList and sent a notification to the EndDeviceList subscriptions. The notification resource body for the EndDeviceList was correctly formed using the limit parameter requested by the Client in the original subscription request.

[C, S] The Client successfully received the notification for the EndDeviceList and did additional HTTP GETs to receive the rest of the EndDeviceList contents not sent as part of the Notification message payload. Client also received a notification on the deleted EndDevice instance. Based on the received EndDeviceList, Client found the EDA1X EndDevice instance is deleted and its internal state was updated so it no longer manages that device.
[TC, S] The Client successfully did an HTTP GET on the EDA1X EndDevice href and received an HTTP 404 Not Found error.
observables: Client subscription POSTs for the EndDeviceList and for each EndDevice instance -> HTTP 201 Created with a Location header naming the created subscription instance
Server Notification POST to the client's notificationURI whose body is the EndDeviceList, list length honoring the 'limit' parameter from the original subscription
Separate Server Notification POST for the deleted EDA1X EndDevice instance
Client follow-up HTTP GET /edev (EndDeviceList) requests paging in the items the limited Notification body omitted
HTTP GET on the EDA1X EndDevice href -> HTTP 404 Not Found
No client-initiated HTTP DELETE on wire (this is the out-of-band variant - removal is agreed off-protocol and executed by the Server)
requirement_refs: G5 (Requirements Matrix Test column = 'BASIC, UTIL, AGG, MAINT')
P46 (Aggregator SHOULD subscribe to the EndDeviceList to receive notifications for any additions or changes to the list) - matrix Test column = 'AGG'
P47 (Aggregator SHOULD subscribe to each EndDevice instance under its control to receive notifications for any deletions of that instance) - matrix Test column = 'AGG'
notes: Title tag [A, S] = Aggregator + Server EUT; the 'Client' throughout chapter 11 is an aggregator client, not a single DER client, so a plain 2030.5 DER client (lexa-gw) is only indirectly in scope. Setup depends on AGG-001 - Aggregator Operation Subscription, which introduces an extra EndDevice EDA1X under SPA1 that is not shown in Figure 16. The requirement ids listed are cross-references from this document's Requirements Matrices (pp.193-200), which name the group 'MAINT'/'AGG' rather than MAINT-001 specifically; the test body cites no requirement ids. Step 6 is tagged [TC] (Test Client) while the corresponding pass/fail bullet is tagged [TC, S] - a doc inconsistency, the observable is the same 404.

section: 11 Maintenance of the Model Tests
title: Inverter Maintenance (In-Band) [A, S]
purpose: The in-band inverter maintenance test verifies inverter population change handling. The inverter population is managed by an aggregator using an in-band method. This test shall test scenarios that include inverter addition and deletion using EndDevice/EndDeviceList for a client device/aggregator.
applicability_reason: §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves MAINT-002 blank in ALL THREE columns — required of Server, DER Client and DER Aggregator Client alike, i.e. of nobody — so the 2026-07-28 re-scope to the aggregator-client profile does NOT make it required, unlike its four MAINT siblings. Annex A Errata I seq 32 is the reason: 'Test not required as it is unlikely for utilities to utilize the tested behavior. Make the test optional/remove entirely from the spec.' steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.
2. [C] Subscribe to the EndDeviceList so notifications can be received when there are changes to the list.
3. Aggregator found that EDA1X is no longer being managed by its list and needs to be deleted from its list.

section: 11 Maintenance of the Model Tests
title: Group Maintenance [A, S]
purpose: The group maintenance test verifies topology change handling. The topology is managed by the utility server using FunctionSetAssignments. This test shall test scenarios that include topology changes that cause changes in the associated FunctionSetAssignment groups.
applicability_reason: PROFILE SCOPE 2026-07-28 (owner decision, SUPERSEDING the DER Aggregator Client scoping taken earlier the same day; docs/PROFILE_SCOPE_2026-07-28_der-client-gfems.md, and lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1-§1.2 rev. b): the DUT is certified against the CTP §4 DER CLIENT column in the Generating Facility EMS (GFEMS) posture — the DERs behind ONE point of interconnection, presented to the utility as a single 2030.5 client with one EndDevice and one LFDI and each admitted DER a DER instance beneath it (lexa-gw product decision D3.1), which is the shape docs/UTILITY_DECISION_PACK.md §1 already commits to as Scenario 1 / Direct. CSIP Conformance Test Procedures V1.3 §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves this row BLANK in the DER Client column and marks it X only in the DER Aggregator Client column (profile_conformance: der_client_required=false, der_aggregator_client_required=true). INFORMATIVE, NOT UNIMPLEMENTED: the check stays registered in suitecsip and keeps running, which is this tool's standing treatment of an implemented-but-inapplicable row. Its criteria are real evaluators rather than the not-applicable stub, so its verdicts — including negative ones — are evidence about a capability this product does not claim, and no verdict of this row gates conformance. dut_role stays csip-client because the row still exercises the 2030.5 CLIENT surface; `certify -applicable` is the flag that drops it from a run. BENCH: the fixture this row was written against is built and is OFF BY DEFAULT, so an informative lever cannot re-measure certified evidence — `sim/server -fleet` serves the CTP Figure-15 topology (an aggregator EndDevice plus EDA1/EDA2 under SPA1/SPA2 and EDB1/EDB2 under SPB1/SPB2) and the default tree is pinned byte-identical by sim/gridsim/golden_default_test.go. With -fleet on, the per-EndDevice criteria grade for real against the LFDIs gridsim derived for EDA1/EDA2/EDB1/EDB2, read from GET /admin/fleet rather than inferred from /edev ordering; with it off they SKIP naming the fixture, and a SKIP is a runtime fact about this bench, never a pass. BENCH: this row turns on the 2030.5 Subscription/Notification function set — the DUT must accept a server-originated Notification POST at its notificationURI. `sim/server -subscription` serves that function set, also off by default. One bench limit is disclosed rather than papered over: gridsim is pure Go and Go's crypto/tls has no ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-CCM-8, so its built-in notifier REFUSES an https:// notificationURI rather than dialling a non-conformant one (sim/gridsim/subscribe.go), and conformant delivery needs an externally installed Notifier. [C, S] EDB1 and EDB2 end devices correctly processed the DERProgramList associated with its device and applied the TFB DefaultDERControl.
[C, S] Server successfully moved the EDB1 from the SPB1 node to the SPA1 node that caused the EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList/DERProgramList to change.
[C, S] Server successfully sent a notification to aggregator that EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList has changed.

[C, S] Aggregator successfully received the notification that EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList has changed and processes the message in order to determine that it needed to retrieve the updated DERProgramList information.

[C, S] Aggregator successfully performed GETs the new EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList and all DERPrograms, to which that EDB1 now belongs. Server responded successfully to each of the GETs from the Aggregator and sent correct payload as requested.
[C, S] If needed, the aggregator has canceled any subscriptions to the old FunctionSetAssignmentsList for EDB1.
[C, S] If needed, the aggregator has successfully subscribed to the new FunctionSetAssignmentsList of EDB1.

Client HTTP GET on the new EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList href, then GET on the referenced DERProgramList and each DERProgram
Client HTTP DELETE (or equivalent unsubscribe) on the old EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList subscription instance href
Client subscription POST for the new EDB1 FunctionSetAssignmentsList
Behavioral: EDA1/EDA2 running the TFA DefaultDERControl and EDB1/EDB2 running the TFB DefaultDERControl before the move; EDB1 following SPA1/TFA grouping after the move
requirement_refs: G5 (IEEE 2030.5 based grouping and full lifecycle management of group relationships, Section 5.2.3) - matrix Test column = 'BASIC, UTIL, AGG, MAINT'

P48 (For every inverter under its control, the Aggregator SHOULD subscribe to the list pointed to by EndDevice:FunctionSetAssignmentsListLink to receive notifications for any changes in the inverter's group assignments) - matrix Test column = 'AGG'
P51 (Aggregator SHOULD subscribe to all of the DERProgramLists associated with its FSA groups) - matrix Test column = 'AGG'

Setup 1. Follow test setup section in the AGG-001 - Aggregator Operation Subscription test with additional setup as described in this section. 2. [C] Subscribe to the DERProgramList and DERControlList for each EndDevice FunctionSetAssignments instance so notifications can be received when there are changes to each instance. Use the all value of the DERControlList as the limit parameter to the subscription request.

3. [S] Add a new DERControl that starts in plus-fifteen minutes with duration of five minutes (no randomization) with at least one valid immediate or curve-based control to the TFA DERProgram DERControlList. Send a notification message for the affected DERControlList.
4. [C] Receive and process the Notification for the aggregator affected DERs. Client shall do additional HTTP GET on subordinate resources for the DERControlList.

[C, S] Client applied the Event Processing rules to all DERControls for each EndDevice, including the newly created one from step 3 and scheduled the DERControl event(s). Sent a response for each DERControl if required by the Server.

Server Notification POST for the changed DERControlList after a new DERControl is added to the TFA DERProgram

The new DERControl on the wire: DERControl/interval/start = now + 15 minutes, DERControl/interval/duration = 5 minutes (300 s), randomizeStart/randomizeDuration absent or 0, containing at least one immediate control (DERControlBase) or a curve-based control (DERCurveLink)
Client follow-up HTTP GETs on the DERControlList href and on subordinate resources (each DERControl, referenced DERCurve)
Client HTTP POST of a DERControlResponse to the DERControl replyTo URI when responseRequired demands it
Client scheduling behavior consistent with IEEE 2030.5 Section 12.1.3 event rules across all DERControls for every managed EndDevice

notes: 'Use the all value of the DERControlList as the limit parameter' means the subscription limit must equal the full list size so notifications carry every item. 'Event Processing rules' is an unresolved cross-reference in the test body - it points at the event handling rules used elsewhere in this document and at IEEE 2030.5-2018 Section 12.1.3 (see requirement P30 in the CSIP Requirements Matrix, p.195). The response POST is conditional on the DERControl responseRequired bitfield (see BASE.032, p.198). Title tag [A, S]; the 'Client' is an aggregator client.

At the completion of the AGG-001 - Aggregator Operation Subscription test, the set of EndDevice instances included for the aggregator client are: SPA1: EDA1; SPA2: EDA2; SPB1: EDB1; SPB2: EDB2.
Setup 2. Server shall configure the DERProgramList and DERControlList for each EndDevice FunctionSetAssignments with an attribute that can be subscribed to.
Setup 3. Client shall be able to subscribe to its DERProgramList and DERControlList and receive notifications for changes when they occur.
Setup 4. Server shall be able to add or change a DERProgram with different primacy value and send Notification each time a change occurs.

Setup 5. Server shall create DERProgram (primacy=1) for TFA and TFB nodes and DERProgram (primacy=2) for SGA and SGB nodes respectively. TFA/TFB DERProgram shall have different DefaultDERControl values than SGA/SGB DERPrograms.
steps: 1. [T] Record the Client/Server communications.

2. [C] Subscribe to the DERProgramList for each EndDevice FunctionSetAssignments instance so notifications can be received when there are changes to each instance. If the notification payload does not contain all the available programs, then the client should get the additional items.
3. [S] Swap the primacy values of TFA/TFB DERPrograms with the values of SGA/SGB DERPrograms. Send Notification messages to the affected DERProgram and DERProgramList with active subscriptions.
4. [C] Receive the incoming Notifications and process the resource information to reflect changes in the DERProgram instances, including Primacy value changes.
5. [C] Based on the updated Primacy values, activate the DefaultDERControl that belongs to the highest priority DERProgram if there is no active DERControl event.

Subscription request used the all value of the DERProgramList as the limit parameter.

[C, S] Server found the two highest priority DERPrograms and swapped the values so the second highest priority DERProgram now becomes the highest. Sent Notification messages to the affected DERProgram and DERProgramList with active subscriptions.
[C] The Client successfully received the incoming Notifications and processed the resource information to reflect changes in the DERProgram instances, including Primacy value changes.
[C] Client, based on the updated Primacy values, activated the DefaultDERControl that belonged to the highest priority DERProgram if there is no active DERControl event.

Client follow-up HTTP GETs for DERProgramList items not carried in a truncated Notification payload
DERProgram/primacy element values observable in the notification body and in subsequent GET responses

Behavioral: the DER settings change to the DefaultDERControl of the newly highest-priority DERProgram (SGA/SGB values replace TFA/TFB values) while no DERControl event is active - verifiable by reading back the DER settings / DefaultDERControl the client is applying

G7 (Modifications to default settings SHALL occur immediately upon receipt and have indefinite duration)
