notes: MAINT-005 is the only chapter-11 test named by id in the IEEE 2030.5 Requirements Matrix - it is cited for DER.001 through DER.012 (pp.199-200), notably DER.005 'If there are no active Events, the DER client SHALL be managed by the DefaultDERControl instance exposed by the preferred DERProgram'. Primacy inconsistency: Setup 5 assigns primacy=1 to TFA/TFB and primacy=2 to SGA/SGB, whereas Figure 16 (p.182) labels TFA/TFB primacy 5 and SGA/SGB primacy 6 - a harness should follow Setup 5. In IEEE 2030.5 a lower primacy value means higher priority, so 'highest priority DERProgram' = the one with the numerically lowest primacy after the swap. Procedure step 2 says subscribe to the DERProgramList; Pass/Fail additionally asserts a subscription to the DERProgram itself and that the subscription used the all value as limit - subscribe to both. Title tag [A, S].

We should only require subscription to the List, which is what the tester currently does. Also, Step 2 requires the limit parameter to be set to all by the client. It should instead state that if the number of end devices available is greater than the limit value, the client should get the additional items after notification of any changes by the server. The tester currently sets a limit of 100.

title: Utility Server Startup Configuration Group Assignment of Inverters [S]

section: 8 Utility Server Aggregator Model Tests
title: Utility - Aggregator Operations Commissioning [A, S]
purpose: The utility-aggregator operations commissioning test verifies that the aggregator can interact with its utility server to be commissioned using the topology-based grouping for its managed inverters. This test shall include test scenarios that test the commissioning aspects of the operation, including discovery, secure connection, and retrieval of device information for all managed downstream inverters.
applicability_reason: PROFILE SCOPE 2026-07-28 (owner decision, SUPERSEDING the DER Aggregator Client scoping taken earlier the same day; docs/PROFILE_SCOPE_2026-07-28_der-client-gfems.md, and lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1-§1.2 rev. b): the DUT is certified against the CTP §4 DER CLIENT column in the Generating Facility EMS (GFEMS) posture — the DERs behind ONE point of interconnection, presented to the utility as a single 2030.5 client with one EndDevice and one LFDI and each admitted DER a DER instance beneath it (lexa-gw product decision D3.1), which is the shape docs/UTILITY_DECISION_PACK.md §1 already commits to as Scenario 1 / Direct. CSIP Conformance Test Procedures V1.3 §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves this row BLANK in the DER Client column and marks it X only in the DER Aggregator Client column (profile_conformance: der_client_required=false, der_aggregator_client_required=true). The two client columns nest strictly — no row is required of a DER Client that is not also required of a DER Aggregator Client — so this is one of exactly twenty-two rows the narrower claim drops: it is NOT REQUIRED of this DUT and is no part of the certification claim. INFORMATIVE, NOT UNIMPLEMENTED: the check stays registered in suitecsip and keeps running, which is this tool's standing treatment of an implemented-but-inapplicable row. Its criteria are real evaluators rather than the not-applicable stub, so its verdicts — including negative ones — are evidence about a capability this product does not claim, and no verdict of this row gates conformance. dut_role stays csip-client because the row still exercises the 2030.5 CLIENT surface; `certify -applicable` is the flag that drops it from a run. BENCH: the fixture this row was written against is built and is OFF BY DEFAULT, so an informative lever cannot re-measure certified evidence — `sim/server -fleet` serves the CTP Figure-15 topology (an aggregator EndDevice plus EDA1/EDA2 under SPA1/SPA2 and EDB1/EDB2 under SPB1/SPB2) and the default tree is pinned byte-identical by sim/gridsim/golden_default_test.go. With -fleet on, the per-EndDevice criteria grade for real against the LFDIs gridsim derived for EDA1/EDA2/EDB1/EDB2, read from GET /admin/fleet rather than inferred from /edev ordering; with it off they SKIP naming the fixture, and a SKIP is a runtime fact about this bench, never a pass. BENCH: this row turns on the 2030.5 Subscription/Notification function set — the DUT must accept a server-originated Notification POST at its notificationURI. `sim/server -subscription` serves that function set, also off by default. One bench limit is disclosed rather than papered over: gridsim is pure Go and Go's crypto/tls has no ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-CCM-8, so its built-in notifier REFUSES an https:// notificationURI rather than dialling a non-conformant one (sim/gridsim/subscribe.go), and conformant delivery needs an externally installed Notifier. The three outcomes stay apart: the DUT answered wrongly is a FAIL; nobody was subscribed, or the server could not DELIVER, is a SKIP naming which. The notification halves of this row rest on that same function set, which lexa-gw does not implement and which the owner intends to add as an optional capability under this profile (see CORE-018). The whole commissioning walk this row specifies — /dcap → EndDeviceList → match own LFDI → GET RegistrationLink → compare pIN → PUT DERCapability/DERSettings/DERStatus/DERAvailability — IS driven and asserted for real for the DUT's own EndDevice, and under -fleet the 'for all other EndDevice instances (EDA1, EDA2, EDB1, EDB2)' half is graded too. ERRATA seq 3 applies: the PUT goes to the DER field resources, NOT to the DERListLink.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: n/a — no lexa-gw surface implements this test; the HTTP PUT request lines (DERCapability/DERSettings/DERStatus/DERAvailability hrefs) with 204/200 responses in the gridsim transcript; the GET on the RegistrationLink and the pIN value compared against the configured PIN; source observables to assert verbatim: HTTP GET /dcap -> 200 XML DeviceCapability with EndDeviceListLink / HTTP GET <EndDeviceListLink URI> (e.g. /edev) -> 200 XML EndDeviceList; per-EndDevice GETs
preconditions: Perform the test setup from the UTIL-001 - Utility Server Startup Configuration Group Assignment of Inverters test to configure the Utility Server.
The aggregator client device has preregistered a PIN value with the utility server.
The aggregator EUT shall have completed the tests described in Communication Fundamentals Tests, Core Function Set Tests, and Basic Functions Tests.

title: Utility - Aggregator Operations DER Retrieval [A, S]
purpose: The utility-aggregator operations DER retrieval test verifies that the aggregator can interact with its utility server to get the DERProgram/DERControl and associated information, such as DERCurve, DefaultDERControl, and ActiveDERControl. This test shall include test scenarios that test aggregator conformance to get and process relevant DERProgram/DERControl information for all managed inverters, including scheduling of appropriate DER events as applicable.
applicability_reason: PROFILE SCOPE 2026-07-28 (owner decision, SUPERSEDING the DER Aggregator Client scoping taken earlier the same day; docs/PROFILE_SCOPE_2026-07-28_der-client-gfems.md, and lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_CSIP.md §1.1-§1.2 rev. b): the DUT is certified against the CTP §4 DER CLIENT column in the Generating Facility EMS (GFEMS) posture — the DERs behind ONE point of interconnection, presented to the utility as a single 2030.5 client with one EndDevice and one LFDI and each admitted DER a DER instance beneath it (lexa-gw product decision D3.1), which is the shape docs/UTILITY_DECISION_PACK.md §1 already commits to as Scenario 1 / Direct. CSIP Conformance Test Procedures V1.3 §4 Profile Test Conformance leaves this row BLANK in the DER Client column and marks it X only in the DER Aggregator Client column (profile_conformance: der_client_required=false, der_aggregator_client_required=true). The two client columns nest strictly — no row is required of a DER Client that is not also required of a DER Aggregator Client — so this is one of exactly twenty-two rows the narrower claim drops: it is NOT REQUIRED of this DUT and is no part of the certification claim. INFORMATIVE, NOT UNIMPLEMENTED: the check stays registered in suitecsip and keeps running, which is this tool's standing treatment of an implemented-but-inapplicable row. Its criteria are real evaluators rather than the not-applicable stub, so its verdicts — including negative ones — are evidence about a capability this product does not claim, and no verdict of this row gates conformance. dut_role stays csip-client because the row still exercises the 2030.5 CLIENT surface; `certify -applicable` is the flag that drops it from a run. BENCH: the fixture this row was written against is built and is OFF BY DEFAULT, so an informative lever cannot re-measure certified evidence — `sim/server -fleet` serves the CTP Figure-15 topology (an aggregator EndDevice plus EDA1/EDA2 under SPA1/SPA2 and EDB1/EDB2 under SPB1/SPB2) and the default tree is pinned byte-identical by sim/gridsim/golden_default_test.go. With -fleet on, the per-EndDevice criteria grade for real against the LFDIs gridsim derived for EDA1/EDA2/EDB1/EDB2, read from GET /admin/fleet rather than inferred from /edev ordering; with it off they SKIP naming the fixture, and a SKIP is a runtime fact about this bench, never a pass. BENCH: this row turns on the 2030.5 Subscription/Notification function set — the DUT must accept a server-originated Notification POST at its notificationURI. `sim/server -subscription` serves that function set, also off by default. One bench limit is disclosed rather than papered over: gridsim is pure Go and Go's crypto/tls has no ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-CCM-8, so its built-in notifier REFUSES an https:// notificationURI rather than dialling a non-conformant one (sim/gridsim/subscribe.go), and conformant delivery needs an externally installed Notifier. The three outcomes stay apart: the DUT answered wrongly is a FAIL; nobody was subscribed, or the server could not DELIVER, is a SKIP naming which. The notification halves of this row rest on that same function set, which lexa-gw does not implement and which the owner intends to add as an optional capability under this profile (see CORE-018). The DERControl (start +2 min, duration 2 min) is published for real and the GET DERControlList → GET DERControl → POST Response(1/2/3) loop asserted. The scope ladder SKIPs naming its own reason rather than the fixture: POST /admin/control addresses a DERProgram by INDEX, so a published control reaches TFA and SY and no other node. section: 2.4 Scale Factor Test
title: Scale Factor Test
purpose: "The scale factor test verifies the scale factors are valid and in the correct range." It proves each implemented scale-factored point carries a scale factor whose value keeps the point's representable range/resolution within what IEEE 1547 requires for that point's data type.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4 + §4: the northbound chain carries Model 1, 701, 702, 704, 713 and a header-only 714 with their mandatory points and scale factors, all readable with FC=0x03, so both mandatory-point and scale-factor sweeps execute. CAVEAT — this is a per-(build, DER model) claim, not a fixed gap. 703 and 705-712 ARE chained northbound, DEVICE-CONDITIONALLY: a unit carries a conditional model iff its own DER serves it southbound (lexa-gw internal/regmap/chain.go deviceConditionalModels :193-203, applied by ClassModelsFor :235-252), because a chained-but-empty curve or trip model would be the gateway claiming a function whose every required point reads not-implemented — which fails MOD-4 step 3 for the WHOLE unit and is worse than the honest absence. So the 'every required model is implemented' verdict is a property of the (gateway build, DER model) PAIR and must be reported per DER model: a DER serving 703 and 705-712 yields a unit that can pass, a weaker DER yields a unit that truthfully does not claim, and the claim is capped by the weakest DER in the fleet because the gateway serves one unit per device and makes no aggregate unit (lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_SUNSPEC_MODBUS.md §3.1 and docs/design/MOD4_1547_PROFILE_SCOPE.md §4.5; pinned by TestChain_AWeakDERClaimsOnlyWhatItServes and TestChain_A707CapableDERClaimsEveryProfileRequiredModel). This replaces a stale caveat which said BuildChain REJECTS 703 and 705-712 northbound. HARNESS: this suite carries no transcription of the flattened curve-model layouts, so for a unit that DOES chain them the per-point sweep reports SKIP for those models naming that (checks_1547.go:100-107) while the model-presence assertion still grades.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: The returned int16 scale-factor value (SunSpec sunssf range -10..10, with 0x8000 meaning not-implemented) captured in the read response PDU. / Pairing on the wire of the value register(s) for a point with its scale-factor register within the same model block, so the effective engineering value = raw x 10^sf can be computed.
preconditions: The DUT implements the SunSpec Modbus interface and at least one point that has an associated scale factor.
The set of implemented points and their scale factors is known (from the device PICS workbook per 2.1, and/or from model discovery).
The IEEE 1547 accuracy/range requirements applicable to each point and the point's data type are known (referenced but not enumerated in this document).
steps: For each implemented point that has a scale factor:
1. Read the corresponding scale factor value.
2. Verify the scale factor value lies in the acceptable range to meet the IEEE 1547 requirements based on the data type of the corresponding point.
expected: Each read scale factor value lies within the acceptable range required to meet the IEEE 1547 requirements for the corresponding point.

The acceptable range is determined per point as a function of the data type of that point (e.g. a signed 16-bit point needs a scale factor that yields sufficient resolution and headroom over the required measurement/setting range).
The check is repeated for every implemented scale-factored point, i.e. it fails if any single scale factor is out of range.
observables: Modbus register read of each scale-factor register (SunSpec sunssf / int16 scale-factor point) inside the implemented model's block - the document does not state a function code, but in practice FC=0x03 Read Holding Registers over Modbus/TCP port 502.
The returned int16 scale-factor value (SunSpec sunssf range -10..10, with 0x8000 meaning not-implemented) captured in the read response PDU.
Pairing on the wire of the value register(s) for a point with its scale-factor register within the same model block, so the effective engineering value = raw x 10^sf can be computed.
notes: This procedure is printed WITHOUT a MOD-style test identifier; the only identifier available is the section number 2.4, used here as the id. Unlike 2.3.1, section 2.4 contains no explicit 'MUST' sentence of its own - the MUST is inherited from section 1 Introduction ('the tests mentioned in this document MUST be performed successfully'). The document does NOT enumerate the acceptable scale-factor ranges, the per-point data types, or the IEEE 1547 accuracy requirements that define 'acceptable range', so a harness must source those externally (PICS + the IEEE 1547-2018 profile guide). Categorization: this is not explicitly assigned to one of the four categories in 2.2 (general device / general model / curve / reversion / Modbus protocol); it reads as per-point and therefore effectively per-model.

section: 2.3.1 MOD-4 - Mandatory Points (under 2.3 General SunSpec Model Tests)
title: MOD-4 - Mandatory Points
purpose: "This test validates all the points required for IEEE 1547 implementation are present in the device." It proves the DUT exposes every mandatory SunSpec point, and every required SunSpec model, called for by the SunSpec Modbus IEEE 1547-2018 profile.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4 + §4: the northbound chain carries Model 1, 701, 702, 704, 713 and a header-only 714 with their mandatory points and scale factors, all readable with FC=0x03, so both mandatory-point and scale-factor sweeps execute. So the 'every required model is implemented' verdict is a property of the (gateway build, DER model) PAIR and must be reported per DER model: a DER serving 703 and 705-712 yields a unit that can pass, a weaker DER yields a unit that truthfully does not claim, and the claim is capped by the weakest DER in the fleet because the gateway serves one unit per device and makes no aggregate unit (lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_SUNSPEC_MODBUS.md §3.1 and docs/design/MOD4_1547_PROFILE_SCOPE.md §4.5; pinned by TestChain_AWeakDERClaimsOnlyWhatItServes and TestChain_A707CapableDERClaimsEveryProfileRequiredModel). This replaces a stale caveat which said BuildChain REJECTS 703 and 705-712 northbound. HARNESS: this suite carries no transcription of the flattened curve-model layouts, so for a unit that DOES chain them the per-point sweep reports SKIP for those models naming that (checks_1547.go:100-107) while the model-presence assertion still grades.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Per-point register read-back values for every point in every implemented model, used for the presence comparison against the mandatory-point list. / Model discovery chain terminating at the end-of-map marker (model ID 0xFFFF), from which 'every required model is implemented' is judged.
preconditions: The DUT implements the SunSpec Modbus interface and can be probed over it (per 2.1, the SVP Dashboard probes device contents through the SunSpec Modbus interface).

A device PICS (protocol implementation conformance statement) Excel workbook exists that specifies the SunSpec models and points supported in the implementation along with the supported value ranges associated with each adjustable point (2.1 Test Inputs). A SunSpec Modbus PICS template can be obtained from the SunSpec Alliance; an initial PICS may be auto-generated by the SunSpec Dashboard / SVP Dashboard and then updated by hand for details not discoverable during initial discovery.

The list of mandatory IEEE 1547 points is obtained from the external document 'SunSpec Modbus IEEE 1547-2018 Profile Specification and Implementation Guide' (hyperlinked in the text; content NOT reproduced in this document).

All tests in the (separate) SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures document have been / are also being performed successfully (see 1 Introduction and 2.3 preamble: this test is performed 'in addition to' the General SunSpec Model Tests in that document).

Only SunSpec standardized models are considered during certification testing; any additional vendor-specific models must conform to SunSpec information modeling rules to the extent that they do not inhibit discovery and use of the standardized models supported in the device (2.1).
steps: 1. For each model, read the point in the model.
2. Compare the point to the list of mandatory points for IEEE 1547 implementation.
3. Verify all the required points are implemented in the model.
4. Verify every required model is implemented.
expected: Every point listed as mandatory for IEEE 1547 implementation (per the SunSpec Modbus IEEE 1547-2018 Profile Specification and Implementation Guide) is present/implemented in its model on the device.
Every model required by the IEEE 1547-2018 profile is implemented in the device.
The test is a general model test, so it is performed once for each SunSpec model implemented in the device (2.2 Test Categories).
observables: Modbus read of each implemented model's register block (SunSpec device map walk: 'SunS' identifier followed by (model ID, model length) headers and per-model register blocks) - the document does not state a function code, but in practice FC=0x03 Read Holding Registers over Modbus/TCP port 502.
Per-point register read-back values for every point in every implemented model, used for the presence comparison against the mandatory-point list.
Model discovery chain terminating at the end-of-map marker (model ID 0xFFFF), from which 'every required model is implemented' is judged.

A non-implemented mandatory point would be observable either as an absent point in the model's declared length/repeating-block layout or as the SunSpec 'not implemented' sentinel value for the point's data type in the read-back.
requirement_refs: SunSpec Modbus IEEE 1547-2018 Profile Specification and Implementation Guide
SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures (General SunSpec Model Tests)
notes: MUST-level: section 2.3 states 'In addition to the General SunSpec Model Tests in the SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures, this test MUST be performed.' The actual mandatory point/model list is NOT in this document - it is entirely delegated to the hyperlinked SunSpec Modbus IEEE 1547-2018 Profile Specification and Implementation Guide, so a harness cannot execute MOD-4 from this PDF alone. No register numbers, model IDs (e.g. 701-713), point names, function codes, or pass/fail thresholds appear anywhere in this document. 'Verify' in steps 3-4 is a comparison against an external list, observable via Modbus register read-back of the device model map. Test ID 'MOD-4' implies sibling tests MOD-1..MOD-3 exist in the separate SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures document; they are not in this PDF.

section: 1 Introduction
title: Test Results Report (TRR) deliverable exists and is split into public vs. archived parts
purpose: Proves the submission package is the artifact SunSpec uses to determine compliance of a DER device to IEEE 2030.5/CSIP and to grant the SunSpec Certified mark, and that the submitter has correctly separated the publicly-posted portion from the archive-only portion.
applicability_reason: Report-format requirement on the CONFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION TOOL rather than on the DUT. It is satisfiable today: facts-dut-capability.md §5 shows the estate already emits verdict artifacts (sim/ssm-conformance's CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md section, gw-mayhem's JSON verdict board, cmd/dashboard's /api/gw/qa/report), and the harness owns one end of every TLS session so it can log the exchange in unencrypted form; the missing piece is the emitter itself (facts-dut-capability.md §8.4: 'Evidence-capture is the real gap'). The value is supplied by the certifying lab or the submitter, not derivable from a bench run.
evidence: the emitted TRR artifacts themselves: the Summary Test Results CSV (key,value rows incl. `Test <ID>,PASS`) and the Detailed Test Log JSON objects, plus the raw pcap files they reference; source observables to assert verbatim: Delivered file set: one CSV document (Summary Test Results) + one or more JSON documents (Detailed Test Logs) / For CSIP submissions the Summary CSV row `Certificate Type,IEEE 2030.5/CSIP`
preconditions: A DUT (client, aggregator client, or server) has been tested by a SunSpec Authorized Test Laboratory using the SunSpec IEEE 2030.5/CSIP Conformance Test Procedures.
The testing tool that implements the SunSpec IEEE 2030.5/CSIP Test Procedures is able to generate a Test Results Report.
steps: Generate the Test Results Report using a testing tool that implements the SunSpec IEEE 2030.5/CSIP Conformance Test Procedures.
Confirm the report addresses the General Testing Considerations section content (setup/run validity information, per Chapter 2).
Confirm the report contains the Test Results Report (TRR) Format Specification content (Chapter 3) — the specific data SunSpec needs to make a certification evaluation of the device that was tested.
Confirm the Detailed Test Logs (Chapter 4) are supplied as the data used by SunSpec to verify successful execution of each test procedure.

Confirm the submitter understands that Chapter 3 content is posted on the SunSpec web site and made available to the general public, while Chapter 4 content is archived by SunSpec, used only for confirming test results, and NOT shared with the public.
expected: The submission is composed of the three specified parts: General Testing Considerations conformity, TRR Format Specification data, and Detailed Test Logs.
TRR Format Specification data (Chapter 3) is publishable — it contains nothing the submitter needs withheld from the public.
Detailed Test Logs (Chapter 4) are supplied for EACH test procedure executed.

section: 2.1 Equipment Version
title: Equipment version unaltered for the whole test campaign
purpose: Proves that every reported test result was produced by one single, unmodified software/hardware build, so results are attributable to the exact version identified in the Summary Test Results.
applicability_reason: Report-format requirement on the CONFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION TOOL rather than on the DUT. It is satisfiable today: facts-dut-capability.md §5 shows the estate already emits verdict artifacts (sim/ssm-conformance's CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md section, gw-mayhem's JSON verdict board, cmd/dashboard's /api/gw/qa/report), and the harness owns one end of every TLS session so it can log the exchange in unencrypted form; the missing piece is the emitter itself (facts-dut-capability.md §8.4: 'Evidence-capture is the real gap'). The tool can auto-fill this from the board (image hash, /etc/os-release, configs) over ssh, but an operator must confirm the declared identity/version freeze.
evidence: the emitted TRR artifacts themselves: the Summary Test Results CSV (key,value rows incl. `Test <ID>,PASS`) and the Detailed Test Log JSON objects, plus the raw pcap files they reference; source observables to assert verbatim: Summary CSV rows `Software Version 1`, `Software Checksum 1`, `Operating System Version 1`, `Hardware Model 1` identical across the whole campaign / Detailed Test Log timestamps (`time` field) forming one monotonic campaign window with no version change in between
preconditions: The DUT software version, software checksum, OS version and hardware model are recorded before testing starts (see RPT-024, RPT-025, RPT-026).
steps: Record DUT software name/version/checksum, operating system and version, and hardware manufacturer/model before starting the test procedures.
Execute all test procedures without altering the software or hardware during the testing process.
If any change is made to the software or hardware at any point, restart the entire testing process.
expected: All tests were completed without altering the software or hardware during the testing process.
If any software or hardware change occurred, the testing process was restarted and only results from the restarted (unmodified) run are reported.
observables: Summary CSV rows `Software Version 1`, `Software Checksum 1`, `Operating System Version 1`, `Hardware Model 1` identical across the whole campaign
Detailed Test Log timestamps (`time` field) forming one monotonic campaign window with no version change in between
notes: MUST-level ('All tests must be completed without altering...'). No mechanism is specified for evidencing non-alteration; the software checksum key is the only machine-checkable anchor. Our tool should stamp the build checksum into every log bundle.

section: 4 Detailed Test Logs
title: Detailed Test Logs contain every HTTP(S) message in UNENCRYPTED form, JSON-encoded
purpose: Proves SunSpec can verify successful execution of each test procedure by reading the actual protocol exchange, which requires the TLS-protected traffic be decrypted in the log.
applicability_reason: Report-format requirement on the CONFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION TOOL rather than on the DUT. It is satisfiable today: facts-dut-capability.md §5 shows the estate already emits verdict artifacts (sim/ssm-conformance's CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md section, gw-mayhem's JSON verdict board, cmd/dashboard's /api/gw/qa/report), and the harness owns one end of every TLS session so it can log the exchange in unencrypted form; the missing piece is the emitter itself (facts-dut-capability.md §8.4: 'Evidence-capture is the real gap'). Decryption is not needed: the harness terminates the peer end of every session (gridsim for CSIP, the aggregator/ssm-conformance client for mbaps), so it can serialise the HTTP/Modbus messages in the clear at the application layer.
evidence: the emitted TRR artifacts themselves: the Summary Test Results CSV (key,value rows incl. `Test <ID>,PASS`) and the Detailed Test Log JSON objects, plus the raw pcap files they reference; source observables to assert verbatim: JSON document(s) containing arrays of message objects with readable `body` strings such as `<DeviceCapability href="/sep2/dcap" .../>` / No TLS record framing in the log — the log is at the HTTP layer, not the TLS layer
preconditions: All test procedures have been executed and their HTTP(S) traffic captured.
The testing tool has access to the plaintext of the HTTPS exchange (e.g. it terminates TLS itself).
steps: Collect the HTTP message logs for ALL the tests performed.
Supply the detailed test logs in a single document or in multiple documents, in the format of §4.1.1–§4.1.3.
Ensure the logs contain ALL HTTP(S) messages that were transferred as part of the test, in UNENCRYPTED form.
Encode the detailed test logs in JSON using the three defined object types: Test Log, Message, and Test Logs.
expected: Detailed test logs consist of HTTP message logs for all tests performed.
Single-document or multi-document delivery is both acceptable.
Every HTTP(S) message transferred as part of the test is present.
Messages are recorded in unencrypted (plaintext) form — an encrypted or ciphertext-only capture does not satisfy this.
Encoding is JSON using the Test Log, Message, and Test Logs object definitions.
observables: JSON document(s) containing arrays of message objects with readable `body` strings such as `<DeviceCapability href="/sep2/dcap" .../>`
No TLS record framing in the log — the log is at the HTTP layer, not the TLS layer
notes: Key requirement for our demo tool: it must be able to dump DECRYPTED HTTP for a mutually-authenticated TLS CSIP session. Note the contrast with Chapter 5, which requires RAW TLS packets for COMM-004 — the two artifacts are complementary, not alternatives.

expected: Object literal form is: {"logs": [<array of test log objects>], "cid": <context id>}
`logs` is an array of test log objects — mandatory.
`cid` is the context id — OPTIONAL.
notes: The heading in §4 calls this 'Test Logs Object' while the two content labels in §4.1.3 read 'Tests Logs Object contents' and 'Tests Logs Object JSON format' — a naming inconsistency in the source. `cid` is the mechanism that stitches separately-archived documents back together, so our tool should always emit a stable cid per campaign even though it is optional.

section: 5 COMM-004 Connection TLS Packet Traces
title: COMM-004 raw TLS packet traces submitted per certificate scenario (added in v1.1)
purpose: Proves the DUT exhibited the correct TLS connection-establishment behaviour for each certificate scenario presented to it in COMM-004 — behaviour that is invisible in the decrypted HTTP logs of Chapter 4 because a rejected connection produces no HTTP at all.
applicability_reason: Report-format requirement on the CONFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION TOOL rather than on the DUT. It is satisfiable today: facts-dut-capability.md §5 shows the estate already emits verdict artifacts (sim/ssm-conformance's CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md section, gw-mayhem's JSON verdict board, cmd/dashboard's /api/gw/qa/report), and the harness owns one end of every TLS session so it can log the exchange in unencrypted form; the missing piece is the emitter itself (facts-dut-capability.md §8.4: 'Evidence-capture is the real gap'). facts-dut-capability.md §6.4 is explicit that pcap exists ONLY for the CSIP loopback leg today (run-conformance.sh --capture on `lo`, port 11111); per-scenario capture on the bench legs is new work, but the board having no tcpdump is not a blocker because the desktop is the peer on every link.
evidence: the emitted TRR artifacts themselves: the Summary Test Results CSV (key,value rows incl. `Test <ID>,PASS`) and the Detailed Test Log JSON objects, plus the raw pcap files they reference; the fatal TLS Alert record (level=fatal, description code visible in the clear even for a TLS1.3 handshake failure) followed by FIN/RST from the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: Libpcap (.pcap) or PcapNg (.pcapng) file per COMM-004 scenario / TLS ClientHello / ServerHello / Certificate / CertificateRequest / CertificateVerify / Finished records for accepted scenarios
preconditions: COMM-004 has been executed. COMM-004 specifies a series of connection tests involving different certificate scenarios being presented to the device under test.
A packet capture facility was running on the connection path for each COMM-004 connection scenario.
steps: For each connection scenario specified in COMM-004, present the scenario's certificate to the device under test.
Capture the TLS packets so they can be inspected to verify the correct test behavior.
Produce a packet trace in either Libpcap or PcapNg format that includes ALL the TLS packets associated with connection establishment.
Submit one such packet trace for EACH connection scenario specified in COMM-004.
expected: A packet trace is submitted for each connection scenario specified in COMM-004.
Trace format is Libpcap OR PcapNg.
Each trace includes all the TLS packets associated with connection establishment (not just a summary, and not truncated before the handshake completes or aborts).
The traces permit inspection of the TLS packets to verify the correct test behavior for the certificate scenario presented.
observables: Libpcap (.pcap) or PcapNg (.pcapng) file per COMM-004 scenario
TLS ClientHello / ServerHello / Certificate / CertificateRequest / CertificateVerify / Finished records for accepted scenarios
TLS Alert record (e.g. bad_certificate, unknown_ca, certificate_expired, handshake_failure) or TCP RST/FIN with no Finished for rejected scenarios
Full TCP handshake + TLS handshake for each certificate scenario, unencrypted at the record-header level
notes: This whole chapter is the ONLY change in v1.1 ('Added COMM-004 connection TLS packet trace requirement.'). The requirement is stated at SHOULD level ('A packet trace ... should be submitted'), not MUST, but the revision history calls it a 'requirement'. The specific certificate scenarios, expected accept/reject outcomes, and any required alert codes live in COMM-004 in the SunSpec IEEE 2030.5/CSIP Conformance Test Procedures document — they are NOT enumerated here. Note the tension with §4: Chapter 4 wants HTTP decrypted, Chapter 5 wants the TLS layer raw, so our tool must be able to emit both from the same COMM-004 run.

2. Share the server TCP or RTU settings with the CUT operator or send this data to the CUT test interface.

Three separate discovery sessions in the pcap, each with a different base register, each ending in a Common Model (ID 1) read

section: 2.9.1 ERR-1 – Noncompliant Server (under 2.9 Error Tests)
title: Noncompliant Server
purpose: Verifies the CUT recovers when connecting to a non-SunSpec compliant Server.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. Requires new fault modes in the desktop sim (partial response, TCP segmentation, forced exception codes, unimplemented-value seeding, non-compliant base address); modsim's simapi (facts-dut-capability.md §5) has the injection surface but not these vocabularies yet.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: CUT FC=0x03 probes at the legal SunSpec base addresses (0, 40000, 50000) that do NOT return the 'SunS' identifier (0x5375 0x6e53), because the map is offset by one register to 40001 / TCP connection established but discovery failing — no valid model chain walk follows
preconditions: Server 1 must be configurable to place the SunSpec register map at an arbitrary (noncompliant) base address.
Per §2.9 preamble: these tests verify that the device under test performs exception handling correctly.
steps: 1. Configure Server 1 to start the SunSpec registers at holding register 40001.
2. Attempt to connect the CUT to Server 1.
expected: The Client SHALL accurately log the noncompliant server.
The log may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
The CUT recovers (does not hang or crash) when connecting to the non-SunSpec-compliant Server.
observables: CUT FC=0x03 probes at the legal SunSpec base addresses (0, 40000, 50000) that do NOT return the 'SunS' identifier (0x5375 0x6e53), because the map is offset by one register to 40001
TCP connection established but discovery failing — no valid model chain walk follows
CUT log entry explicitly identifying Server 1 as noncompliant / SunSpec identifier not found
CUT remains responsive afterwards (no crash, process still alive)
notes: The noncompliance is a deliberate one-register offset: 40001 instead of the compliant 40000 exercised in CLI-4. The test does NOT require the CUT to auto-discover the offset map — the required behavior is to LOG the server as noncompliant. Ambiguity: the doc does not say whether 40001 means Modbus data-model address 40001 or the 1-based holding-register convention where 40001 == address 0; the intent from CLI-4 (which uses 0/40000/50000) is that 40001 is off-by-one from a valid base.

section: 2.9.2 ERR-2 – Exception Tests (under 2.9 Error Tests)
title: Exception Tests
purpose: Verifies the CUT appropriately interprets, logs, manages, and recovers from Modbus Exceptions.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. Requires new fault modes in the desktop sim (partial response, TCP segmentation, forced exception codes, unimplemented-value seeding, non-compliant base address); modsim's simapi (facts-dut-capability.md §5) has the injection surface but not these vocabularies yet.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; the Modbus exception response PDU (FC|0x80 + exception byte) in the app-layer log; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus exception responses on the wire: function code with the high bit set (request FC | 0x80) followed by a one-byte exception code / Exception code 0x01 ILLEGAL FUNCTION — provoked by requesting illegal function code 0x88
preconditions: Server 1 configured per §2.3 and able to return Modbus exception responses.

Server 1 must contain at least one Read-Only register, at least one unimplemented point, and at least one Enum register with values that are not defined/supported, so the four exception classes can be provoked.
Test engineer has determined which operations on Server 1 generate Exception codes 1, 2, 3 and 4.
steps: 1. Determine operations for Server 1 that generate Exception codes 1, 2, 3 and 4. Examples include: (a) Requesting illegal function code 0x88; (b) Writing a Read-Only register; (c) Writing to unimplemented point; (d) Writing an Enum register to a value that is not defined or supported in the Server.
2. Request operations from Server 1 that produces Exception codes 1, 2, 3 and 4.
3. Verify the CUT logs each Modbus Exception and continues to operate normally.
expected: The Client SHALL accurately log all exception codes.
The CUT continues to operate normally after each Modbus Exception.
The log may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
observables: Modbus exception responses on the wire: function code with the high bit set (request FC | 0x80) followed by a one-byte exception code
Exception code 0x01 ILLEGAL FUNCTION — provoked by requesting illegal function code 0x88
Exception code 0x02 ILLEGAL DATA ADDRESS — e.g. writing to an unimplemented point/address
Exception code 0x03 ILLEGAL DATA VALUE — e.g. writing an Enum register to a value not defined or supported in the Server
Exception code 0x04 SERVER DEVICE FAILURE — e.g. writing a Read-Only register (server-dependent)
CUT log entries naming each exception code received
Subsequent successful Modbus transactions on the same or a new connection, proving the CUT continues to operate normally
notes: The doc lists four example provocations (a-d) but does NOT map each example to a specific exception code — the mapping above is the conventional Modbus mapping and must be confirmed against the actual server. 'Requesting illegal function code 0x88' is odd wording: 0x88 is itself the exception-response encoding of FC 0x08; read it as 'send a request with a function code the server does not implement'. Exception codes are written as decimal 1,2,3,4 in the doc (= 0x01-0x04).

section: 2.9.3 ERR-3 – Unknown Model ID Test (under 2.9 Error Tests)
title: Unknown Model ID Test
purpose: Verifies the CUT appropriately responds to presence of models with unknown IDs.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. Requires new fault modes in the desktop sim (partial response, TCP segmentation, forced exception codes, unimplemented-value seeding, non-compliant base address); modsim's simapi (facts-dut-capability.md §5) has the injection surface but not these vocabularies yet.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: Successful TCP connect and FC=0x03 discovery: 'SunS' identifier read, then the model chain walk / The model-chain walk skips over the unknown model by using its length (L) header register and continues to the next model ID — i.e. the CUT does not abort discovery at the unknown model
preconditions: Server 1 must be configurable with a SunSpec map containing a model whose model ID is not present in the CUT's model definition directory.
The CUT's model definition directory contents must be known to the test engineer so an unknown ID can be chosen.
steps: 1. Configure Server 1 to start the SunSpec map that includes a model with a model ID that is not in the CUTs model definition directory.
2. Attempt to connect the CUT to Server 1.
expected: The Client SHALL connect to the server without issues.
The list of discovered models MUST not include the model with the unknown ID.
observables: Successful TCP connect and FC=0x03 discovery: 'SunS' identifier read, then the model chain walk
The model-chain walk skips over the unknown model by using its length (L) header register and continues to the next model ID — i.e. the CUT does not abort discovery at the unknown model
CUT-reported list of discovered models omits the unknown model ID while including all subsequent known models
No connection reset, no discovery abort, no error terminating the session
notes: Added in doc revision 1.0.1 (10-21-2025) as 'an error test for unknown model ID present in the server'. This is the only criterion in the document phrased with MUST rather than SHALL. Key behavioral implication: the CUT must use the model length header to skip an unrecognized model and continue the chain walk, and must NOT surface it as a discovered model. The doc does not say whether logging the unknown ID as a warning is permitted — it only forbids it appearing in the discovered-models list.

section: 2.7.1 INFO-1 – SunSpec Type Interpretations (under 2.7 Information Tests)
title: SunSpec Type Interpretations
purpose: Validates that the CUT can interpret all data points in the PICS.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. CAVEAT: the DUT reads whole model blocks through sunspec.Reader and renders only the measurement/identity points it consumes; it is not a generic point-browser, so 'read every point individually' and 'log every SunSpec datatype human-readably' are only partially demonstrable.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; the compression_methods field of the ClientHello (must be the single byte 0x00); source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 reads covering the Common Model (ID 1) and every PICS model on Server 1 / CUT-side human-readable log/report: this test's pass evidence is primarily the DECODED OUTPUT, not the wire
preconditions: Server 1 configured per §2.3 with all PICS models present.
CUT PICS enumerating every supported standardized model — §2.7 states these tests must be performed for each SunSpec supported standardized model specified in the PICS.
CUT able to render/print human-readable point values (not just raw hex).
steps: 1. Connect the CUT to Server 1.

2. Have the CUT read all Common model (model 1) points and print the human-readable information for these points. The values for the points SHALL comply with the following: (a) The CUT SHALL log the decimal value for all numerical points (int16, int32, int64, uint16, uint32, uint64), and convert all points using the appropriate scale factors. (b) The CUT SHALL log the decimal value for all points with floating points (float32, float64). (c) The CUT SHALL log ipaddr points in dotted-decimal format, e.g., 192.168.1.2. (d) The CUT SHALL log ipv6addr points with 128 bits written in hexadecimal notation, e.g., 2001:db8:1234::f350:2256:f3dd. The leading zeros in each group can be removed and two or more consecutive groups of zeros can be replaced by a double colon (::). (e) The CUT SHALL log eui48 points in capitalized decimal-hex format, e.g., B8:27:EB:12:34:56. (f) The CUT SHALL log bitfield16 and bitfield32 points as hex strings. (g) The CUT SHALL log string as human-readable UTF-8 strings. (h) The CUT SHALL log enum16 and enum32 points as the base 10 value (not name). (i) The CUT SHALL log all other points (pad, count, sunssf, acc16, acc32, acc64) as base 10 values.
3. Repeat Step 2 for each of the models in the PICS. Duplicated models may be skipped, i.e., the client may skip additional models of the same model ID.
expected: The Client SHALL accurately log all values in human-readable values.
Numerical points (int16, int32, int64, uint16, uint32, uint64) logged as decimal and scaled by the appropriate scale factors.
float32 and float64 points logged as decimal values.
ipaddr points logged in dotted-decimal format (e.g., 192.168.1.2).
ipv6addr points logged as 128 bits in hexadecimal notation with optional leading-zero suppression and :: compression (e.g., 2001:db8:1234::f350:2256:f3dd).
eui48 points logged in capitalized decimal-hex format (e.g., B8:27:EB:12:34:56).
bitfield16 and bitfield32 points logged as hex strings.
string points logged as human-readable UTF-8 strings.
enum16 and enum32 points logged as the base 10 value, not the symbolic name.
pad, count, sunssf, acc16, acc32, acc64 points logged as base 10 values.
The log may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 reads covering the Common Model (ID 1) and every PICS model on Server 1
CUT-side human-readable log/report: this test's pass evidence is primarily the DECODED OUTPUT, not the wire
Scale-factor application visible as decoded value = raw * 10^sunssf in the CUT log

Formatting assertions checkable by regex on the CUT log: dotted-quad for ipaddr, RFC-4291-style hextets with :: for ipv6addr, uppercase colon-separated hex octets for eui48, 0x-style hex for bitfield16/32, UTF-8 text for string, integers for enum16/32
notes: 'capitalized decimal-hex format' for eui48 is the doc's wording — the example B8:27:EB:12:34:56 is uppercase colon-separated hex. Note the deliberate asymmetry: enums must be logged as NUMBERS (not names) while bitfields must be logged as HEX STRINGS. Duplicate-model skipping is a MAY. §2.7 preamble scopes these tests to standardized models in the PICS.

section: 2.7.2 INFO-2 – Unimplemented Point Interpretations (under 2.7 Information Tests)
title: Unimplemented Point Interpretations
purpose: Validates that the CUT can interpret unimplemented points.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. Requires new fault modes in the desktop sim (partial response, TCP segmentation, forced exception codes, unimplemented-value seeding, non-compliant base address); modsim's simapi (facts-dut-capability.md §5) has the injection surface but not these vocabularies yet.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: CUT log marking those points as unimplemented / not-present rather than reporting the sentinel as a real numeric value / At least one unimplemented point logged for every data type present in the PICS models
preconditions: Server 1 configured per §2.3 with all PICS models present.

Test engineer has captured all the data types present in the PICS models (§2.3 data type list: int16, uint16, count, acc16, enum16, bitfield16, pad, int32, uint32, acc32, enum32, bitfield32, ipaddr, int64, uint64, acc64, ipv6addr, float32, float64, string, sunssf, eui48).
Server 1 must be re-configurable to set individual points to their type-specific unimplemented (not-implemented) sentinel value.
steps: 1. Connect the CUT to Server 1.
2. For all the data types present in the PICS models, update Server 1 to configure at least one of these points in the PICS models to the unimplemented value.
3. Have the CUT read all SunSpec points in all models in Server 1 and log the unimplemented points.
expected: The Client SHALL accurately log all unimplemented values in the PICS models.
The log may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 reads returning the type-specific unimplemented sentinel raw values (e.g. 0x8000 for int16, 0xFFFF for uint16/enum16/bitfield16, 0x80000000 for int32, 0xFFFFFFFF for uint32/enum32/bitfield32, 0x7FC00000 NaN for float32, 0x00 first byte for string)
CUT log marking those points as unimplemented / not-present rather than reporting the sentinel as a real numeric value
At least one unimplemented point logged for every data type present in the PICS models
notes: The document does NOT enumerate the per-type unimplemented sentinel values — those come from the SunSpec Device Information Model Specification. The harness must source the sentinel table from that spec. The criterion 'accurately log all unimplemented values' does not state a required rendering (e.g. 'N/A' vs sentinel echo), so the assertion is that the point is identified AS unimplemented.

section: 2.8.1 PROT-1 – Partial Response (under 2.8 Modbus Protocol Tests)
title: Partial Response
purpose: Validates the CUT can recover from an incomplete Modbus response message.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. Requires new fault modes in the desktop sim (partial response, TCP segmentation, forced exception codes, unimplemented-value seeding, non-compliant base address); modsim's simapi (facts-dut-capability.md §5) has the injection surface but not these vocabularies yet.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: First session: CUT FC=0x03 request for the Common Model (ID 1), server reply truncated — MBAP length field larger than the bytes actually delivered, or byte-count field inconsistent with the PDU payload / CUT does not hang or crash: a subsequent TCP connect and a second FC=0x03 Common Model request appear on the wire after the server is restored
preconditions: Server 1 must be preconfigurable to emit a partial (truncated/incomplete) Modbus response.
Server 1 must be reconfigurable back to normal behavior mid-test.
CUT able to issue a Common model read on demand.
steps: 1. Preconfigure Server 1 to respond with a partial Modbus response.
2. Connect CUT to Server 1.
3. Send a Common model read request from the client.
4. Reconfigure Server 1 to behave normally.
5. Connect CUT to Server 1.
6. Send a Common model read request from the client.
7. Verify the CUT logs the read values as expected.
expected: The Client SHALL remain functional after receiving the partial response.
The read log in Step 7 may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
The CUT logs the Common model read values as expected after the server returns to normal behavior.
observables: First session: CUT FC=0x03 request for the Common Model (ID 1), server reply truncated — MBAP length field larger than the bytes actually delivered, or byte-count field inconsistent with the PDU payload
CUT does not hang or crash: a subsequent TCP connect and a second FC=0x03 Common Model request appear on the wire after the server is restored
Second session: complete, well-formed FC=0x03 response and correctly decoded Common Model values in the CUT log
Optionally a CUT error/timeout log entry for the truncated first response
notes: The doc does not define what 'partial' means precisely (short TCP payload vs. inconsistent byte count vs. connection reset mid-PDU) — the harness should pick one and note it. Steps 2 and 5 both say 'Connect CUT to Server 1', implying the CUT reconnects; it does not say the CUT must recover on the SAME connection. No explicit timeout value is given.

CUT able to issue a read request on demand.

2. Connect CUT to Server 1.
3. Send a read request from the CUT.
4. Verify the CUT can parse the data from the TCP-segmented Modbus response.

Flagged as a document defect. Applies only to Modbus TCP clients (Table 6), which is the lexa-gw southbound case.

section: 2.5.2 READ-2 – Multiple Point Reads (under 2.5 Read Tests)
title: Multiple Point Reads
purpose: Validates the SunSpec Client Under Test (CUT) can read SunSpec Servers points at lengths up to the Modbus maximum read length (125 registers).
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: A single Modbus FC=0x03 request covering the entire Common Model (ID 1) body after the ID and L header registers (i.e. starting at base+2, quantity = model length) / For any model with length > 125 registers: a sequence of FC=0x03 requests each with quantity as close to 125 as the point boundaries allow, with no request splitting a single multi-register point
preconditions: Server 1 configured per §2.3 (100/200/700/800-series models, all PICS models in random order, >=5 extra models injected at random, >=1 PICS model duplicated).
CUT PICS enumerating the supported models, including at least one model whose length exceeds 125 registers if such a model is supported.
steps: 1. Connect the CUT to Server 1.
2. Verify all points after the ID and L points in the Common model (model 1) SHALL be read with a single request.

3. Repeat Step 2 for each of the models in the PICS. If the model length exceeds 125 registers, the model SHALL be read in multiple reads that maximize the number of points read in each holding register read operation. Partial point reads are not required.
expected: All points after the ID and L points of the Common model (model 1) are retrieved in a single Modbus read request.
For models longer than 125 registers, the model is read in multiple reads that maximize the number of points read in each holding register read operation.
Partial point reads are not required (a read need not split a multi-register point across requests).
The Client SHALL accurately log all points for all PICS models.
The log data SHALL be represented as hex strings.
The log may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
Network or serial traffic SHALL be analyzed to verify CUT operations.
observables: A single Modbus FC=0x03 request covering the entire Common Model (ID 1) body after the ID and L header registers (i.e. starting at base+2, quantity = model length)
For any model with length > 125 registers: a sequence of FC=0x03 requests each with quantity as close to 125 as the point boundaries allow, with no request splitting a single multi-register point
Absence of one-request-per-point traffic for this test (contrast with READ-1)
CUT log containing all point values as hex strings
notes: NOTE in the doc: 'this test may be completed in the discovery process in CLI-1, CLI-2, CLI-3, or CLI-4.' Modbus maximum read length is stated as 125 registers (FC=0x03 limit). 'Partial point reads are not required' means the client MAY under-fill a request to avoid splitting a point; 'maximize' is a SHALL but bounded by point boundaries.

section: 2.6.1 WR-1 – Write Single Point (under 2.6 Write Tests)
title: Write Single Point
purpose: Validates that all implemented adjustable points in the model can be written individually using Modbus Function Code 0x06.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.4: cmd/modbus is a SunSpec Modbus client over tcp://, rtu://, rtuovertcp://, bus:// and mbaps://, it probes all three standard bases (admission/identify.go:106 — 40000/0/50000), classifies by model (801/802 battery, 201-203 meter, 101-103 or 701-714 inverter) and reads/writes the 1547 profile models — the CUT role this procedure needs. CAVEAT: the DUT is a gateway, not an operator console — southbound writes are emitted only as the reconcilers act on a northbound command, so the write sweep must be driven indirectly (mbaps aggregator campaign or a CSIP DERControl) and covers only the executed point set of §1.5 / the reconcile_adv axes of §2.3.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 5020` — southbound plain Modbus/TCP is fully decodable in Wireshark: MBAP transaction id + unit id and FC=0x03/0x04/0x06/0x10 request+response frames issued BY the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06 (Write Single Register) requests, one per value, targeting each adjustable point's register address / Five distinct FC=0x06 writes per adjustable point: min, max, and three intermediate values from the Server 1 PICS (or all possible values if fewer than 5 exist)
preconditions: Server 1 configured per §2.3 and its PICS available, defining for every adjustable point the minimum value, maximum value, and the set of supported/enumerated values.
CUT connected to Server 1.
Server 1 PICS provided to the CUT operator, or a mechanism to programmatically send the CUT the 5 values for each point.
The CUT PICS indicates whether the CUT supports RTU server interfaces (required for step 3).
steps: 1. Verify all implemented adjustable points can be written to the minimum value, maximum value, and three intermediate values as defined in the Server 1 PICS using Modbus function code 0x06. If an adjustable point has fewer possible values, all possible values must be tested. (This can be done by providing the Server 1 PICS to the CUT operator or programmatically sending the CUT the 5 values for each point.)
2. For adjustable enumerated points, verify each supported value in the Server 1 PICS can be written using Modbus function code 0x06.
3. If the CUT supports RTU server interfaces as indicated in the PICS, rerun Steps 1 and 2 using Unit ID = 0 (the broadcast ID).
expected: The Client SHALL accurately log all write operations.
The log data SHALL be represented as hex strings.
The log may be displayed to the screen, saved to a file, transferred to the testing software, or otherwise shared with the test engineer.
Server write operations SHALL be validated by the test engineer.
Network or serial traffic SHALL be analyzed to verify CUT operations.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06 (Write Single Register) requests, one per value, targeting each adjustable point's register address
Five distinct FC=0x06 writes per adjustable point: min, max, and three intermediate values from the Server 1 PICS (or all possible values if fewer than 5 exist)
One FC=0x06 write per supported enum value for each adjustable enumerated point
Modbus RTU frames with slave address 0x00 (broadcast Unit ID = 0) carrying FC=0x06, if the CUT declares RTU support — and no response expected from the server for broadcast
Server-side state change confirmed by the test engineer (register read-back on the server)
CUT log of every write operation as hex strings
notes: FC 0x06 writes exactly one 16-bit register, so this test is inherently limited to single-register (16-bit) adjustable points unless the server permits per-register writes of multi-register points — the doc does not resolve this. Unit ID = 0 broadcast is explicitly for RTU server interfaces only; broadcast writes elicit no Modbus response, so the 'log all write operations' criterion must be satisfied without a reply.
