section: 2.5.1 CRV-1 - Curve 1 Support (under 2.5 Curve Tests)
title: Curve 1 Support
purpose: Validates that curve 1, which represents the current/active curve settings, is supported and that all points in curve 1 are implemented as read-only.
applicability_reason: APPLICABLE. CTP v1.4 §2.5.1 CRV-1 tests that curve 1 EXISTS, is declared read-only, and that its points CANNOT be written — it asserts a REFUSAL, not a writability, which is what separates it from CRV-2/CRV-3 and why it survives the read-only posture that kills those two. The DUT's northbound projection does serve curve models: lexa-gw internal/regmap/chain.go chains 703, 705, 706, 707-710, 711 and 712 DEVICE-CONDITIONALLY — a unit carries a conditional model iff its own DER serves it southbound (deviceConditionalModels chain.go:193-203, applied by ClassModelsFor :235-252) — and Curve 1 is mirrored from the DER's own block at admission with Crv1.ReadOnly authored to 1, which is profile item G2 (internal/regmap/curves.go:274-284, :303), while every write to a Crv1. point is refused (internal/regmap/pointgroups.go:274-276). lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_SUNSPEC_MODBUS.md §2.8 records CRV-1 as implemented [B,D]. This CORRECTS a stale reason which said BuildChain 'explicitly REJECTS the curve models 705-712 (chain.go:46-58)'; that stopped being true when the Stage 3 and Stage 4 chaining landed. SCOPE: the claim is per-(build, DER model) — a unit whose DER serves no 7xx curve model has no curve to test, which is a fact about that DER and not about the gateway, and the CTP's own precondition scopes the row to 'each curve-based model implemented in the device'. HARNESS: suitemodbusserver registers a check and it can only go so far. This suite carries no transcription of the flattened curve-model layouts (the same gap checks_1547.go:100-107 reports for MOD-4), so the curve-1 sub-block and its read-only indicator cannot be located on the wire; the check grades what the discovery walk proves — which curve models this unit chains — and SKIPs steps 2 and 3 naming the missing transcription. A registered SKIP with a reason is an engineering judgement; an unregistered row is an oversight.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the Modbus exception response PDU (FC|0x80 + exception byte) in the app-layer log; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 read of the curve repeating block showing curve index 1 populated. / Modbus FC=0x03 read of the curve's read-only indicator point (model-specific; the doc does not name it) showing read-only.
preconditions: The model under test contains curve or curve-like control functionality.
Curve tests are only applicable to models in the 7xx range (2.5).
Curve tests are performed for each curve-based model implemented in the device (2.2). Label = CRV-1.<modelID>, e.g. CRV-1.705.
steps: 1. Verify curve 1 is supported in the model.
2. Verify that curve 1 is marked as read-only.
3. Verify that the points associated with curve 1 cannot be written.
expected: Curve index 1 exists in the model's curve repeating block.
Curve 1 is flagged/declared read-only by the device.
Any write attempt to a point belonging to curve 1 fails (the write does not take effect).
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 read of the curve repeating block showing curve index 1 populated.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the curve's read-only indicator point (model-specific; the doc does not name it) showing read-only.
Modbus FC=0x06 or FC=0x10 write attempt to a curve-1 point followed by a Modbus exception response (per EXC-2, exception code 2, 3, or 4) and/or an unchanged value on read-back.
notes: The doc does not name the specific point that 'marks' curve 1 read-only, nor the exact exception expected on a curve-1 write — cross-reference EXC-2 (2.8.2), which requires exception code 2, 3, or 4 on a read-only write. Applicability is limited to 7xx models.

section: 2.5.2 CRV-2 - Apply Settings (under 2.5 Curve Tests)
title: Apply Settings
purpose: Validates that the current curve settings (curve 1) can be updated from each of the supported additional curves via the adopt-curve operation.
applicability_reason: Curve models ARE served northbound — see CRV-1, which corrects the stale claim that the northbound chain has no curve model at all. What this row needs and the DUT does not have is a WRITABLE SECOND curve. lexa-gw serves the staging curve wholly not-implemented: every Crv2. and Ctl2. field reads the sentinel and every write to one is refused before ACK (exception 02 for numeric points, 03 for enumerated ones), so profile §3.1 item G3 — 'the second curve MUST be writable, for settings updates' — is NOT IMPLEMENTED and there is no AdptCrvReq write executor for the adopt handshake to run against (AdptCrvReq is authored as 0, internal/regmap/curves.go:291-299; lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_SUNSPEC_MODBUS.md §2.8, §3.2). The write path is design Stage 5 (lexa-gw docs/design/DESIGN_2026-07-28_1547-northbound-models.md §5, §9) and is not built: MbapsCurveWrite, regmap.Staged and any staged branch in internal/listener/serve.go are absent from the tree. G3 and MOD-4 are different requirements and MOD-4 does not test G3.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x10 write of the differing curve point values into the writable curve's repeating-block registers (step 1 writable path). / Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of the adopt-curve request (curve index) — the register name is model-specific; for 7xx models the result point is AdptCrvRslt (named in 2.4.3).
preconditions: The model contains curve functionality and is in the 7xx range.
At least one additional curve (beyond curve 1) is supported.
CRV-1 established that curve 1 holds the current settings and is read-only.
Performed for each curve-based model (2.2). Label = CRV-2.<modelID>.
steps: For each supported additional curve:

1. For a writable curve, apply a different set of curve settings to the curve being tested than are present in curve 1. For a read-only curve, update curve 1 to contain a different set of settings than the read-only curve being tested.
2. Adopt the updated curve.
3. Verify that the update curve status indicates success.
4. Verify that the values in curve 1 match the values in the curve used for update.
5. Verify that the current curve settings (curve 1) can be updated from each of the additional supported curves.
6. If additional read-only curves are present, verify they are located after the writable curves.
expected: The adopt-curve request completes and the update curve status point indicates success.
After adoption, every point in curve 1 equals the corresponding point in the source curve that was adopted.
Curve 1 can be successfully updated from every additional supported curve, not just one.
Any read-only curves are ordered after the writable curves in the curve index space.
observables: Modbus FC=0x10 write of the differing curve point values into the writable curve's repeating-block registers (step 1 writable path).
Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of the adopt-curve request (curve index) — the register name is model-specific; for 7xx models the result point is AdptCrvRslt (named in 2.4.3).
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the update-curve-status / AdptCrvRslt point returning the success value.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the curve-1 block, register-for-register equal to the adopted source curve block.
Curve index ordering visible in the repeating-block read: writable curve indices precede read-only curve indices.
notes: The doc names the check as 'the update curve status' without giving the exact point name or the enumerated success value — a harness must resolve these from the specific 7xx model definition. Step 5 restates the loop condition rather than adding a distinct action. Step 6 is conditional ('If additional read-only curves are present').

section: 2.5.3 CRV-3 - Apply Settings Error (under 2.5 Curve Tests)
title: Apply Settings Error
purpose: Validates the behavior on an adopt-curve-settings error: the failure is reported and no partial change is made to the active curve.
applicability_reason: Curve models ARE served northbound — see CRV-1. This row fails on the same narrower fact as CRV-2: profile §3.1 item G3 is NOT IMPLEMENTED, the second (staging) curve is served wholly not-implemented and every write to it is refused before ACK, so an out-of-range adopt request cannot be issued to the DUT at all and there is no error to observe being reported (lexa-gw docs/conformance/PICS_SUNSPEC_MODBUS.md §2.8, §3.2; the write path is design Stage 5, docs/design/DESIGN_2026-07-28_1547-northbound-models.md §5, §9). This replaces a stale reason which said no curve model appears in any northbound class chain.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of an out-of-range curve index to the adopt-curve request register. / Modbus FC=0x03 read of the update-curve-status / AdptCrvRslt point returning the failure enumeration.
preconditions: The model contains curve functionality and is in the 7xx range.
The current state of all curve 1 settings is captured before the test so it can be compared afterwards.
Performed for each curve-based model (2.2). Label = CRV-3.<modelID>.
steps: 1. Perform an adopt curve request for a curve index that is out of range.
2. Verify that the update curve status indicates failure.
3. Verify that all curve 1 settings are in the same state as before performing the test.
expected: The device reports failure via the update curve status point after an out-of-range adopt-curve request.
Curve 1 settings are byte-for-byte unchanged from their pre-test state (no partial adoption).
observables: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of an out-of-range curve index to the adopt-curve request register.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the update-curve-status / AdptCrvRslt point returning the failure enumeration.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the full curve-1 block before and after, compared register-by-register for equality.
notes: The doc does not say whether the out-of-range adopt request itself must be accepted at the Modbus layer (write succeeds, status reports failure) or may be rejected with a Modbus exception. The step wording ('verify that the update curve status indicates failure') implies the write is accepted and the error is surfaced in the status point. The doc does not define 'out of range' numerically.

section: 2.3.1 DEV-1 - General Discovery (under 2.3 General Device Tests)
title: General Discovery
purpose: Validates SunSpec model organization and location within the device — i.e. that every model declared in the PICS is discoverable at a standard SunSpec base address behind the standard start marker, and that the model map is properly terminated.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 (Read Holding Registers) read of 2 registers at base address 0, 40000, or 50000 returning the two-register SunSpec start marker (marker value itself is not printed in this document). / Sequence of Modbus FC=0x03 reads walking the model chain: at each model header, 2 registers giving model ID and model length, then a skip of (length) registers to the next header.
preconditions: A device PICS (Excel workbook) exists declaring the SunSpec models and points supported by the implementation, including supported value ranges for each adjustable point (2.1 Test Inputs).
The DUT is reachable over at least one SunSpec Modbus interface (RTU and/or TCP).
Only SunSpec standardized models are considered during certification testing; vendor-specific models must not inhibit discovery/use of the standardized models (2.1).
General device tests are performed once for a device (2.2 Test Categories).
steps: 1. Verify that supported SunSpec models specified in the PICS can be found using the standard SunSpec discovery procedure.
2. Verify the SunSpec Modbus content is located at one of the SunSpec standard Modbus start addresses (0, 40000, or 50000) and begins with the two-register standard SunSpec Modbus start marker.
3. Verify that the SunSpec Modbus end model (ID 65535) is present with a length of 0.
expected: Every SunSpec model listed in the PICS is located by the standard SunSpec discovery walk.
The SunSpec model map base address is one of 0, 40000, or 50000.
The first two registers at the base address contain the standard SunSpec Modbus start marker.
An end model with model ID 65535 and length 0 terminates the model chain.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 (Read Holding Registers) read of 2 registers at base address 0, 40000, or 50000 returning the two-register SunSpec start marker (marker value itself is not printed in this document).
Sequence of Modbus FC=0x03 reads walking the model chain: at each model header, 2 registers giving model ID and model length, then a skip of (length) registers to the next header.
Final Modbus FC=0x03 read returning model ID = 65535 and length = 0.
Absence of Modbus exception responses during the discovery walk.
requirement_refs: SunSpec Device Information Model Specification (cited in Abstract as the requirement source)
notes: The document does not print the literal value of the 'two-register standard SunSpec Modbus start marker' — a harness must obtain it from the SunSpec Device Information Model Specification. Address 40000/50000 are given as 'standard Modbus start addresses' without stating whether they are 0-based protocol addresses or 4xxxx-style entity numbers; the doc lists 0, 40000, 50000 verbatim.

section: 2.3.2 DEV-2 - Model 1 Support (under 2.3 General Device Tests)
title: Model 1 Support
purpose: Validates that SunSpec Model 1 (the common model) is supported by the device and that its contents agree with the PICS.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 read of the model 1 header returning model ID = 1 and its declared length. / Modbus FC=0x03 read of the model 1 body registers; the decoded point values (e.g. manufacturer, model, serial number, Device Address) compared against the PICS.
preconditions: PICS declares the content of model 1.
DEV-1 discovery is available (model chain is walkable).
General device tests are performed once for a device (2.2).
steps: 1. Verify that SunSpec Modbus model 1 is present in the implementation and that the content contained in the model matches that declared in the PICS.
expected: Model ID 1 is present in the device model chain.
The point values / implemented points in model 1 match what the PICS declares.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 read of the model 1 header returning model ID = 1 and its declared length.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the model 1 body registers; the decoded point values (e.g. manufacturer, model, serial number, Device Address) compared against the PICS.
notes: The document does not enumerate model 1's individual points here; the point set comes from the model 1 definition and the PICS. Model 1 is also the location of the Device Address field exercised by RTU-5 (2.7.5).

section: 2.8.1 EXC-1 - Invalid Value (under 2.8 Exception Generation Tests)
title: Invalid Value
purpose: Verifies the device throws a Modbus exception when an invalid value is written to a point, and that the invalid write does not take effect.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the Modbus exception response PDU (FC|0x80 + exception byte) in the app-layer log; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06 or FC=0x10 write of an out-of-range / out-of-enumeration value to an RW point register. / Modbus exception response: function code with the high bit set (0x86 for FC 6, 0x90 for FC 16) and exception code byte = 0x02, 0x03, or 0x04.
preconditions: Each model implemented in the device has at least one RW point.
For enumerated points, the defined enumeration set is known (from the model definition / PICS) so a value outside it can be chosen.
The point's pre-write value is captured so 'was not written' can be proven.
steps: 1. For each model, write an invalid value to a RW point. For enum points, write a value outside of the defined enumerations.
2. Verify the device responds with an exception code of 2, 3 or 4.
3. Read the point to verify it was not written.
expected: The device returns a Modbus exception response with exception code 2 (Illegal Data Address), 3 (Illegal Data Value), or 4 (Slave Device Failure) — any of the three is a pass.
A subsequent read shows the point retains its pre-write value; the invalid value was NOT applied.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06 or FC=0x10 write of an out-of-range / out-of-enumeration value to an RW point register.
Modbus exception response: function code with the high bit set (0x86 for FC 6, 0x90 for FC 16) and exception code byte = 0x02, 0x03, or 0x04.
Modbus FC=0x03 read-back of the same register returning the original (pre-write) value.
requirement_refs: Modbus exception code 4 (Slave Device Failure / Server Device Failure)
notes: The doc accepts a set of exception codes {2,3,4} rather than mandating one — a harness must not assert a single code. The doc does not define 'invalid value' for non-enumerated points beyond 'invalid'; the PICS value ranges (2.1) are the practical source. This test is per-model ('For each model'), unlike the once-per-device protocol tests.

section: 2.8.2 EXC-2 - Writing a Read-Only Register (under 2.8 Exception Generation Tests)
title: Writing a Read-Only Register
purpose: Verifies the device throws a Modbus exception when a write request is sent to a read-only register, and that the read-only value is unchanged.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the Modbus exception response PDU (FC|0x80 + exception byte) in the app-layer log; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06 or FC=0x10 write requests targeting three or more read-only register addresses. / Modbus exception responses: function code 0x86 (for FC 6) or 0x90 (for FC 16) with exception code byte = 0x02, 0x03, or 0x04.
preconditions: At least three read-only registers are identifiable in the device's SunSpec map (from the model definitions / PICS).
The pre-write values of those registers are captured for comparison.
steps: 1. Identify three or more read-only registers and send a write request to change the values in them.
2. Verify the device responds with an exception code of 2, 3 or 4.
3. Read each point to verify it was not written in the previous step.
expected: Every write to a read-only register returns a Modbus exception with exception code 2, 3, or 4.
Each of the three-or-more read-only points retains its original value after the attempted write.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06 or FC=0x10 write requests targeting three or more read-only register addresses.
Modbus exception responses: function code 0x86 (for FC 6) or 0x90 (for FC 16) with exception code byte = 0x02, 0x03, or 0x04.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of each targeted register returning the pre-write value.
notes: Same {2,3,4} acceptance set as EXC-1. This test provides the concrete pass criterion referenced implicitly by CRV-1 step 3 ('points associated with curve 1 cannot be written'). The doc does not say the three registers must be in different models.

section: 2.8.3 EXC-3 - Illegal Function Code (under 2.8 Exception Generation Tests)
title: Illegal Function Code
purpose: Verifies the device correctly throws Modbus Exception 1 (Illegal Function) when it receives a function code that does not exist in the Modbus specification.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the Modbus exception response PDU (FC|0x80 + exception byte) in the app-layer log; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus request ADU carrying an undefined function code, e.g. FC=50 (0x32), addressed at an implemented RW register. / Modbus exception response with function code = request FC | 0x80 (e.g. 0xB2 for FC 50) and exception code byte = 0x01.
preconditions: An RW register implemented in the device is identified as the request target.
The test client can emit an arbitrary/undefined Modbus function code (e.g. 50).
steps: 1. Select a RW register implemented in the device and send a request with a function code that doesn't exist in the Modbus specification (e.g., 50).
2. Verify the device responds with Modbus Exception 1.
expected: The device returns a Modbus exception response with exception code 1 (Illegal Function).
Exactly exception code 1 — unlike EXC-1/EXC-2, no alternative codes are accepted here.
observables: Modbus request ADU carrying an undefined function code, e.g. FC=50 (0x32), addressed at an implemented RW register.
Modbus exception response with function code = request FC | 0x80 (e.g. 0xB2 for FC 50) and exception code byte = 0x01.
On TCP: the exception response echoes the request Transaction ID; on RTU: valid CRC and matching Unit ID.
notes: The doc names function code 50 only as an example ('e.g., 50'); any code absent from the Modbus specification qualifies. This is the one exception test with a single mandated code (1), in contrast to EXC-1 and EXC-2 which accept 2, 3, or 4. The doc does not say what the DUT should do with function codes that exist in Modbus but are unsupported by the device (that case would normally also be exception 1, but the doc is silent).

section: 2.7.9 MB-1 - Modbus Single/Multiple Register Write (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / General Modbus Tests)
title: Modbus Single/Multiple Register Write
purpose: Validates the device under test can perform multiple write (Function Code 16) and single write (Function Code 06) operations.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x10 request spanning >= 2 consecutive registers at the selected RW point offsets; normal response echoing starting address and quantity. / Modbus FC=0x03 read-back of those registers returning the FC 16 written values.
preconditions: At least two consecutive read-write (RW) points exist in the device's SunSpec map.
The new values to be written differ from the current values so success is observable.
This is a 'General Modbus Test' — it applies to both RTU and TCP interfaces (it sits under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests after both the RTU and TCP subsections).
steps: 1. Select two consecutive RW points to be written.
2. Send a multiple write request using function code 16 to write the new values to the points.
3. Verify both the points are written successfully.
4. Send a single write request using function code 6 on the two points one by one.
5. Verify the points are written successfully.
expected: A Function Code 16 (0x10, Write Multiple Registers) request covering both consecutive RW points is accepted (no exception).
Read-back confirms both points hold the values written by the FC 16 request.
Two separate Function Code 6 (0x06, Write Single Register) requests — one per point — are each accepted (no exception).
Read-back confirms both points hold the values written by the FC 6 requests.
observables: Modbus FC=0x10 request spanning >= 2 consecutive registers at the selected RW point offsets; normal response echoing starting address and quantity.
Modbus FC=0x03 read-back of those registers returning the FC 16 written values.
Two Modbus FC=0x06 requests, each to one register address, each returning a normal response echoing the address and the written value.
Modbus FC=0x03 read-back returning the FC 6 written values.
No exception responses (no function code with the 0x80 bit set).
requirement_refs: Modbus Function Code 16 (0x10) Write Multiple Registers
Modbus Function Code 06 (0x06) Write Single Register
notes: Single register write test added in v1.2 per the Revision History. Step 4 says FC 6 is applied 'on the two points one by one' — implying each of the two points must be a single 16-bit register (a 32-bit point cannot be written with FC 6). The doc does not say the read-back must be immediate; note the v1.3 removal of the 1000 ms read-after-write allowance applies to Section 2.4.3 specifically, but the same strictness is the safe assumption here.

section: 2.7.10 MB-2 - Modbus Single Register Read (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / General Modbus Tests)
title: Modbus Single Register Read
purpose: Validates the device under test can perform single register reads, which are allowed in function code 3.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 request with quantity field = 0x0001 at the chosen register address; normal response with byte count = 2 and the register value. / Repeated for three distinct addresses.
preconditions: The device's Modbus map is known (from discovery / PICS) so registers inside the map can be selected.
Three distinct registers within the map are available for reading.
This is a 'General Modbus Test' — it applies to both RTU and TCP interfaces.
steps: 1. Select a register within the modbus map of the device under test.
2. Perform a single register read using function code 3 and register count 1.
3. Verify the register has been read correctly.
4. Repeat steps 1-3 for two other registers.
expected: A Function Code 3 request with quantity = 1 returns a normal response containing that register's value.
The returned value matches the register's known/expected content.
The behavior holds for three distinct registers in total.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 request with quantity field = 0x0001 at the chosen register address; normal response with byte count = 2 and the register value.
Repeated for three distinct addresses.
Where a device legitimately rejects the read, a Modbus exception response for that address — permitted only when the address is part of a value longer than 16 bits.
requirement_refs: Modbus Function Code 03 (0x03) Read Holding Registers
notes: IMPORTANT EXPLICIT CARVE-OUT printed in the doc: 'Some devices may reject a read of a register if it's a part of a value longer than 16 bits. This may be done to avoid reading a part of a value and getting incomplete information. This is not considered non-compliant. In such cases, a 16-bit value should be read.' So a harness must select 16-bit points for this test, or accept an exception when the target register is a fragment of a 32/64-bit or string point. Step 4 says 'Repeat steps 1-3' though the loop logically covers steps 1-3 for two more registers.

section: 2.4.1 MOD-1 - Model Implementation (under 2.4 General SunSpec Model Tests)
title: Model Implementation
purpose: Validates that a model specified in the PICS is present in the implementation, has the correct length, implements the mandatory points, matches the PICS point set, and returns in-range values on individual point reads.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 read of the 2-register model header returning (model ID, model length). / One Modbus FC=0x03 request per point, with register count equal to that point's register size (1 for 16-bit, 2 for 32-bit, N for strings), targeting the point's offset within the model.
preconditions: PICS declares the model, its implemented points, and (optionally) a value range per point.
This test is performed once for each SunSpec model implemented in the device (2.2, 2.4).
Test instance label = test name + '.' + model ID (e.g. MOD-1 for model 701 is labeled MOD-1.701).
steps: 1. Verify model is discovered and present using the standard SunSpec discovery procedure.
2. Verify model has the correct length for the contents.
3. Verify each SunSpec mandatory point (ID, Length) is implemented.
4. Verify the implemented points match the PICS.

5. Verify all points in the model can be read as a single point. Each value should be verified based on the expected value range. If a range for the point is specified in the PICS, the value should be validated against the range.
expected: The model is found by the standard SunSpec discovery procedure.
The model's declared length register equals the correct length for the model contents.
The mandatory points ID and Length are implemented.
The set of implemented points equals the set declared in the PICS (no missing, no unexpected).
Every point can be read individually (as a single point read).
Each read value falls inside the expected value range for its datatype, and inside the PICS-declared range where one is specified.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 read of the 2-register model header returning (model ID, model length).
One Modbus FC=0x03 request per point, with register count equal to that point's register size (1 for 16-bit, 2 for 32-bit, N for strings), targeting the point's offset within the model.
Decoded point values, checked against datatype range and PICS range.
No Modbus exception response for any implemented point read.
requirement_refs: Model-specific SunSpec information model specifications (per the Abstract)
notes: Step 5 says 'read as a single point' — this is a per-point read, distinct from MOD-2's whole-model read. Note the interaction with the MB-2 note on page 16: some devices legitimately reject a read of one register that is part of a value longer than 16 bits; MOD-1 step 5 reads whole points so that caveat should not trigger. 'should be verified' / 'should be validated' is SHOULD-language in the doc, but the surrounding framing ('must be performed') treats the test itself as mandatory.

section: 2.4.2 MOD-2 - Model Read (under 2.4 General SunSpec Model Tests)
title: Model Read
purpose: Validates that the whole model can be read in a single Modbus read operation (multiple reads permitted only when the model length exceeds the Modbus maximum read length).
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x03 request with quantity = model length (+2 for the header, if the harness includes the header) issued at the model's start address, returning a single non-exception response. / For >125-register models: a series of Modbus FC=0x03 requests each with quantity <= 125 covering the model contiguously.
preconditions: The model is present and discoverable (MOD-1 / DEV-1).
Performed once for each SunSpec model implemented in the device (2.2).
Test instance label = test name + '.' + model ID (e.g. MOD-2.701).
steps: 1. Verify the model can be read in a single read (or several reads if the length exceeds 125 registers) and that the values are in the specified range based on the datatype.
expected: A single Modbus read spanning the entire model returns successfully when the model length is <= 125 registers.
For models longer than 125 registers, the model is readable via several consecutive reads, each within the 125-register limit.
All values returned are within the range specified by their datatype.
observables: Modbus FC=0x03 request with quantity = model length (+2 for the header, if the harness includes the header) issued at the model's start address, returning a single non-exception response.
For >125-register models: a series of Modbus FC=0x03 requests each with quantity <= 125 covering the model contiguously.
Decoded values checked against datatype ranges.
requirement_refs: Modbus application protocol maximum read quantity of 125 registers (cited numerically in the step text)
notes: 125 registers is the only numeric limit the doc gives; it is stated as the threshold beyond which multiple reads are permitted. The doc does not say whether the single read must include the 2-register model header.

section: 2.4.3 MOD-3 - Point Write (under 2.4 General SunSpec Model Tests)
title: Point Write
purpose: Validates that all implemented adjustable points in the model can be written individually and as a group, that a subsequent read returns exactly the written value, and that any additional processing triggered by the write (e.g. updates to AdptCrvRslt) is complete at that time.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; the supported_groups / ec_point_formats extensions in the ClientHello and the named_curve in the ServerKeyExchange; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06 (Write Single Register) and/or FC=0x10 (Write Multiple Registers) to the adjustable point's register offset(s) within the model. / A group write: one Modbus FC=0x10 covering several adjustable points in one request.
preconditions: PICS specifies the value range for each adjustable point, and the supported enumeration values for each adjustable enumerated point.
The model is present and its adjustable points are writable per the PICS.
An automated methodology is available to perform the write/read sequence (required by step 2).
Performed once for each SunSpec model implemented in the device (2.2). Label = MOD-3.<modelID>.
steps: 1. Verify all implemented adjustable points can be written based on the value range specified in the PICS. The point must be written with the minimum value, maximum value, and three intermediate values. If an adjustable point has fewer possible values, all the possible values must be tested.

2. Verify all implemented adjustable points can be written and then read. An automated methodology must be used to perform the write and read sequence to accomplish these requirements and to model typical device-to-device communication.
3. For adjustable enumerated points, verify each supported value in the PICS can be written.
expected: Each adjustable point accepts a write of its PICS minimum value, its PICS maximum value, and three intermediate values (or all possible values if fewer than five exist).
Adjustable points can be written individually AND as a group (per the test description).
A read-back after each write returns exactly the value that was written.
Any additional processing associated with the write (e.g. updates to AdptCrvRslt) is complete by the time the read-back is performed.
Every enumeration value listed as supported in the PICS is accepted by a write to the corresponding enumerated point.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06 (Write Single Register) and/or FC=0x10 (Write Multiple Registers) to the adjustable point's register offset(s) within the model.
A group write: one Modbus FC=0x10 covering several adjustable points in one request.
Modbus FC=0x03 read-back of the same register(s) immediately after the write, returning the written value with no settling delay allowed.
For curve/adopt models, read-back of AdptCrvRslt showing the post-write result value.
No Modbus exception response for any in-range/enumerated-supported write.
requirement_refs: AdptCrvRslt (point name cited verbatim in the test description)
notes: IMPORTANT VERSION NUANCE: v1.2 added an allowable delay of 1000 ms on read after write; v1.3 REMOVED that allowance from Section 2.4.3 (see Revision History). So under v1.3/v1.4 the read-back must reflect the write with no specified grace period. Procedure numbering in the PDF is malformed: items 1 and 2 are top-level and item 3 is rendered nested under item 2; it is treated here as a third top-level step. Doc says 'alltthe' (typo for 'all the') in step 1. The prose mentions writing 'individually and as a group' but the numbered steps never spell out the group write explicitly.

section: 2.6.1 REV-1 - Reversion Timeout (under 2.6 Reversion Tests)
title: Reversion Timeout
purpose: Validates that the required set of reversion points is implemented for the reversion timer and that the reversion operation is performed when the timer expires.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; successive FC=0x03 reads of the *RvrtRem remaining-time readback showing the countdown and the post-timeout register state; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 writes setting the reversion points to new values. / Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write to the reversion timer register with the reversion time.
preconditions: The model implements at least one reversion timer; if reversion functionality is not implemented in a model, the reversion tests are not performed (2.6).
PICS specifies which reversion timer(s) and reversion points are implemented.
Reversion tests are performed for each reversion timer implemented in models contained in the device (2.2). Label = REV-1.<modelID>, e.g. REV-1.705.
Current settings of the reversion points are known so 'different than current settings' values can be chosen.
steps: For each set of points in the model that support reversion:
1. Verify all reversion points are implemented for the reversion timer specified in the PICS.
2. Set the points to values that are different than current settings.
3. Set the reversion timer.

4. Verify the reversion time remaining point is updated and is within two seconds of the remaining reversion time as the reversion timer counts down. Check at least three times during countdown duration.
5. Verify the reversion timer times out and the timeout is within 2 seconds of the reversion time setting.
6. Verify the reversion settings are applied on reversion timeout.
expected: Every reversion point declared in the PICS for that timer is present in the model.
The reversion time remaining point decrements and tracks the true remaining time within a +/- 2 second tolerance, verified on at least three separate samples during the countdown.
The timer expires at the configured reversion time within a +/- 2 second tolerance.
On timeout, the reversion settings (not the temporarily written values) are the values in effect.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 writes setting the reversion points to new values.
Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write to the reversion timer register with the reversion time.
At least three Modbus FC=0x03 polls of the reversion-time-remaining register during the countdown, each compared against wall-clock elapsed time with a 2 s tolerance.
Modbus FC=0x03 read after expiry showing the reversion time remaining at 0 / timer expired, timestamped within 2 s of the configured reversion time.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the controlled points after expiry showing the reversion values in effect.
requirement_refs: SunSpec information model specifications defining reversion timers (7xx-series and others)
notes: The doc does not name the reversion timer register or the reversion-time-remaining point — these are model-specific and must come from the model definition / PICS. Note 'Some models may define more than one reversion timer, but an implementation may choose to implement any specific reversion timer independently from other reversion timers in the same model' — so the harness must iterate per implemented timer, not per model. Tolerance is stated as 'two seconds' in step 4 and '2 seconds' in step 5 (same value).

section: 2.6.2 REV-2 - Reversion Time Update (under 2.6 Reversion Tests)
title: Reversion Time Update
purpose: Validates the ability to update (extend) the reversion timer value while the reversion timer is running, and that the original timeout no longer fires once the time is rewritten.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; successive FC=0x03 reads of the *RvrtRem remaining-time readback showing the countdown and the post-timeout register state; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 writes to the reversion points and to the reversion timer register. / Modbus FC=0x03 polls of the reversion-time-remaining register before and after the rewrite, compared against wall clock with 2 s tolerance.
preconditions: The model implements a reversion timer (else the test is not performed).
Reversion tests are performed for each reversion timer implemented (2.2). Label = REV-2.<modelID>.
A reversion time long enough to allow a mid-countdown rewrite and three repeats.
steps: For each set of points in the model that support reversion:
1. Set the reversion points to values that are different than current settings.
2. Set the reversion timer.
3. Verify the reversion time remaining point is updated and is within two seconds of the remaining reversion time as the reversion timer counts down.
4. After at least half of the reversion time has elapsed, rewrite the reversion time register to the full reversion time value.
5. Verify the reversion time remaining point is updated and is within two seconds of the remaining reversion time based on the updated reversion time and elapsed time since the update.
6. Allow the test to run longer than the original reversion timeout period.
7. Verify the reversion timer is still running based on the time update.
8. Verify the reversion settings are not applied on original reversion timeout period.
9. Repeat steps 4 - 8 at least two more times and verify that each test pass is successful.
expected: The reversion time remaining point tracks the countdown within +/- 2 seconds before the update.

Rewriting the reversion time register mid-countdown restarts/extends the countdown; the remaining-time point thereafter tracks the updated reversion time minus elapsed-since-update, within +/- 2 seconds.
The timer is still running after the original timeout instant has passed.
The reversion settings are NOT applied at the original reversion timeout instant.
The extend-and-verify cycle (steps 4-8) succeeds on at least three total passes.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 writes to the reversion points and to the reversion timer register.
Modbus FC=0x03 polls of the reversion-time-remaining register before and after the rewrite, compared against wall clock with 2 s tolerance.
A second (and third, fourth) Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of the full reversion time value occurring after >= 50% of the reversion time has elapsed.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the controlled points taken after the original timeout instant showing the written (non-reversion) values still in effect.
Modbus FC=0x03 read showing reversion time remaining > 0 after the original timeout instant.
requirement_refs: SunSpec information model specifications defining reversion timers
notes: Step 9 says repeat steps 4-8 'at least two more times', i.e. three extension cycles minimum. Unlike REV-1, REV-2 has no step that verifies the reversion points are implemented — it presumes REV-1 passed. The doc does not state whether the rewrite must be the same value or may be any value; it says 'the full reversion time value'.

section: 2.6.3 REV-3 - Reversion Cancel (under 2.6 Reversion Tests)
title: Reversion Cancel
purpose: Validates that writing 0 to the reversion time cancels the running reversion timer so that reversion settings are never applied.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; successive FC=0x03 reads of the *RvrtRem remaining-time readback showing the countdown and the post-timeout register state; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of value 0 to the reversion time register, issued after >= 50% of the reversion time has elapsed. / Modbus FC=0x03 read of the reversion-time-remaining register returning 0 after the cancel write.
preconditions: The model implements a reversion timer (else the test is not performed).
Reversion tests are performed for each reversion timer implemented (2.2). Label = REV-3.<modelID>.
steps: For each set of points in the model that support reversion:
1. Set the reversion points to values that are different than current settings.
2. Set the reversion timer.
3. Verify the reversion time remaining point is updated and is within two seconds of the remaining reversion time as the reversion timer counts down.
4. After at least half of the reversion time has elapsed, set the reversion time to 0.
5. Verify the reversion time remaining point is updated to 0.
6. Allow the test to run longer than the original reversion timeout period.
7. Verify the reversion settings are not applied on original reversion timeout period.
expected: The reversion time remaining point tracks the countdown within +/- 2 seconds before the cancel.
Writing 0 to the reversion time causes the reversion time remaining point to read 0.
After the original timeout instant has passed, the reversion settings have NOT been applied; the written values remain in effect.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of value 0 to the reversion time register, issued after >= 50% of the reversion time has elapsed.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the reversion-time-remaining register returning 0 after the cancel write.
Modbus FC=0x03 read of the controlled points taken after the original timeout instant showing the written (non-reversion) values still in effect.
requirement_refs: SunSpec information model specifications defining reversion timers
notes: Title and description conflict slightly: the section heading is 'Reversion Cancel' but the description text reads 'This test validates the timeout behavior of the reversion timer' — apparently copy-paste residue from REV-1. The procedure is unambiguously a cancel test. Steps 1-3 and 6-7 are identical in wording to REV-2.

section: 2.7.1 RTU-1 - RTU Interface (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus RTU)
title: RTU Interface
purpose: Validates the support of a Modbus RTU interface by running the entire conformance suite over that interface.
applicability_reason: No northbound serial server exists. RS-485 (bus://, /dev/lexa/rs485-1) is a SOUTHBOUND CLIENT transport only (facts-dut-capability.md §2.1).
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Serial-line capture of Modbus RTU ADUs: [Unit ID][Function Code][Data][CRC16], with no MBAP header. / Correct CRC on every response frame; inter-frame silence delimiting.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus RTU interface (the RTU tests are only for devices supporting one).
Modbus protocol tests are performed once for a device (2.2).
This test can be run concurrently with other required conformance tests.
steps: 1. Perform all the conformance tests over the Modbus RTU interface.
expected: Every conformance test in this document passes when the transport is Modbus RTU.
observables: Serial-line capture of Modbus RTU ADUs: [Unit ID][Function Code][Data][CRC16], with no MBAP header.
Correct CRC on every response frame; inter-frame silence delimiting.
Successful responses for all of DEV-1/2, MOD-1/2/3, CRV-*, REV-*, MB-1/2 and correct exception responses for EXC-1/2/3, all carried over RTU.
notes: This is a meta-test — it has no assertions of its own beyond 'the whole suite passes on this transport'. For the lexa-gw DUT (SunSpec Modbus TCP server) this test is NOT APPLICABLE unless an RTU interface is also exposed. Recorded here for completeness of the shard.

section: 2.7.2 RTU-2 - Baud Rate (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus RTU)
title: Baud Rate
purpose: Validates each of the additional supported baud rates for the Modbus RTU interface.
applicability_reason: No northbound serial server exists; baud rates apply to the southbound RS-485 client only (facts-dut-capability.md §2.1).
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Serial capture at each configured line rate showing well-formed Modbus RTU ADUs with valid CRC16 and no framing errors. / Successful (non-exception) Modbus responses for the three chosen test cases at each baud rate.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus RTU interface.
The set of supported baud rates is known (declared by the vendor / PICS).
A means exists to change the DUT's baud rate and to match it on the test client.
steps: 1. Perform at least three of the specified conformance test cases for each supported baudrate.
expected: For every supported baud rate, at least three conformance test cases from this document execute and pass over Modbus RTU at that baud rate.
observables: Serial capture at each configured line rate showing well-formed Modbus RTU ADUs with valid CRC16 and no framing errors.
Successful (non-exception) Modbus responses for the three chosen test cases at each baud rate.
notes: The PDF renders this section with the '1.' step number run into the description sentence ('...for the Modbus RTU interface.1.  Perform at least three...'), and there is no separate '2.7.2.1 Procedure' heading as every other test has. The doc does NOT enumerate which baud rates are required or which three test cases to pick — both are left to the tester. NOT APPLICABLE to a TCP-only DUT.

section: 2.7.3 RTU-3 - Partial Request (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus RTU)
title: Partial Request
purpose: Validates that a device can recover from an incomplete Modbus request message and ignore it.
applicability_reason: No northbound Modbus RTU listener (facts-dut-capability.md §2.1, §7).
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Serial capture: a truncated RTU ADU (fewer bytes than the function code implies, or missing/invalid CRC) with NO response frame from the DUT. / Serial capture: a following complete RTU ADU (e.g. FC=0x03) receiving a normal, CRC-valid response with the correct Unit ID and function code.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus RTU interface.
A test client able to emit a deliberately truncated RTU frame.
steps: 1. Send an incomplete partial Modbus request.
2. Send a different complete Modbus request.
3. Verify the successful response to the second Modbus request.
expected: The device ignores the truncated/incomplete request (it does not respond to it and does not lock up or desynchronize).
The subsequent complete, well-formed request receives a successful (non-exception) Modbus response.
observables: Serial capture: a truncated RTU ADU (fewer bytes than the function code implies, or missing/invalid CRC) with NO response frame from the DUT.
Serial capture: a following complete RTU ADU (e.g. FC=0x03) receiving a normal, CRC-valid response with the correct Unit ID and function code.
requirement_refs: Modbus standard framing / inter-frame timeout behavior
notes: Compared to TCP-2 (2.7.7), RTU-3's description explicitly adds 'and ignore it'; the numbered steps are otherwise word-for-word identical. The doc does not define how incomplete the partial request must be, nor how long to wait before sending the second request (the RTU inter-frame timeout governs). NOT APPLICABLE to a TCP-only DUT.

section: 2.7.4 RTU-4 - Broadcast Test (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus RTU)
title: Broadcast Test
purpose: Verifies the broadcast functionality works on the device as described in the Modbus standard: a write to Unit ID 0 is acted on but not answered.
applicability_reason: No northbound RTU listener; additionally unit-ID 0 is reserved as broadcast and never allocated (facts-dut-capability.md §1.4, unitmap.go:45-51).
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Serial capture: an RTU ADU with Unit ID (address byte) = 0x00 carrying a write function code (FC=0x06 or FC=0x10), followed by silence from the DUT. / Serial capture: a following addressed Modbus FC=0x03 read (Unit ID = the device's configured address) returning the broadcast-written value.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus RTU interface.
A writable (RW) point is identified whose value can be changed and read back.
The write value differs from the point's current value so the update is detectable.
steps: 1. Send a write request from the testing client to the SunSpec Server with a Unit ID set to 0.
2. Confirm the device does not respond to the request.
3. Read the point in the device to verify the point has been updated with the 'write' value from step 1.
expected: No Modbus response frame of any kind (neither normal nor exception) is emitted for the Unit ID 0 broadcast write.
The targeted point's value HAS been updated to the broadcast write value, confirmed by a subsequent addressed read.
observables: Serial capture: an RTU ADU with Unit ID (address byte) = 0x00 carrying a write function code (FC=0x06 or FC=0x10), followed by silence from the DUT.
Serial capture: a following addressed Modbus FC=0x03 read (Unit ID = the device's configured address) returning the broadcast-written value.
requirement_refs: Modbus standard broadcast semantics (Unit ID / slave address 0, no response)
notes: Added in v1.2 per the Revision History. This is an RTU-section test; broadcast has no defined meaning on Modbus TCP, so it is NOT APPLICABLE to a TCP-only DUT. The doc does not state a wait time for step 2 before declaring 'no response'.

section: 2.7.5 RTU-5 - Device Address Write (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus RTU)
title: Device Address Write
purpose: Verifies the device has the capability to change the device address / Unit ID to any value between 1 and 247, that it responds only on the configured address, and that address 0 is rejected as a device address.
applicability_reason: No northbound RTU listener, and the Model 1 Device Address point cannot be written: internal/writes/decode.go:19-24 refuses any write to a Model 1 point even for a 'rw *' SuperAdmin grant (facts-dut-capability.md §1.3).
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write to the Device Address register inside SunSpec Model 1, five times with distinct values in 1..247. / Serial capture: Modbus FC=0x03 read and FC=0x06/0x10 write ADUs carrying the new address byte, each receiving a matching response with that same address byte.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus RTU interface.
SunSpec Model 1 is implemented and exposes the Device Address field (see DEV-2).
The test client can retarget its Unit ID after each address change.
steps: 1. Write five different values between 1 and 247 to the Device Address in Model 1. For each value, read and write at least 1 SunSpec register using the updated Unit ID (Device Address).
2. Verify for each of the 5 Device Addresses in Step 1, the device does not respond to either read or write requests for 3 other Unit ID values.
3. Verify the device rejects writing zero to the Device Address field.
expected: All five Device Address values in the range 1..247 are accepted by a write to the Model 1 Device Address point.
After each address change, at least one SunSpec register read AND one write succeed when addressed with the new Unit ID.
For each configured address, requests sent to 3 other (non-matching) Unit ID values receive no response — neither reads nor writes.
A write of 0 to the Device Address field is rejected by the device.
observables: Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write to the Device Address register inside SunSpec Model 1, five times with distinct values in 1..247.
Serial capture: Modbus FC=0x03 read and FC=0x06/0x10 write ADUs carrying the new address byte, each receiving a matching response with that same address byte.
Serial capture: ADUs carrying 3 non-matching Unit ID values, each followed by silence from the DUT.
Modbus FC=0x06/0x10 write of value 0 to the Device Address register followed by a rejection — either a Modbus exception response or an unchanged value on read-back.
requirement_refs: Modbus standard address range 1-247 for slave/unit addresses
notes: Added in v1.2 per the Revision History. The doc says 'the device does not response' (typo for 'respond'). It does not specify HOW the zero-write must be rejected (Modbus exception vs. silently not applied) — treat either as a pass unless a profile narrows it. NOT APPLICABLE to a TCP-only DUT, although the Model 1 Device Address point exists on TCP devices too.

section: 2.7.6 TCP-1 - TCP Interface (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus TCP)
title: TCP Interface
purpose: Validates the support of a Modbus TCP interface by running the entire conformance suite over that interface.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §7 (secure-sunspec-modbus-traceability.md:157-159): 'lexa-gw uses [secure 802 + plain 502 coexistence] southbound as a client; its own northbound Modbus is mbaps-only (there is no plain northbound listener)'. A run of the whole suite over plain Modbus/TCP has no listener to talk to.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: TCP three-way handshake to the Modbus listener (the doc does not state the port; Modbus TCP default is 502). / Modbus TCP ADUs with MBAP header: [Transaction ID (2)][Protocol ID = 0x0000 (2)][Length (2)][Unit ID (1)][Function Code][Data], no CRC.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus TCP interface (the TCP tests are only for devices supporting one).
Modbus protocol tests are performed once for a device (2.2).
A TCP connection can be established to the DUT's Modbus listener.
steps: 1. Perform all the conformance tests over the Modbus TCP interface.
expected: Every conformance test in this document passes when the transport is Modbus TCP.
observables: TCP three-way handshake to the Modbus listener (the doc does not state the port; Modbus TCP default is 502).
Modbus TCP ADUs with MBAP header: [Transaction ID (2)][Protocol ID = 0x0000 (2)][Length (2)][Unit ID (1)][Function Code][Data], no CRC.
Responses echoing the request Transaction ID and Unit ID.
Successful responses for DEV-1/2, MOD-1/2/3, CRV-*, REV-*, MB-1/2 and correct exception responses for EXC-1/2/3, all carried over TCP.
notes: This is the primary applicability anchor for the lexa-gw DUT (SunSpec Modbus TCP server). It is a meta-test with no independent assertions — it makes every other test in this document in-scope over TCP. The doc does not state the TCP port number, does not mention TLS, and does not mention concurrent-connection limits.

section: 2.7.7 TCP-2 - Partial Request (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus TCP)
title: Partial Request
purpose: Validates that a device can recover from an incomplete Modbus request message received over TCP.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set. Framing manipulation must be done inside the TLS session (split the PDU across two TLS records / two TCP segments), which the stock bench client cannot yet do.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: pcap: a TCP segment carrying fewer bytes than the MBAP Length field declares (truncated PDU) with no Modbus response for that Transaction ID. / pcap: a following complete Modbus TCP ADU (e.g. FC=0x03) receiving a normal response echoing its Transaction ID and Unit ID.
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus TCP interface.
A test client able to emit a deliberately truncated Modbus TCP ADU on an established connection.
steps: 1. Send an incomplete partial Modbus request.
2. Send a different complete Modbus request.
3. Verify the successful response to the second Modbus request.
expected: The device recovers from the incomplete request (it does not hang, does not mis-parse the following request).
The subsequent complete, well-formed request receives a successful (non-exception) Modbus response.
observables: pcap: a TCP segment carrying fewer bytes than the MBAP Length field declares (truncated PDU) with no Modbus response for that Transaction ID.
pcap: a following complete Modbus TCP ADU (e.g. FC=0x03) receiving a normal response echoing its Transaction ID and Unit ID.
The TCP connection state after the partial request — the doc does not say whether the device may reset the connection, so record whether a RST/FIN occurs.
notes: Unlike RTU-3, the TCP-2 description omits 'and ignore it' — it only requires recovery. Critically, the doc does not state whether the second request may be sent on the SAME TCP connection or a new one, nor whether the DUT is permitted to close the connection after the partial request. A harness should test the same-connection case and record connection-close behavior as an observation rather than a failure.

section: 2.7.8 TCP-3 - Multiple TCP Packets (under 2.7 Modbus Protocol Tests / Modbus TCP)
title: Multiple TCP Packets
purpose: Validates that a device can support a Modbus request that is divided across multiple TCP frames (i.e. the server reassembles a TCP stream rather than assuming one segment = one PDU).
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.4: the gateway projects one contiguous SunSpec chain per admitted device at base 40000 — 'SunS' marker, Model 1 (66-register data block), the class models (inverter 701/702/704, battery 701/702/704/713/714-hdr, meter 701) and the [0xFFFF,0x0000] end marker — with FC 0x03/0x04 reads and FC 0x06/0x10 writes and the full exception ladder of §1.3. NOTE the transport deviation: there is no plain northbound listener (§7), so this procedure runs over mbaps/TLS on :802 rather than plain :502 and the PICS must declare the v1 northbound model set. Framing manipulation must be done inside the TLS session (split the PDU across two TLS records / two TCP segments), which the stock bench client cannot yet do.
evidence: harness-side Modbus PDU log in SS-MODBUS-RESULTS RPT-LOG-8 form (ascii-hex MBAP+PDU, `conn`/`disc` entries with ipaddr/ipport) taken at the application layer of the mbaps session, plus a `tcp port 802` pcap binding those PDUs to a real TLS session on the wire; source observables to assert verbatim: pcap: two TCP data segments on the same connection whose concatenated payload forms exactly one Modbus TCP ADU (MBAP header possibly split across the segment boundary). / pcap: one Modbus response with the matching Transaction ID and no exception bit set (function code returned without the 0x80 high bit).
preconditions: The device supports a Modbus TCP interface.
A test client able to split a single Modbus TCP ADU across two TCP segments (e.g. by disabling Nagle / issuing two writes with a flush between).
steps: 1. Send a Modbus TCP request that is broken across two TCP frames.
2. Verify the successful response to the Modbus TCP request.
expected: The device reassembles the two TCP segments into one Modbus request.
A single successful (non-exception) Modbus response is returned for that request, echoing its Transaction ID.
observables: pcap: two TCP data segments on the same connection whose concatenated payload forms exactly one Modbus TCP ADU (MBAP header possibly split across the segment boundary).
pcap: one Modbus response with the matching Transaction ID and no exception bit set (function code returned without the 0x80 high bit).
Absence of a TCP RST or a malformed-frame exception after the split request.
requirement_refs: Modbus TCP (MBAP) framing / TCP stream reassembly
notes: The doc does not specify WHERE the split must occur (mid-MBAP-header vs. mid-PDU) — splitting inside the 7-byte MBAP header is the stricter case and is the one most likely to break naive implementations. It also does not specify a delay between the two segments.

section: 2.1 Equipment Version (under 2 General Testing Considerations)
title: Equipment version must not change during the testing process
purpose: Proves that the whole TRR describes a single, frozen software/hardware build, so the certificate can be bound to exactly one version.
applicability_reason: Report-format requirement on the CONFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION TOOL rather than on the DUT. It is satisfiable today: facts-dut-capability.md §5 shows the estate already emits verdict artifacts (sim/ssm-conformance's CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md section, gw-mayhem's JSON verdict board, cmd/dashboard's /api/gw/qa/report), and the harness owns one end of every TLS session so it can log the exchange in unencrypted form; the missing piece is the emitter itself (facts-dut-capability.md §8.4: 'Evidence-capture is the real gap'). The tool can auto-fill this from the board (image hash, /etc/os-release, configs) over ssh, but an operator must confirm the declared identity/version freeze.
evidence: the emitted TRR artifacts themselves: the Summary Test Results CSV (key,value rows incl. `Test <ID>,PASS`) and the Detailed Test Log JSON objects, plus the raw pcap files they reference; source observables to assert verbatim: TRR Summary Test Results CSV: a single 'Software Version <n (Software)>' and a single 'Software Checksum <n (Software)>' value covering every 'Test <Test ID>' row / No mid-run firmware/OTA transaction in the detailed test logs
preconditions: A DUT (DER device / SunSpec Certified Software) is assembled at a known software and hardware version
Software Name/Version/Checksum and Hardware Manufacturer/Model are recorded before test start (see RPT-KV-14..16, RPT-KV-25..26)
steps: 1. Record the software and hardware version of the equipment before starting the test procedures.
2. Run all SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures without altering the software or hardware during the testing process.
3. If any change is made to the software or hardware at any point, discard the run and restart the entire testing process.
expected: All tests are completed without altering the software or hardware during the testing process.
If any changes are made to the software or hardware, the testing process must be restarted (partial re-run is not permitted).
observables: TRR Summary Test Results CSV: a single 'Software Version <n (Software)>' and a single 'Software Checksum <n (Software)>' value covering every 'Test <Test ID>' row
No mid-run firmware/OTA transaction in the detailed test logs
Test Completion Date single value in the Summary Test Results
notes: Normative 'must'. Phrased as a process constraint on the lab, not a wire-observable device behavior; the automated harness can enforce it by hashing the DUT image before and after the run and refusing to emit a TRR if the checksum changed.
