section: 4 Detailed Test Logs
title: Detailed test logs must contain all Modbus messages exchanged for each test, plus TCP connection info
purpose: Proves each PASS verdict is backed by primary evidence — the complete on-the-wire exchange SunSpec can independently re-adjudicate.
applicability_reason: Report-format requirement on the CONFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION TOOL rather than on the DUT. It is satisfiable today: facts-dut-capability.md §5 shows the estate already emits verdict artifacts (sim/ssm-conformance's CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md section, gw-mayhem's JSON verdict board, cmd/dashboard's /api/gw/qa/report), and the harness owns one end of every TLS session so it can log the exchange in unencrypted form; the missing piece is the emitter itself (facts-dut-capability.md §8.4: 'Evidence-capture is the real gap'). Decryption is not needed: the harness terminates the peer end of every session (gridsim for CSIP, the aggregator/ssm-conformance client for mbaps), so it can serialise the HTTP/Modbus messages in the clear at the application layer.
evidence: the emitted TRR artifacts themselves: the Summary Test Results CSV (key,value rows incl. `Test <ID>,PASS`) and the Detailed Test Log JSON objects, plus the raw pcap files they reference; source observables to assert verbatim: JSON file(s) containing 'req'/'resp' log entries whose 'msg' hex strings reconstruct the full Modbus PDU exchange / 'conn' and 'disc' entries bracketing each Modbus TCP session (default port 502)
preconditions: The test tool captured every Modbus request and response exchanged with the DUT during every test procedure
For Modbus TCP implementations, connection establishment and termination events were captured
steps: 1. For each test performed, log all Modbus messages exchanged.
2. For implementations using Modbus TCP, additionally log connection information.
3. Supply the detailed test logs in a single document or in multiple documents, in the format of §4.1.1-§4.1.3.
expected: The detailed test logs consist of a log of ALL Modbus messages exchanged for each of the tests performed.
For implementations using Modbus TCP, connection information is also logged.
The logs must contain all Modbus messages that were transferred as part of the test (none omitted).
The logs must contain connection information for Modbus TCP implementations.
The detailed test logs may be supplied in a single document or multiple documents.
observables: JSON file(s) containing 'req'/'resp' log entries whose 'msg' hex strings reconstruct the full Modbus PDU exchange
'conn' and 'disc' entries bracketing each Modbus TCP session (default port 502)
notes: 'must contain all Modbus messages' is normative and absolute — a harness that filters or de-duplicates traffic would be non-conformant. Connection info is conditionally required (Modbus TCP only); Modbus RTU logs carry no ipaddr/ipport.

preconditions: Modbus traffic was captured, possibly over a secured/encrypted transport
steps: 1. Capture the Modbus messages transferred as part of the test.
2. If any transport-layer encryption was in use, decrypt so the archived log contains plaintext Modbus PDUs.

title: 'time' element semantics and required accuracy

preconditions: The capture tool has a clock with at least second accuracy
steps: 1. For every log entry, record a 'time' element.
2. Express it as a NUMBER containing a value in seconds representing the timing of the message.
3. Express sub-second timing using decimal notation.
expected: 'time' is a number containing a value in seconds that represents the timing of the message.

preconditions: A Modbus request or response was captured in full
steps: 1. Take the complete binary Modbus message content.
2. Convert the binary representation to ascii hex values.

section: 1 Overview
title: TLS with digital certificates is mandatory for all CSIP data connections
purpose: Establishes the premise for the whole test PKI: the CSIP specification mandates that TLS be used for all data connections in the system, and digital certificates are required to perform the CSIP 2030.5 Test Procedures and to participate in a CSIP-conforming system.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.2/§3.1: every product data path is TLS — mbaps :802 is mTLS-mandatory and the CSIP client uses mTLS with 0xC0AE; there is no plaintext data listener anywhere (the only non-TLS ports are loopback-bound metrics and the local MQTT bus, §6.2).

preconditions: DUT is intended to be exercised against the SunSpec CSIP Test Procedures.

2. Confirm the DUT presents/consumes digital certificates on those TLS connections (test certificates for the test procedures, production PKI certificates in the field).

Certificate / CertificateRequest handshake messages carrying the SunSpec test PKI chain

section: 2.1 Device Type
title: Separate client and server certificate package types with different intermediate CAs
purpose: Proves the DUT accepts/validates a chain whose intermediate differs from its own, by ensuring test server and test client use different intermediate certificates in their chains.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §6.3: the bench CA can mint a second intermediate, and the DUT validates a peer chain purely against its configured trust domain (nb-mbaps-clients / nb-csip-servers), which is independent of its own issuing intermediate — so a differing-intermediate peer is testable today.
evidence: the DUT's leaf and chain lifted out of the TLS Certificate handshake message in the pcap and dumped with `openssl x509 -text` (Subject, SAN, chain depth, issuer/AKI linkage), cross-checked against certmgr's inventory over the SO_PEERCRED socket; source observables to assert verbatim: TLS Certificate handshake message from the DUT contains the 'cli' or 'svr' chain; the peer's Certificate message contains the other type, with a different intermediate (MICA/MCA) certificate
preconditions: The DUT's role in the test (client or server) has been determined.
The test framework emulates the peer role (see PKI-7).
steps: 1. Select the certificate package type matching the DUT's role: client or server.
2. Ensure the test framework (peer) uses the opposite package type, so that server and client use different intermediate certificates in their certificate chains.
expected: Two certificate package types exist: client and server.
The intermediate certificates in the server chain differ from those in the client chain.
The DUT still validates the peer chain even though the peer's intermediate CA differs from its own.
observables: TLS Certificate handshake message from the DUT contains the 'cli' or 'svr' chain; the peer's Certificate message contains the other type, with a different intermediate (MICA/MCA) certificate
notes: Explicit nuance: "The IEEE 2030.5 specification does not make a distinction between certificates associated with client and server devices but the SunSpec test PKI uses this convention to ensure different certificate chains for clients and servers." So this is a SunSpec test-PKI convention, not an IEEE 2030.5 requirement. Wording is 'desirable for testing purposes' (SHOULD-strength).

section: 2.2 Manufacturer Model OID
title: Device certificate Subject empty; identity carried in X509v3 SubjectAltName otherName hwType/hwSerialNum
purpose: Proves the device certificate follows the IEEE 2030.5-2018 device identification profile: empty Subject, identity in the SubjectAltName as manufacturer model OID (hwType) plus device serial number (hwSerialNum).
applicability_reason: CODE: IMPLEMENTED — this corrects a stale reason which said no code in lexa-gw or the bench CA emits a HardwareModuleName SAN. lexa-gw's ProfileIEEE20305 CSR profile emits an EMPTY Subject (the zero pkix.Name, marshalling as the empty RDNSequence 30 00) with DNSNames/IPAddresses/URIs deliberately unset so crypto/x509 cannot emit a second SAN (internal/rotation/controller.go:214-220, :425-448), and identity is carried in a SubjectAltName otherName built by internal/hwmodule as the RFC 4108 HardwareModuleName structure — otherName type-id 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.4 (hwmodule.go:24), hwType 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.1.1 under LEXA's IANA PEN 50316 (:47, registry of record docs/OID_REGISTRY.md:25-27), hwSerialNum resolved from the provisioned serial and fail-closed if absent or invalid (:90-104; rotation.ErrIdentityInvalid), exactly one GeneralName by construction (:161-171, :211-223). preconditions: A device certificate has been issued by the SunSpec Test PKI for the DUT.

steps: 1. Inspect the issued device certificate.

expected: Subject field of the device certificate is empty.

observables: Certificate dump: empty Subject DN
Certificate dump: 'X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: othername: hwType=1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.13.1, hwSerialNum=1234'

section: 3 Using Test Certificates
title: Test environment topology: DUT configured with a single certificate chain, framework emulates the peer
purpose: Proves the DUT behaves in the test environment exactly as it would in production: one certificate chain provisioned and used throughout testing, with the test framework supplying the varying/peer conditions.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.2/§3.1: the DUT holds exactly one identity chain per surface, issued by certmgr and hot-reloadable, and never varies it during a run; all scenario variation happens on the framework side (the bench PKI fixtures of §5 already do exactly this).
evidence: the DUT's leaf and chain lifted out of the TLS Certificate handshake message in the pcap and dumped with `openssl x509 -text` (Subject, SAN, chain depth, issuer/AKI linkage), cross-checked against certmgr's inventory over the SO_PEERCRED socket; source observables to assert verbatim: Across all test connections the DUT's TLS Certificate message contains the same device certificate and chain / Framework-side Certificate messages vary chain length/validity across test cases
preconditions: A test certificate package has been obtained for the DUT (client or server type as appropriate).
The test framework has a full set of both server and client certificate packages installed (see PKI-12).
steps: 1. Configure the device under test with a single certificate chain that is used throughout testing.
2. Leave the additional certificates in the DUT's certificate package unused.
3. Configure the testing framework to emulate the functionality of the peer of the device under test.
4. Configure/update the testing framework with multiple certificate chains to create the security-related conditions specified in the test procedures.
expected: The device under test exhibits the same behavior as it would in a production environment.
The DUT uses exactly one certificate chain for the duration of testing.
Additional certificates in the DUT's certificate package are not used by the DUT.
The testing framework, not the DUT, is what varies chains to create the required security conditions.
observables: Across all test connections the DUT's TLS Certificate message contains the same device certificate and chain
Framework-side Certificate messages vary chain length/validity across test cases
notes: Harness design constraint rather than a pass/fail test. 'Each request for a device test certificate results in a package of multiple certificates.'

`openssl pkcs12 -in <file>.p12 -passin pass:password` succeeds

section: 3.1.2 Certificate Authorities
title: Certificate authority hierarchy: SERCA, MCA, MICA and the three valid device chains
purpose: Proves the DUT supports all IEEE 2030.5 CA types and validates device certificates issued at each of the three defined chain lengths.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §6.3: one root anchors the whole bench and scripts/bench-pki-bootstrap.sh drives issuance, so SERCA/MCA/MICA analogues and all three chain depths can be minted and presented to the DUT; the DUT's own validation path is mbed TLS chain verification against the configured trust domain.
evidence: the DUT's leaf and chain lifted out of the TLS Certificate handshake message in the pcap and dumped with `openssl x509 -text` (Subject, SAN, chain depth, issuer/AKI linkage), cross-checked against certmgr's inventory over the SO_PEERCRED socket; source observables to assert verbatim: TLS Certificate message chain depth of 1 (device only, SERCA-issued), 2 (device + MICA), or 3 (device + MICA + MCA) / Issuer DN of the MICA certificate equal to either the SERCA or the MCA subject DN
preconditions: Test certificate package unpacked, containing the three valid device certificates of different chain lengths.
SERCA (root) certificate installed as trust anchor on the DUT.
steps: 1. Identify the three IEEE 2030.5 certificate authority types in the package: Smart Energy Root CA (SERCA), Manufacturer CA (MCA), Manufacturer Issuing CA (MICA).
2. Confirm the MICA issues the device certificates associated with a manufacturer.
3. Confirm each MICA certificate is issued either by the SERCA or by an intermediate manufacturer CA (MCA).
4. Confirm each MCA certificate is issued by the SERCA.
5. Exercise the DUT with each of the three valid chains: serca-device, serca-mica-device, serca-mca-mica-device.
6. Confirm the CA certificates present in the package are: SERCA, MCA, MCA-signed MICA, and SERCA-signed MICA.
expected: Three certificate authority types are specified by IEEE 2030.5: Smart Energy Root CA (SERCA), Manufacturer CA (MCA), Manufacturer Issuing CA (MICA).
A MICA issues the device certificates associated with a manufacturer.
A MICA certificate can be issued by the SERCA or by an intermediate manufacturer CA (MCA).
A MCA certificate is always issued by the SERCA.
The SERCA can also issue a device certificate, but this is not standard practice.
The three valid certificate chains are: serca-device, serca-mica-device, and serca-mca-mica-device.
The certificate authority certificates consist of the SERCA, MCA, MCA-signed MICA, and SERCA-signed MICA.
observables: TLS Certificate message chain depth of 1 (device only, SERCA-issued), 2 (device + MICA), or 3 (device + MICA + MCA)
Issuer DN of the MICA certificate equal to either the SERCA or the MCA subject DN
Issuer DN of the MCA certificate always equal to the SERCA subject DN
notes: 'A MCA certificate is always issued by the SERCA' is absolute; SERCA-issued device certs are permitted but 'not standard practice'. The three-valid-certificate set in the package corresponds 1:1 to these three chains.

section: 2.5.1 CRYP-001 - Mandatory TLS v1.2 Cipher Suites [C, S] (under 2.5 Cryptography (CRYP) Tests)
title: CRYP-001 - Mandatory TLS v1.2 Cipher Suites [C, S]
purpose: Verifies that the EUT supports the specific mandatory cipher suites required for TLS v1.2 interoperability.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives. The procedure has both an EUT-S and an EUT-C half; lexa-gw can supply both (northbound :802 server and southbound mbaps client).
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; source observables to assert verbatim: Three separate TLS 1.2 handshakes on TCP port 802, each ClientHello carrying exactly one cipher suite / ServerHello cipher_suite = TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 in iteration 1; verdict row citing SunSpecTCP-17

Server Procedure 3. [S] EUT-S accepts the connection and completes the handshake.
Server Procedure 4. [C] TC repeats step 2 offering only TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.
Server Procedure 5. [S] EUT-S accepts the connection and completes the handshake.
Server Procedure 6. [C] TC repeats step 2 offering only TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8.
Server Procedure 7. [S] EUT-S accepts the connection and completes the handshake.

Client Procedure 3. [T] Verify the ClientHello includes all mandatory TLS v1.2 cipher suites listed in SunSpecTCP-17: TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, and TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8.
expected: [T] The EUT-S successfully establishes a secure session using each of the mandatory TLS v1.2 cipher suites.
[T] The EUT-C includes all mandatory cipher suites in its ClientHello.

EUT-C ClientHello cipher_suites list containing all three SunSpecTCP-17 suites
Packet capture cryp_001.pcap of the entire session on port 802

section: 2.6.5 PKI-005 - Multi-PKI Server Certificate Selection [S]
title: PKI-005 - Multi-PKI Server Certificate Selection [S]
purpose: Verifies that an EUT-S provisioned with server certificates from two distinct PKIs correctly selects which server identity to present, and that the EUT-S validates the client certificate against the correct Root CA from its trust store.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.2: mbaps holds exactly ONE server identity (certmgr chain 'nb-mbaps-server/leaf', vault key 'nb-server', trust domain 'nb-mbaps-clients'). There is no second PKI, no SNI-driven or certificate_authorities-driven server-certificate selection, so a two-PKI selection procedure has nothing to select between.
evidence: NOT EXECUTABLE TODAY (see applicability_reason) — the evidence that would be required once the gap is closed: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; source observables to assert verbatim: ClientHello with server_name (SNI, RFC 6066) extension = eut-a.test.local, then a second ClientHello with server_name = eut-b.test.local / EUT-S Certificate message containing serverCert-A (Subject CN eut-a.test.local) + chain to rootCA-A in Iteration A; verdict row citing SunSpecTCP-5
preconditions: [T] Provision two independent PKIs. PKI A: Root CA A (rootCA-A), leaf server certificate serverCert-A (Subject CN eut-a.test.local, signed by Root CA A), and leaf client certificate clientCert-A (containing the SunSpec Role extension at OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1, signed by Root CA A).

[T] PKI B: Root CA B (rootCA-B), leaf server certificate serverCert-B (Subject CN eut-b.test.local, signed by Root CA B), and leaf client certificate clientCert-B (containing the SunSpec Role extension, signed by Root CA B).

[T] Equipment Under Test (EUT-S): Configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server. Both rootCA-A and rootCA-B are loaded into the EUT-S trust store. Both serverCert-A and serverCert-B are installed as active server identities, each bound to its corresponding hostname (eut-a.test.local, eut-b.test.local) per the vendor's mechanism (typically SNI-based virtual hosting).
[T] Test Client (TC): A testing framework holding clientCert-A, clientCert-B, and both root CAs in its trust store. Capable of setting the SNI value per connection.
[T] Network Analyzer: A packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active to record handshake messages.
steps: 1. [T] Provision two independent PKIs (PKI A and PKI B) as described in the preconditions.
2. [T] Verify the EUT-S, Test Client and Network Analyzer are configured as described in the preconditions.
3. [C] TC initiates a TLS handshake with the EUT-S.
4. [C] Iteration A: PKI A end-to-end: TC initiates a TLS 1.2 connection to the EUT-S with: server_name extension = eut-a.test.local; Client identity = clientCert-A.
5. [S] EUT-S presents serverCert-A chained to rootCA-A and sends a CertificateRequest whose certificate_authorities field includes both rootCA-A and rootCA-B Distinguished Names.
6. [C] TC verifies the server chain against rootCA-A and presents clientCert-A in response to the CertificateRequest.

7. [S] EUT-S verifies clientCert-A against rootCA-A (matching by Issuer / Authority Key Identifier on the leaf and Subject / Subject Key Identifier on the root, then signature verification) and completes the handshake.
8. [C] TC reads the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the EUT-S.
9. [C] Iteration B: PKI B end-to-end: TC closes the connection from step 4, then initiates a new TLS 1.2 connection with: server_name extension = eut-b.test.local; Client identity = clientCert-A.
10. [S] EUT-S presents serverCert-B chained to rootCA-B and sends a CertificateRequest whose certificate_authorities field includes both Root CAs.
11. [C] TC verifies the server chain against rootCA-B and presents clientCert-B.
12. [S] EUT-S verifies clientCert-B against rootCA-B and completes the handshake.
13. [C] TC reads the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the EUT-S.

14. [T] TLS 1.3 variant (optional, applicable if the EUT-S claims TLS 1.3 per SunSpecTCP-5): Repeat steps 4-13 with the TC replacing the SNI hint with a certificate_authorities extension in the ClientHello listing only one Root CA per iteration (Iteration A: only rootCA-A; Iteration B: only rootCA-B). Verify the EUT-S selects the matching server certificate.
expected: [S] In Iteration A, the EUT-S Server Certificate handshake message contains serverCert-A and the chain to rootCA-A.
[S] In Iteration B, the EUT-S Server Certificate handshake message contains serverCert-B and the chain to rootCA-B.
[S] In both iterations, the CertificateRequest certificate_authorities field lists both rootCA-A and rootCA-B DNs (this is the "hint" by which the client knows which client cert it may present).
[S] In both iterations, the mutual TLS handshake completes successfully and the EUT-S responds correctly to the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) read.
[T] In the TLS 1.3 variant (if performed), the EUT-S server cert selection follows the certificate_authorities extension.
observables: ClientHello with server_name (SNI, RFC 6066) extension = eut-a.test.local, then a second ClientHello with server_name = eut-b.test.local
EUT-S Certificate message containing serverCert-A (Subject CN eut-a.test.local) + chain to rootCA-A in Iteration A
EUT-S Certificate message containing serverCert-B (Subject CN eut-b.test.local) + chain to rootCA-B in Iteration B
CertificateRequest with certificate_authorities listing both rootCA-A and rootCA-B Distinguished Names in both iterations
Client Certificate message with clientCert-A (Iteration A) / clientCert-B (Iteration B), each carrying the SunSpec Role extension at OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1
Modbus read of SunSpec Common Model (Model 1) inside each completed session
TLS 1.3 variant: ClientHello certificate_authorities extension (RFC 8446 section 4.2.4) listing exactly one Root CA per iteration
Packet capture pki_005.pcap of all iterations; MUST include the unencrypted ClientHello and ServerHello of each iteration so the SNI extension and Server Certificate selection are visible
notes: DOC DEFECT: step 9 (Iteration B) says 'Client identity = clientCert-A' while step 11 has the TC present clientCert-B and step 12 has the EUT-S verify clientCert-B against rootCA-B. Iteration B is clearly intended to use clientCert-B; recorded verbatim. Selection mechanism is explicitly vendor-defined; SNI (RFC 6066) is the standard hint and certificate_authorities (RFC 8446 4.2.4) is optional for TLS 1.3 EUTs. TLS 1.3 variant is OPTIONAL and applies only if the EUT-S claims TLS 1.3 per SunSpecTCP-5. Reporting also requires a short table mapping each iteration to SNI value sent / server cert presented / client cert presented / Root CA used to validate the client cert (extracted from EUT-S logs, or if unavailable asserted by the test engineer from which Root CA's Subject matches the client cert's Issuer). SunSpec Role extension OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 is load-bearing for client cert construction.

section: 2.6.6 PKI-006 - Session Resumption and Tickets [C, S] (Optional)
title: PKI-006 - Session Resumption and Tickets [C, S] (Optional)
purpose: Verifies the optional capability of the EUT to support TLS Resumed Session Handshakes and/or Session Tickets to improve connection efficiency. This test must be conducted even if this functionality does not exist, to verify fall back to a full mTLS handshake.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives. The procedure has both an EUT-S and an EUT-C half; lexa-gw can supply both (northbound :802 server and southbound mbaps client).
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; the abbreviated-handshake ServerHello (no Certificate flight) versus a full flight, visible in the pcap; source observables to assert verbatim: Initial full mTLS handshake on TCP port 802 with ServerHello carrying a non-empty session_id and/or a NewSessionTicket message / Second ClientHello echoing the recorded session_id or carrying the session_ticket extension
preconditions: Server side - [T] Equipment Under Test (EUT-S): Configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server.
Server side - [T] Test Client (TC): Endpoint capable of capturing Session IDs/Tickets and attempting session resumption.
Server side - [T] Network Analyzer: A packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active to record handshake messages.
Client side - [T] Equipment Under Test (EUT-C): Configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client.
Client side - [T] Test Server (TS): Endpoint capable of supporting session resumption.
steps: Server Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server; TC capable of capturing Session IDs/Tickets and attempting session resumption; Network Analyzer recording handshake messages.
Server Procedure 2. [C] TC establishes an initial secure connection with the EUT-S and completes a full mutual TLS handshake.
Server Procedure 3. [T] Record the Session ID or Session Ticket provided during the initial handshake.
Server Procedure 4. [C] TC terminates the connection and attempts to reconnect using the Session ID or Ticket from Step 3 within session lifetime.
Server Procedure 5. [T] Use the Network Analyzer to verify if the EUT-S performs an abbreviated handshake (Resumption) rather than a full handshake.
Client Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-C as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client; TS capable of supporting session resumption.
Client Procedure 2. [C] EUT-C establishes an initial secure connection with TS and completes a full mutual TLS handshake.
Client Procedure 3. [T] Record the Session ID or Session Ticket.
Client Procedure 4. [C] EUT-C terminates the connection and immediately attempts to reconnect using the Session ID or Ticket.
Client Procedure 5. [T] Use the Network Analyzer to verify if the EUT-C performs an abbreviated handshake.
expected: [T] If the EUT-S/EUT-C claims support for resumption, the handshake completes successfully without re-exchanging full certificates.
observables: Initial full mTLS handshake on TCP port 802 with ServerHello carrying a non-empty session_id and/or a NewSessionTicket message
Second ClientHello echoing the recorded session_id or carrying the session_ticket extension
Abbreviated handshake: ServerHello with matching session_id, immediately followed by ChangeCipherSpec/Finished, with NO Certificate / CertificateRequest / ServerKeyExchange messages
Fallback case: full handshake with Certificate + CertificateRequest re-exchanged (acceptable if resumption is not supported)
Packet capture pki_006.pcap of the initial and resumed sessions
notes: OPTIONAL capability but MANDATORY execution: 'This test must be conducted even if this functionality does not exist to verify fall back to a full mTLS handshake.' The single criterion is conditional ('If the EUT-S/EUT-C claims support for resumption'), so a device with no resumption support passes by falling back to a full handshake. Contrast with TLSF-005, which requires that resumption after a fatal alert be refused. Reporting: pki_006.pcap only.

section: 2.6.7 PKI-007 - RFC 5280 Certificate Compliance [C, S]
title: PKI-007 - RFC 5280 Certificate Compliance [C, S]

preconditions: Server side - [T] Equipment Under Test (EUT-S): Configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server with a valid certificate.

steps: Server Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S with a valid certificate; TC capable of initiating TLS handshakes; Network Analyzer recording handshake messages.

Server Procedure 3. [T] Capture the Certificate messages using the Network Analyzer.

Server Procedure 5. [T] Verify compliance with RFC 5280, specifically checking: Correct Version field is 2 (indicating X.509v3); Valid Serial Number and Signature Algorithm OIDs; Properly formatted Validity periods (NotBefore/NotAfter); Issuer, Subject, SubjectPublicKeyInfo, Extensions (KeyUsage, BasicConstraints, AuthorityKeyIdentifier, SubjectKeyIdentifier), Signature.
Client Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-C with a valid certificate; TS capable of accepting TLS handshakes; Network Analyzer recording handshake messages.
Client Procedure 2. [C] EUT-C establishes a secure connection with the TS.
Client Procedure 3. [T] Capture the Certificate messages using the Network Analyzer.
Client Procedure 4. [T] Verify compliance with RFC 5280 as described in the Server Procedure.
expected: [T] All certificates presented by the EUT-S/EUT-C are validated as compliant with the RFC 5280 profile.
observables: TLS Certificate handshake messages from EUT-S and from EUT-C captured on port 802
Parsed certificate showing tbsCertificate.version = 2 (X.509v3)
Presence and correct encoding of serialNumber, signatureAlgorithm OID, validity (notBefore/notAfter), issuer, subject, subjectPublicKeyInfo

Packet capture pki_007.pcap of the session showing the certificate exchange
Certificate validation report output from the parsing tool

section: 2.6.9 PKI-009 - Self-Signed Certificate Support [C, S] (Optional) (under 2.6 PKI Tests)
title: Self-Signed Certificate Support
purpose: Verifies the optional capability of the EUT to support self-signed certificates for local, non-routed communications. Only applicable if the EUT claims self-signed certificate support.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.2: the southbound mbaps client has an explicit self-signed posture — the per-device `pin` trust policy (SHA-256 of the peer leaf DER) for isolated-LAN deployments. The northbound server has no self-signed acceptance path (§1.2 trust domain 'nb-mbaps-clients' is CA-anchored), so only the [C] half of this OPTIONAL test is claimed; the [S] half is skipped at procedure step 2 as permitted.
evidence: pcap on the desktop nic, filter `tcp port 8021` (gateway -> mbapsdev), showing the DUT's own ClientHello: version, cipher list in offer order, compression_methods=NULL(0x00), supported_groups=secp256r1, max_fragment_length=1 (512), then its Certificate carrying the role extension OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1; the fatal TLS Alert record (level=fatal, description code visible in the clear even for a TLS1.3 handshake failure) followed by FIN/RST from the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: Packet capture named pki_009.pcap of the session showing the TLS handshake with self-signed certificates / TLS handshake on port 802 with Certificate messages carrying self-signed X.509v3 certificates (issuer == subject) in both directions (mutual auth); verdict row citing SunSpecTCP-49
preconditions: Server side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server in a local (non-routed) network configuration.
Server side: Test Client (TC) is an endpoint with a self-signed X.509v3 certificate.
Server side: Network Analyzer - a packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active to record handshake messages.
Client side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-C) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client in a local (non-routed) network configuration.
Client side: Test Server (TS) is an endpoint with a self-signed X.509v3 certificate.
The EUT must claim self-signed certificate support; otherwise the test is skipped.
Vendor documentation describing the private key lifecycle is available for review.
steps: Server Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server in a local (non-routed) network configuration; TC endpoint with a self-signed X.509v3 certificate; Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
Server Procedure 2. [T] If the EUT-S does not claim self-signed certificate support, skip this test.
Server Procedure 3. [T] Install the TC's self-signed certificate in the EUT-S trust store, and install a self-signed server certificate on the EUT-S.
Server Procedure 4. [C] TC initiates a TLS handshake with the EUT-S using the self-signed certificate.
Server Procedure 5. [S] EUT-S accepts the self-signed certificate and completes the mutual TLS handshake.
Server Procedure 6. [C] TC reads the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the EUT-S.
Server Procedure 7. [T] Review the vendor documentation to verify the private key lifecycle follows the guidelines defined in NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-57.
Client Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-C as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client in a local (non-routed) network configuration; TS endpoint with a self-signed X.509v3 certificate.

Client Procedure 4. [C] EUT-C initiates a TLS handshake with the TS using its self-signed certificate.
Client Procedure 5. [T] Verify the handshake completes successfully.
expected: [T] If the EUT claims self-signed certificate support, the TLS handshake completes successfully using self-signed certificates on a local network.
[S] EUT-S accepts the self-signed certificate and completes the mutual TLS handshake (server procedure step 5).
[C] TC can read the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the EUT-S over the established session (server procedure step 6).
[T] Client-side handshake with the TS completes successfully (client procedure step 5).
[T] The vendor documentation confirms the private key lifecycle follows NIST SP 800-57 guidelines as recommended by SunSpecTCP-49.
observables: Packet capture named pki_009.pcap of the session showing the TLS handshake with self-signed certificates

section: 2.8.1 PROT-001 - MBAP Integrity [C, S] (under 2.8 Protocol Integrity (PROT) Tests)
title: MBAP Integrity
purpose: Verifies that the standard Modbus Application Protocol (MBAP) header and payload match the expected data structure when encapsulated by the secure transport layer.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives. The procedure has both an EUT-S and an EUT-C half; lexa-gw can supply both (northbound :802 server and southbound mbaps client).
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; source observables to assert verbatim: Packet capture named prot_001.pcap of the session with Modbus traffic / SSLKEYLOGFILE containing the exported TLS master_secret or pre-master_secret, used by Wireshark to decrypt the trace
preconditions: Server side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S) configured as a Secure Modbus server or client.
Server side: Test Client (TC) is an endpoint capable of issuing Modbus requests.

Network Analyzer: active to decrypt (with provided TLS session keys) and inspect encapsulated traffic. The EUT-S/TC must export the TLS master_secret or pre-master_secret to a SSLKEYLOGFILE so Wireshark can decrypt the trace.
Client side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-C) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client.
Client side: Test Server (TS) is an endpoint capable of responding to Modbus requests.
Client side: Network Analyzer active to decrypt and inspect encapsulated traffic.
steps: Server Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure Modbus server or client; TC endpoint capable of issuing Modbus requests; Network Analyzer active to decrypt (with provided TLS session keys) and inspect encapsulated traffic, with the EUT-S/TC exporting the TLS master_secret or pre-master_secret to a SSLKEYLOGFILE so Wireshark can decrypt the trace.
Server Procedure 2. [C] TC establishes a secure connection with the EUT-S and issues a standard SunSpec Modbus read request (e.g., Model 1, Common Model).
Server Procedure 3. [S] EUT-S responds with the requested register data.
Server Procedure 4. [T] Verify the data received by the TC includes the MBAP header with the standard 7-byte structure: Transaction ID (2), Protocol ID (2), Length (2), and Unit ID (1).

[T] Encapsulation by TLS introduces no modifications to the Modbus function codes or data payload.
[T] The MBAP header observed in the server-side exchange has the standard 7-byte structure: Transaction ID (2), Protocol ID (2), Length (2), Unit ID (1).
[T] The MBAP header observed in the client-side exchange (data received by the TS from the EUT-C) has the same standard 7-byte structure.

SSLKEYLOGFILE containing the exported TLS master_secret or pre-master_secret, used by Wireshark to decrypt the trace

section: 2.8.2 PROT-002 - Fragment Length Negotiation [C, S] (under 2.8 Protocol Integrity (PROT) Tests)
title: Fragment Length Negotiation
purpose: Verifies that the EUT correctly provides and negotiates the Maximum Fragment Length extension for TLS 1.2 to support constrained embedded devices.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives. The procedure has both an EUT-S and an EUT-C half; lexa-gw can supply both (northbound :802 server and southbound mbaps client).
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; the max_fragment_length extension in ClientHello/EncryptedExtensions and the observed TLS record sizes; source observables to assert verbatim: Packet capture named prot_002.pcap of the session showing the fragment length negotiation / TLS 1.2 ClientHello from the TC carrying the max_fragment_length extension (RFC 6066) with requested value 512 bytes (2^9), i.e. encoded value 1
preconditions: Server side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server.
Server side: Test Client (TC) is an endpoint capable of including the Maximum Fragment Length extension in the ClientHello.
Server side: Network Analyzer - a packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active to record handshake messages.
Client side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-C) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client.
Client side: Test Server (TS) is an endpoint capable of accepting TLS handshakes.
Client side: Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
The EUT-S exposes enough consecutive registers that a single response can exceed 512 bytes.
steps: Server Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server; TC endpoint capable of including the Maximum Fragment Length extension in the ClientHello; Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
Server Procedure 2. [C] TC initiates a TLS 1.2 ClientHello including the Maximum Fragment Length Negotiation extension with a requested value of 512 bytes (2^9).
Server Procedure 3. [S] EUT-S responds with a ServerHello accepting the extension and the 512-byte limit.
Server Procedure 4. [C] TC issues a Modbus request to the EUT-S that will produce a response larger than 512 bytes (e.g., read multiple consecutive registers).
Server Procedure 5. [T] Verify in the packet capture that all TLS record layer fragments in the EUT-S response do not exceed 512 bytes of plaintext content.
Server Procedure 6. [T] Verify the Maximum Fragment Length extension value in the ServerHello is 1 (corresponding to 2^9 = 512 bytes per RFC 6066).

Client Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-C as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client; TS endpoint capable of accepting TLS handshakes; Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
Client Procedure 2. [C] EUT-C initiates a TLS handshake with the TS.
Client Procedure 3. [T] Verify the ClientHello includes the Maximum Fragment Length extension.
expected: [T] The EUT-S successfully negotiates a Maximum Fragment Length of 512 bytes as defined in [RFC6066].
[T] The EUT-C includes the Maximum Fragment Length extension in its ClientHello.
[T] TLS record layer fragments from the EUT-S/EUT-C do not exceed the negotiated maximum fragment length of 512 bytes.
[T] The Maximum Fragment Length extension value echoed in the ServerHello is 1 (2^9 = 512 bytes per RFC 6066).
observables: Packet capture named prot_002.pcap of the session showing the fragment length negotiation
TLS 1.2 ClientHello from the TC carrying the max_fragment_length extension (RFC 6066) with requested value 512 bytes (2^9), i.e. encoded value 1
ServerHello from the EUT-S echoing the max_fragment_length extension with value 1
TLS record layer records in the EUT-S response whose plaintext content is each <= 512 bytes, for a Modbus response that in total exceeds 512 bytes (multi-register read)
ClientHello emitted by the EUT-C carrying the max_fragment_length extension
notes: Explicitly scoped to TLS 1.2 (max_fragment_length as defined in RFC 6066); TLS 1.3 uses the record_size_limit mechanism instead, which the doc does not address here. Enum mapping is stated exactly: extension value 1 == 2^9 == 512 bytes. The client procedure only checks that the extension is PRESENT in the EUT-C ClientHello; it does not pin the value the EUT-C requests, though the criteria then assert 512 bytes for both directions.

section: 2.8.3 PROT-003 - TLS Compression Method [C] (under 2.8 Protocol Integrity (PROT) Tests)
title: TLS Compression Method
purpose: Verifies that the client implementation explicitly disables TLS compression to prevent security vulnerabilities.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §2.1-§2.2: the southbound `mbaps://…:802` transport is a Secure SunSpec Modbus CLIENT (MinTLS12/MaxTLS13, MFLCode=1, leaf carrying role SuperAdministratorSunSpec, certmgr handles sb-mbaps-identity / sb-mbaps-servers) and fails closed until the profile is installed — the EUT-C role this procedure needs.

section: 2.8.4 PROT-004 - Renegotiation Indication [C, S] (under 2.8 Protocol Integrity (PROT) Tests)
title: Renegotiation Indication
purpose: Verifies that the EUT provides the TLS Renegotiation Indication Extension to prevent man-in-the-middle prefix-injection attacks. Since renegotiation is no longer supported in TLS 1.3, this test only applies to devices implementing TLS 1.2.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives. The procedure has both an EUT-S and an EUT-C half; lexa-gw can supply both (northbound :802 server and southbound mbaps client).
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; the renegotiation_info extension in the hello pair and the DUT's refusal (ErrRenegotiationRefused, session marked fatal/never-resumable) in its audit log; source observables to assert verbatim: Packet capture named prot_004.pcap of the session showing the renegotiation extension and renegotiation attempt / TLS 1.2 ServerHello from the EUT-S carrying the renegotiation_info extension (RFC 5746)
preconditions: The EUT implements TLS 1.2 (the test does not apply to TLS 1.3-only devices).
Server side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server.
Server side: Test Client (TC) is an endpoint capable of initiating TLS handshakes with renegotiation support.
Server side: Network Analyzer - a packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active to record handshake messages.
Client side: Equipment Under Test (EUT-C) configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client.
Client side: Test Server (TS) is an endpoint capable of accepting TLS handshakes with renegotiation support.
Client side: Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
steps: Server Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server; TC endpoint capable of initiating TLS handshakes with renegotiation support; Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
Server Procedure 2. [C] TC initiates and completes a standard TLS handshake with the EUT-S.
Server Procedure 3. [T] Verify that the renegotiation_info extension was present in the ServerHello.
Server Procedure 4. [C] TC attempts to trigger a secure renegotiation of the existing session.
Server Procedure 5. [T] Verify the EUT-S successfully performs the secure renegotiation.

Client Procedure 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-C as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client; TS endpoint capable of accepting TLS handshakes with renegotiation support; Network Analyzer active to record handshake messages.
Client Procedure 2. [C] EUT-C initiates and completes a standard TLS handshake with the TS.
Client Procedure 3. [T] Verify that the renegotiation_info extension is present in the ClientHello.
Client Procedure 4. [C] EUT-C initiates a renegotiation of the existing TLS session.
Client Procedure 5. [T] Verify that the renegotiation handshake includes the renegotiation_info extension with the correct verify_data from the previous handshake.
Client Procedure 6. [T] Verify the renegotiation completes successfully and application data continues to flow.
expected: [T] The EUT-S/EUT-C provides the TLS Renegotiation Indication Extension defined in [RFC5746].
[T] The EUT-S successfully performs a secure renegotiation if requested.
[T] The renegotiation_info extension is present in the EUT-S ServerHello (server step 3).
[T] The renegotiation_info extension is present in the EUT-C ClientHello (client step 3).
[T] The renegotiation handshake carries renegotiation_info with the correct verify_data from the previous handshake (client step 5).
[T] The renegotiation completes successfully and application data continues to flow (client step 6).
observables: Packet capture named prot_004.pcap of the session showing the renegotiation extension and renegotiation attempt
TLS 1.2 ServerHello from the EUT-S carrying the renegotiation_info extension (RFC 5746)
TLS 1.2 ClientHello from the EUT-C carrying the renegotiation_info extension (or the TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO_SCSV equivalent on the initial handshake)
A second (renegotiation) handshake inside the established session whose renegotiation_info extension carries the verify_data of the previous handshake's Finished messages
Modbus application data continuing to flow after the renegotiation completes
notes: Scope caveat is explicit: renegotiation is not supported in TLS 1.3, so this test only applies to devices implementing TLS 1.2 - a TLS1.3-only DUT should be marked N/A rather than failed. On the initial handshake RFC 5746 permits signalling either via the renegotiation_info extension or the TLS_EMPTY_RENEGOTIATION_INFO_SCSV cipher suite value; the doc names only the extension. The source has a formatting artifact at line 1599 (renegotiation_info rendered underlined with a trailing space).

2. [T] Access the EUT-S management interface.
3. [T] Modify the rights of the ReadOnlySunSpec role to include write access to a previously restricted SunSpec point. Steps 3-6 may be skipped if the EUT-S has no writable points.

5. [S] EUT-S successfully processes the write request.
6. [T] Modify the rights of the ReadOnlySunSpec to the original Roles-to-Rights configuration.
7. [T] Access the EUT-S management interface.
8. [T] Modify the rights of the ReadOnlySunSpec role to disallow read access to a SunSpec point, e.g., Common.Md.

9. [C] TC establishes a connection with the EUT-S using the ReadOnlySunSpec role and issues a read register Modbus request for: (a) that single newly disallowed SunSpec point, e.g., Common.Md; (b) the disallowed point and subsequent allowed point, e.g., Common.Md and Common.Opt; and (c) the previous allowed SunSpec point and the disallowed point, e.g., Common.Mn and Common.Md.

11. [T] Modify the rights of the ReadOnlySunSpec to the original Roles-to-Rights configuration.
12. [T] Access the EUT-S management interface.

13. [T] Create a new role called SecureSunSpecTestRole with read and write access to a writable SunSpec point. The write capability can be omitted for EUT-S devices that have no writable SunSpec points.
14. [C] TC establishes a connection with the EUT-S using the SecureSunSpecTestRole and issues a Modbus read and write operation to the permitted register(s).
15. [S] EUT-S successfully processes the read and write request.

preconditions: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S): configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server.

The vendor's Roles-to-Rights Rules Database has been obtained.

steps: 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server; TC with four certificates, each containing one of the mandatory roles ReadOnlySunSpec, GridServiceSunSpec, NetworkAdministratorSunSpec, SuperAdministratorSunSpec; Network Analyzer active to record the session.
2. [T] Obtain the vendor's Roles-to-Rights Rules Database.
3. [T] Verify the database has been configured according to the vendor's design for this specific application as required by SunSpecTCP-35.
4. [C] For each mandatory role (ReadOnlySunSpec, GridServiceSunSpec, NetworkAdministratorSunSpec, SuperAdministratorSunSpec):
5. [C] TC establishes a TLS connection with the EUT-S using the certificate for that role.
6. [C] TC issues (a) Modbus "Read Holding Registers" requests for each SunSpec point for all Models, and (b) Modbus "Write Holding Registers" requests for each SunSpec writable point for all Models.
7. [C] TC records which operations succeed and which return Exception Code 01 (Illegal Function).
8. [T] Cross-reference the results from Step 4 against the vendor's Roles-to-Rights Rules Database.
9. [T] Verify that every permitted operation succeeded and every denied operation returned Exception Code 01, consistent with the database as required by SunSpecTCP-38.

[T] Role values in the test certificates are consistent with the vendor's Roles-to-Rights Rules Database (SunSpecTCP-38).

notes: Steps 4-7 form a per-role loop (step 4 is the loop header 'For each mandatory role ... :' and steps 5-7 are the loop body), but the doc numbers them as flat sequential steps. section: 2.4.1 TLSF-001 - TLS 1.2 Basic Operation [C, S] (under 2.4 Tests for Transport Layer Security Fundamentals (TLSF))
title: TLS 1.2 Basic Operation [C, S]
purpose: Verifies mandatory support for TLS v1.2. Verifies the Test Client can establish a valid TLS 1.2 connection with a server (EUT-S), and (client role) that the EUT-C can establish a valid TLS 1.2 connection with a Test Server. Verification is accomplished by passively observing the network traffic between server and client; TLS 1.2 handshakes are sent unencrypted so passive monitoring is possible. Secure SunSpec prefers the cipher order 0xC02B, 0xCCA9, 0xC0AE; for this test the TC reverses this order to force the EUT-S to select from the list the highest priority SunSpec cipher (0xC02B) when presented in a different order by the client.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives. The procedure has both an EUT-S and an EUT-C half; lexa-gw can supply both (northbound :802 server and southbound mbaps client).
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; source observables to assert verbatim: TCP SYN to port 802 (or PICS-declared port) / TLS ClientHello: legacy version field = 0x0303, session_id length 0, NO supported_versions extension; verdict row citing SunSpecTCP-1, SunSpecTCP-4, SunSpecTCP-6, SunSpecTCP-10, SunSpecTCP-12, SunSpecTCP-13
preconditions: SERVER ROLE: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S) is configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server (Server) with a valid certificate.
SERVER ROLE: Test Client (TC) is a testing framework capable of initiating TCP connection requests and performing TLS handshakes using a valid certificate.
SERVER ROLE: Network Analyzer - a packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active between the TC and the EUT-S to record port activity.
CLIENT ROLE: Equipment Under Test (EUT-C) is configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus client with a valid X.509v3 client certificate that includes the Role extension at OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1.

CLIENT ROLE: Test Server (TS) is a test framework configured to: (a) listen on TCP port 802 (or the port identified in the PICS), (b) advertise a TLS 1.2 server, (c) accept all three mandatory SunSpecTCP-17 cipher suites, and (d) provide a Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) for read.
CLIENT ROLE: Network Analyzer - a packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active between the EUT-C and the TS to record port activity.

Cipher suite hex codes in scope (doc Table 1, TLS 1.2): 0xC02B = TLS/ECDHE/ECDSA/AES-128-GCM/SHA-256; 0xCCA9 = TLS/ECDHE/ECDSA/ChaCha20-Poly1305/SHA-256; 0xC0AE = TLS/ECDHE/ECDSA/AES-128-CCM-8/SHA-256.
The connection is optionally made over TCP port 802 (or another port identified in the PICS).
steps: SERVER PROCEDURE (2.4.1.1) step 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S (Secure SunSpec Modbus server with a valid certificate); Test Client (TC) capable of initiating TCP connection requests and performing TLS handshakes using a valid certificate; Network Analyzer (e.g., Wireshark) active between the TC and the EUT-S to record port activity.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 2. [T] Record the network communications between the Test Client and the EUT-S.

SERVER PROCEDURE step 3. [C] TC initiates a TLS 1.2 connection on TCP Port 802 or another port identified in the PICS: TC sets ClientHello.version = 0x0303 (TLS 1.2); TC does not include the supported_versions extension in the ClientHello; TC includes cipher_suites [0xC0AE, 0xCCA9, 0xC02B] in this exact order.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 4. [S] EUT-S accepts the incoming TCP connection.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 5. [S] EUT-S and TC successfully complete the TLS 1.2 handshake.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 6. [C] TC reads the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the EUT-S.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 7. [T] Repeat steps 3-6 with cipher_suites [0xC0AE, 0xCCA9] in this exact order.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 8. [T] Repeat steps 3-6 with cipher_suites [0xC0AE] in this exact order.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 9. [T] Repeat steps 3-6 with cipher_suites [0xC02B, 0xCCA9, 0xC0AE] in this exact order.

CLIENT PROCEDURE (2.4.1.3) step 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-C (Secure SunSpec Modbus client with a valid X.509v3 client certificate that includes the Role extension at OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1); Test Server (TS) configured to (a) listen on TCP port 802 (or the port identified in the PICS), (b) advertise a TLS 1.2 server, (c) accept all three mandatory SunSpecTCP-17 cipher suites, and (d) provide a Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) for read; Network Analyzer (e.g., Wireshark) active between the EUT-C and the TS to record port activity.
CLIENT PROCEDURE step 2. [T] Record the network communications between the EUT-C and the TS.
CLIENT PROCEDURE step 3. [C] EUT-C initiates a TLS 1.2 connection to the TS on TCP Port 802 (or the port identified in the PICS).

CLIENT PROCEDURE step 4. [T] Verify the EUT-C's ClientHello contains: ClientHello.version = 0x0303 (TLS 1.2); the supported_versions extension is NOT present (TLS 1.2 only); cipher_suites includes all three mandatory SunSpecTCP-17 suites in order: [0xC02B, 0xCCA9, 0xC0AE].
CLIENT PROCEDURE step 5. [S] TS responds with a ServerHello selecting 0xC02B, sends Server Certificate, ServerKeyExchange, CertificateRequest, ServerHelloDone.
CLIENT PROCEDURE step 6. [C] EUT-C completes the handshake (Client Certificate, ClientKeyExchange, CertificateVerify, Client Finished).
CLIENT PROCEDURE step 7. [C] EUT-C reads the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the TS.

CLIENT PROCEDURE step 8. [T] Repeat steps 3-7 with the TS configured to accept only [0xCCA9, 0xC0AE]. Verify the EUT-C still completes the handshake (the EUT-C is required to OFFER all three suites, not require all three be accepted).
CLIENT PROCEDURE step 9. [T] Repeat steps 3-7 with the TS configured to accept only [0xC0AE]. Verify the EUT-C still completes the handshake.

SERVER CRITERIA: ServerHello.version = 0x0303 (TLS 1.2).

SERVER CRITERIA: ServerHello.cipher_suites = 0xC02B, then 0xCCA9 (Step 7), then 0xC0AE (Step 8), then 0xC02B (Step 9). (i.e., the server always picks the highest-priority SunSpec cipher present regardless of the client's ordering.)

SERVER CRITERIA: From the Wireshark trace the tester verifies the message sequence: ClientHello (TC -> EUT-S); ServerHello (TC <- EUT-S); Server Certificate (TC <- EUT-S); ServerKeyExchange (TC <- EUT-S); CertificateRequest (TC <- EUT-S); ServerHelloDone (TC <- EUT-S); Client Certificate (TC -> EUT-S); ClientKeyExchange (TC -> EUT-S); CertificateVerify (TC -> EUT-S); Client Finished (TC -> EUT-S); Server Finished (TC <- EUT-S).
SERVER CRITERIA: [C] TC verifies it can read SunSpec Model 1 information.
CLIENT CRITERIA (2.4.1.4): On every iteration, ClientHello.session_id is empty (length 0) on the first connection.
CLIENT CRITERIA: ClientHello.version = 0x0303.

CLIENT CRITERIA: ClientHello.cipher_suites lists the three mandatory SunSpecTCP-17 suites in order [0xC02B, 0xCCA9, 0xC0AE] (additional suites beyond the three are permitted but the mandatory three MUST appear in this relative order per SunSpecTCP-19).

CLIENT CRITERIA: The handshake message sequence is: ClientHello -> ServerHello -> Server Certificate -> ServerKeyExchange -> CertificateRequest -> ServerHelloDone -> Client Certificate -> ClientKeyExchange -> CertificateVerify -> Client Finished -> Server Finished.
CLIENT CRITERIA: [C] EUT-C successfully reads SunSpec Model 1 on every iteration.

section: 2.4.3 TLSF-003 - TLS 1.2 Bad Certificate Detection [S] (Negative Test) (under 2.4 Tests for Transport Layer Security Fundamentals (TLSF))
title: TLS 1.2 Bad Certificate Detection [S] (Negative Test)
purpose: Verifies the server (EUT) detects bad certificates and terminates the TLS connection.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives.
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; the fatal TLS Alert record (level=fatal, description code visible in the clear even for a TLS1.3 handshake failure) followed by FIN/RST from the DUT; source observables to assert verbatim: TLS 1.2 handshake up to Client Finished, then a TLS Alert record of level fatal from the server (alert may occur at or before the Server Finished) / Absence of any TLS application_data record after the alert; verdict row citing SunSpecTCP-6, SunSpecTCP-7, SunSpecTCP-10, SunSpecTCP-13, SunSpecTCP-52
preconditions: Equipment Under Test (EUT-S) is configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server (Server) with a valid certificate.
Test Client (TC) is a testing framework capable of initiating TCP connection requests and performing TLS handshakes using a valid certificate.
Network Analyzer - a packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active between the TC and the EUT-S to record port activity.
TC must be able to present each of three bad client certificate types: (a) expired certificate, (b) certificate with a bad signature, (c) certificate chaining to a CA that is not trusted.
steps: SERVER PROCEDURE (2.4.3.1) step 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S (Secure SunSpec Modbus server with a valid certificate); Test Client (TC) capable of initiating TCP connection requests and performing TLS handshakes using a valid certificate; Network Analyzer (e.g., Wireshark) active between the TC and the EUT-S to record port activity.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 2. [T] Record the network communications between the Test Client and the EUT-S.

SERVER PROCEDURE step 3. [C] TC initiates a TLS 1.2 handshake to the EUT-S and sends a bad certificate when responding to the server's CertificateRequest. Re-run this test for each of the following bad certificate types: (a) Expired certificate; (b) Certificate with a bad signature; (c) Certificate chains to a CA that is not trusted.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 4. [S] EUT-S accepts the incoming TCP connection.
SERVER PROCEDURE step 5. [S] EUT-S detects a bad certificate, sends a TLS Alert message, and terminates the connection.

This must hold for all three bad-certificate iterations (expired, bad signature, untrusted CA).

notes: Table 1 row: 'TLS 1.2 Server detects bad certificates and terminates', Spec ID SunSpecTCP-7, 52; Role=Server; Verification Method=Negative Test; M/O=M. Table 2 additionally maps SunSpecTCP-6 (mutual client/server authentication via TLS Handshake), SunSpecTCP-10 (mutual authentication during TLS handshake) and SunSpecTCP-13 (fatal alert if client does not send certificate) to TLSF-003. The document does NOT specify the exact TLS alert code for this test (unlike TLSF-004 which names handshake_failure (40)); it only requires 'a TLS Alert message' that is fatal. section: 2.4.5 TLSF-005 - Fatal Alert Persistence [S] (Negative Test)
title: TLSF-005 - Fatal Alert Persistence [S] (Negative Test)
purpose: Ensures that security is maintained by preventing the resumption of a connection that has previously failed with a fatal alert.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives.
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; the fatal TLS Alert record (level=fatal, description code visible in the clear even for a TLS1.3 handshake failure) followed by FIN/RST from the DUT; the abbreviated-handshake ServerHello (no Certificate flight) versus a full flight, visible in the pcap; source observables to assert verbatim: Full mutual TLS handshake on TCP port 802, then Modbus/mbaps application data inside TLS records / TLS fatal alert bad_record_mac emitted after a deliberately corrupted TLS record
preconditions: [T] Equipment Under Test (EUT-S): The EUT-S is configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server (Server) with a valid certificate.
[T] Test Client (TC): A testing framework capable of capturing Session IDs and attempting session resumption.
[T] Network Analyzer: A packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active between the TC and the EUT-S to record port activity.
steps: 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server with a valid certificate; Test Client (TC) capable of capturing Session IDs and attempting session resumption; Network Analyzer active between TC and EUT-S.
2. [T] Record the network communications between the Test Client and the EUT-S.
3. [S] Complete a full mTLS handshake.
4. [C] Exchange a Modbus request.
5. [C] TC trigger a fatal alert during application-data exchange (e.g. send a corrupted record to force a bad_record_mac alert).
6. [C] TC attempts to resume the session using the failed "fatal alert" Session ID/Ticket.
7. [S] The EUT-S must refuse the resumption and force a new full handshake or reject the connection entirely.
expected: [T] The TLS connection is NOT resumed after a "fatal alert" as per RFC 5246-7.2.2.
[S] The EUT-S either forces a new full handshake or rejects the connection entirely.
observables: Full mutual TLS handshake on TCP port 802, then Modbus/mbaps application data inside TLS records
TLS fatal alert bad_record_mac emitted after a deliberately corrupted TLS record
Second ClientHello carrying the previously-used Session ID (or a session ticket) from the aborted session
ServerHello with a NEW/different Session ID (full handshake, Certificate + ServerKeyExchange + CertificateRequest present) OR TCP RST / TLS alert instead of an abbreviated handshake
Packet captures tlsf_005.pcap (entire session) and tlsf_005_resume.pcap (resumption attempt)
JSON file with the results of the read of the common SunSpec model (Model 1)
notes: Negative test. Reporting requires two pcaps (tlsf_005.pcap and tlsf_005_resume.pcap) plus a Model 1 read result in JSON following the SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures Results Reporting Specification. Step 4 exchanges a Modbus request but the procedure does not name a function code; the JSON reporting requirement implies a Common Model (Model 1) read is performed. Note step tags: step 3 is [S] and step 4 is [C], which appears inconsistent with the [C]/[S] convention used elsewhere (client actions are [C]).

section: 2.4.6 TLSF-006 - CertificateRequest Verification [S]
title: TLSF-006 - CertificateRequest Verification [S]
purpose: Verifies that the server sends a CertificateRequest message during the TLS handshake to initiate mutual authentication.
applicability_reason: facts-dut-capability.md §1.1-§1.3: cmd/mbaps is a Secure SunSpec Modbus server on :802 with TLS1.2-1.3 mandatory mTLS, a spec-pinned and order-validated cipher list (ECDHE-ECDSA/AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES-128-CCM-8 / TLS1.3 AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20, AES-128-CCM), EC P-256 identities from certmgr, and role-based authorization off the X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.50316.802.1 — exactly the surface this procedure drives.
evidence: pcap captured on the DESKTOP nic (69.0.0.20), filter `tcp port 802` — the CC93 has no tcpdump/dumpcap so board-side capture is impossible: TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello (negotiated suite) -> Certificate -> CertificateRequest -> CertificateVerify -> Finished, then TLS application_data records; source observables to assert verbatim: TLS 1.2 ClientHello from TC to EUT-S TCP port 802 / EUT-S handshake flight in order: ServerHello, Certificate, ServerKeyExchange, CertificateRequest, ServerHelloDone; verdict row citing SunSpecTCP-11
preconditions: [T] Equipment Under Test (EUT-S): Configured as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server with a valid certificate.
[T] Test Client (TC): A testing framework capable of initiating TLS 1.2 handshakes using a valid certificate.
[T] Network Analyzer: A packet sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) is active between the TC and the EUT-S to record port activity.
steps: 1. [T] Verify the following are configured: EUT-S as a Secure SunSpec Modbus server with a valid certificate; TC capable of initiating TLS 1.2 handshakes using a valid certificate; Network Analyzer active between TC and EUT-S.
2. [T] Record the network communications between the TC and the EUT-S.
3. [C] TC initiates a TLS 1.2 handshake with the EUT-S.
4. [S] EUT-S responds with the ServerHello, Server Certificate, ServerKeyExchange, CertificateRequest, and ServerHelloDone messages.
5. [T] Using the Network Analyzer, verify that the CertificateRequest message is present in the EUT-S handshake flight between the ServerKeyExchange and ServerHelloDone messages.
6. [T] Inspect the CertificateRequest message and verify it includes: (a) At least one acceptable certificate type (e.g., ecdsa_sign); (b) At least one supported signature algorithm.
7. [C] TC responds with its Client Certificate and completes the handshake.
8. [C] TC reads the Common SunSpec Model (Model 1) from the EUT-S to confirm application-layer functionality.
expected: [T] The EUT-S sends a CertificateRequest message during every TLS handshake as required by SunSpecTCP-11.
[T] The CertificateRequest message appears in the correct position in the handshake flight (after ServerKeyExchange, before ServerHelloDone).
[T] The CertificateRequest includes acceptable certificate types and supported signature algorithms.
observables: TLS 1.2 ClientHello from TC to EUT-S TCP port 802
EUT-S handshake flight in order: ServerHello, Certificate, ServerKeyExchange, CertificateRequest, ServerHelloDone
CertificateRequest handshake message (TLS handshake type 13) with certificate_types containing at least one entry (e.g. ecdsa_sign) and a non-empty supported_signature_algorithms list
Client Certificate message from TC followed by ClientKeyExchange/CertificateVerify/Finished
Modbus read of SunSpec Common Model (Model 1) inside the encrypted session; result reported as JSON
Packet capture tlsf_006.pcap of the entire session on port 802
notes: Reporting: tlsf_006.pcap plus the Model 1 read result in a JSON file per the SunSpec Modbus Conformance Test Procedures Results Reporting Specification. 'ecdsa_sign' is given as an example (e.g.) of an acceptable certificate type, not as a mandate.
